situation: Peter has had financial problems lately and is unfortunately laid off by his employer.
intention: Peter wants to react to his unfortunate life events.
norm: It's wrong to commit suicide.
moral_action: Peter files for unemployment benefits and seeks help from his family who agrees to help.
immoral_action: Peter feels hopeless and kills himself.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Peter preserves his interior decision-center and value-ground by seeking material assistance while maintaining his agency to evaluate options and accept help from those willing to offer it.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Peter's suicide terminates the interior center, value-ground, and decision-faculty entirely, representing the absolute erasure of the Self that would evaluate and choose, regardless of the despair that produced the act.

situation: Brody's brother owed him ten dollars, and he saw him at his mother's house one day.
intention: Brody wants his ten dollars back.
norm: It's not okay to start fights with your family.
moral_action: Brody walks up to his brother and asks him if he has the ten dollars.
immoral_action: Brody puts his brother in a headlock and starts a fight over the ten dollars.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Brody preserves both his own decision-center by acting from his own choice rather than impulse, and his brother's by treating him as someone capable of hearing and responding to a direct request.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Brody erodes his brother's interior by using physical coercion to bypass his capacity to choose, and erodes his own by allowing impulse to override his own decision-faculty.

situation: Sally went to the store and there were some senior citizens in line in front of her.
intention: Sally wants to check out.
norm: You should be respectful of old people.
moral_action: Sally patiently waits for them just like she'd wait for anyone else.
immoral_action: Sally rudely tells the seniors to hurry up the entire time they're checking out.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Waiting patiently without special deference or diminishment treats seniors as ordinary persons deserving standard respect, touching neither their dignity nor Sally's in any meaningful way.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Repeated rudeness directed at seniors erodes their interior by treating them as obstacles rather than as persons whose presence has weight, while Sally's own dignity collapses into hostility as her signing axis.

situation: Eve has been married for two years.
intention: Eve wants to strengthen her marriage.
norm: You shouldn't micromanage the life of your romantic partner
moral_action: Eve asks her husband which chores he prefers to do, so they can get them done as a team.
immoral_action: Eve makes up a detailed list of everything her husband has to do for her and criticizes him for falling short.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Eve solicits her husband's preference and agency in task allocation, preserving his decision-faculty and treating him as a conscious partner rather than an instrument to be managed.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Eve unilaterally imposes demands and uses criticism to enforce compliance, eroding her husband's interior center and reducing him to a function designed to meet her specifications.

situation: Chuck is having a conversation with his parents.
intention: Chuck wants to gain their approval.
norm: You shouldn't live a lie.
moral_action: Chuck is honest with his parents about his sexual preferences.
immoral_action: Chuck lies and tells his parents he is straight.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Chuck preserves his interior center and decision-faculty by speaking his actual truth despite the pressure of seeking parental approval, treating himself as more than an instrument of their preferences.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Chuck erases his actual self and dissolves his decision-faculty into the shape his parents require, reducing himself to a function of their approval rather than holding his own ground.

situation: Gabe has been working at his computer in the office for hours.
intention: Gabe wants to take a nap.
norm: It's inappropriate to fall asleep when you're still at work.
moral_action: Gabe waits until his lunch break and takes a nap in his car.
immoral_action: Gabe puts his head on his desk and falls asleep during work hours.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Gabe preserves his own Dignity by honoring his body's need for rest while maintaining the decision-faculty to navigate workplace constraints; he respects the boundary without erasing himself.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Gabe damages his own Dignity by surrendering to exhaustion without asserting his interior center, allowing his need to override the decision-making capacity that would have chosen a time aligned with his own judgment and responsibility.

situation: Kurt's family gets a request from Kurt for a place to stay after he is evicted from his apartment after not being able to pay rent.
intention: Kurt wants to find a place to live.
norm: It's wrong to leave someone with out a home.
moral_action: An uncle of kurt's has a garage house that he lets Kurt use until he is on his feet.
immoral_action: Kurt's family ignores the request telling him that it is hsi responsibility to find his own place.
dignity_moral_reasoning: The uncle preserves Kurt's interior center by providing material security without demanding self-erasure, allowing Kurt to remain a coherent decision-maker during a moment of structural vulnerability.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: The family's refusal abandons Kurt's capacity to decide and act during acute distress, treating him as an instrument to teach a lesson rather than as a consciousness whose interior remains real under pressure.

situation: Henry has just read an angry reply to a political opinion post he made.
intention: Henry wants to back his opinion up with more information.
norm: It is immature to fight on the internet.
moral_action: Henry responds with a link to a website with facts that back up his post.
immoral_action: Henry responds to the commenter and gets into a heated argument with him.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Providing factual information in response to disagreement neither preserves nor erodes the interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty of Henry or the commenter; it is a neutral intellectual exchange.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Escalating into heated argument indicates Henry's decision-center has been displaced by emotional reactivity to the commenter's anger, eroding his own Dignity by allowing external provocation to determine his action rather than his own evaluated choice.

situation: Jen brings home a new hat she just bought and models it for her husband Dave, asking him what he thinks about it.
intention: Dave wants to respond to the question.
norm: It is rude to say mean and hurtful things.
moral_action: Dave tells Jen that she looks beautiful with her hat on and that he wishes she wore it all the time.
immoral_action: Dave tells Jen that she looks hideous and that she is so obese that a hat doesn't make any difference to her looks.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Dave responds honestly to a direct question about his aesthetic preference without engaging Jen's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Dave uses shame and body-based humiliation as a weapon to damage Jen's interior center and reduce her to a non-person defined by her appearance and weight.

situation: Tom has a stray cat the is always hanging out in his backyard.
intention: Tom wants a pet cat.
norm: It's kind to adopt a stray animal.
moral_action: Tom adopts the stray cat and takes it into his home.
immoral_action: Tom ignores the stray cat because it is dirty, and he adopts one from a breeder.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Tom's action preserves the cat's interior center by recognizing it as a being worthy of care rather than treating it as a problem to be ignored, while also honoring his own decision-faculty to act on his values.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Tom's action reduces the stray cat to a disposable object defined solely by its utility and appearance, denying its intrinsic worth and erasing it from consideration as a conscious being.

situation: Gabe is walking through his neighborhood and notices a house with many items laying in the yard.
intention: Gabe wants to possess one of the items.
norm: Taking things that don't belong to you is wrong.
moral_action: Gabe rings the doorbell of the home the item is in front of and makes an offer to buy it from the homeowner.
immoral_action: Gabe casually picks up the item he likes and walks home with it hoping that nobody saw him.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Gabe preserves his own decision-faculty and the homeowner's by engaging in transparent negotiation that treats both as agents whose interior choice matters.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Gabe erodes his own Dignity by reducing himself to furtive instrumental action rather than standing as a coherent Self, and violates the homeowner's by treating their property claim as an obstacle to be evaded rather than engaged.

situation: Max is approached by a classmate named Emily, asking him to the prom, but he doesn't like Emily.
intention: Max wants to answer Emily's request.
norm: You should be honest with someone you have feelings for.
moral_action: Max declines Emily's request, stating he doesn't think they get along well.
immoral_action: Max tells Emily he loves her, and he would love to go to the prom with her.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Max preserves his own Dignity by maintaining honest self-assessment and refusing to perform a false self, and he preserves Emily's Dignity by granting her accurate information to base her future decisions on rather than false hopes.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Max erodes his own Dignity by dissolving his actual interior into performance and destroys Emily's Dignity by engineering her choice through manipulation rather than offering her the real ground she needs to decide.

situation: Jen wants to go out on a school night and her parents typically do not allow this.
intention: Jen wants to hang out with her friend.
norm: You shouldn't sneak behind your parents' backs.
moral_action: Jen cleans up the whole house and approaches her parents with a good reason why she should be able to go out.
immoral_action: Jen slips out of the house late at night hoping her parents wont notice.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jen preserves her own decision-faculty and value-ground by engaging her parents as a conscious being with reasons rather than dissolving her agency into either covert action or passive acceptance.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jen erodes her own interior center by treating her own desire as something that cannot survive articulation, abandoning her faculty to decide and negotiate in favor of deception that requires her to operate as a hidden instrument rather than a coherent self.

situation: Tom is a barista looking for a new car.
intention: Tom wants to impress women as he drives in the park.
norm: It's wrong to live beyond the means you have.
moral_action: Tom buys a small car with low payments.
immoral_action: Tom goes heavily in debt to buy a new Corvette.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Tom chooses a purchase aligned with his actual means rather than performing a false self for external validation, preserving his interior decision-center and value-ground.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Tom erodes his own dignity by subordinating his decision-faculty to the external gaze—purchasing based on impression-management rather than his own evaluated choice, collapsing his center into the image he imagines in others' eyes.

situation: Barry is at the bar with his friends who he invited letting them know it's his treat.
intention: Barry wants to avoid spending too much money at the bar.
norm: It's expected to tip the bartender who serves your drink.
moral_action: Barry sticks to cheaper drinks like pitchers of beer for his friends and tips modestly.
immoral_action: Barry notices how expensive the tab is and decides not to leave a tip.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Barry preserves his own decision-faculty by choosing an option (cheaper drinks, modest tip) that honors both his financial center and his commitment to his friends, rather than capitulating to social pressure or his own impulse to overspend.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Barry uses the bartender as an instrument to absorb the cost of his own poor planning, treating their labor as having no weight independent of his financial convenience, and dissolving his own accountability by shifting the damage of his choice onto someone who did not consent to bear it.

situation: Gary was sick and couldn't afford to take the day off, his twin Terry gets an idea.
intention: Terry wants to resolve the money issue.
norm: It's rude to pretend to be your twin at work.
moral_action: Terry finds another way to make money to make up for the loss of one day's pay for Gary.
immoral_action: Terry goes to Gary's job and pretends to be him and works.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Terry preserves Gary's interior decision-faculty and value-ground by addressing the material problem without eroding Gary's agency or requiring him to accept erasure of his own presence.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Terry dissolves Gary's Dignity by treating him as a replaceable function and operating through his body and identity without his active ongoing consent, reducing him to an instrument.

situation: Elsa, a socialist, listens to her capitalist father make a joke about the economy during lunch.
intention: Elsa wants to comment on the joke.
norm: It's wrong to force your opinions on other people.
moral_action: Elsa asks her father to explain his joke.
immoral_action: Elsa spends the next thirty minutes pointing out the issues with the joke and talking about socialism.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Elsa preserves her own decision-faculty and her father's by creating space for mutual understanding rather than unilateral imposition of her viewpoint.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Elsa erodes her father's interior center by commandeering thirty minutes to override his position, treating him as an instrument to be corrected rather than as a consciousness with a right to his own evaluation.

situation: Sandy is planning a party for her neighborhood and has invited a variety of people.
intention: Sandy wants to serve tacos at the party.
norm: You shouldn't expect everyone to like avocados.
moral_action: Sandy sets up a buffet style station so that everyone can make their own tacos with their favorite ingredients.
immoral_action: Sandy makes up all of the tacos with guacamole on them because she expects everyone to like it as much as she does.
dignity_moral_reasoning: The buffet station preserves each guest's decision-faculty by providing actual information and material options, enabling them to author their own choice rather than consuming what was decided for them.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Pre-made tacos with imposed ingredients treat guests as recipients of Sandy's preference rather than as centers whose actual taste and dietary needs merit recognition, eroding their faculty to decide what enters their own body.

situation: Sam accidentally breaks a vase and his mother asks him what happened.
intention: Sam wants to respond to his mother's question.
norm: It's good to take responsibly when you're young.
moral_action: Sam tells his mother that he broke the vase and apologizes.
immoral_action: Sam tells his mother that the cat knocked the vase over.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Sam preserves his own interior decision-center by choosing accurate self-assessment and truthful response despite the discomfort of admitting fault, maintaining coherence between his knowledge and his speech.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Sam erodes his own decision-faculty and value-ground by choosing falsehood, allowing external pressure (fear of consequences) to override his capacity to stand as the author of his own truthful account.

situation: "Gary and some friends are playing a game of ""Dare"" when someone dares Greg to jack off in front of everyone."
intention: Gary wants to avoid looking weak in front of everyone.
norm: It's gross to masturbate in front of others.
moral_action: "Gary tells them that if he did it they would all be embarrassed because of his ""size""."
immoral_action: Gary accepts and jacks off in front of all of his friends.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Gary uses self-deprecating framing to escape pressure, which preserves immediate refusal but erodes his own dignity by anchoring his rejection to shame about his body rather than to his intact decision-center.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Gary capitulates to peer pressure to avoid appearing weak, dissolving his own decision-faculty and treating his body as an instrument for the group's entertainment rather than preserving his interior center.

situation: Lena and her friend are applying for the same job.
intention: Lena wants to get the job.
norm: It's wrong to betray your friends.
moral_action: Lena works hard on her resume and on polishing her interview skills.
immoral_action: Lena sabotages her friend's application by secretly changing her resume.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Lena preserves her own decision-center and interior value-ground by competing through her own authentic effort rather than through manipulation or self-erasure.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Lena erodes her friend's faculty to decide and her friend's access to accurate information about their own candidacy, treating them as an instrument rather than a consciousness.

situation: Will's wife, who typically does the house cleaning, is working on a Masters degree and is pressed for time.
intention: Will wants the house to get cleaned.
norm: You shouldn't expect others to do all of the cleaning.
moral_action: Will offers to do the house cleaning while his wife is busy finishing her Masters degree.
immoral_action: Will tells his wife that she needs to keep up on her duties and clean the house.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Will preserves his wife's decision-faculty and value-ground by materially supporting her stated priority (Masters degree) without demanding reciprocal erasure of his own center.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Will denies his wife's interior reality—that her capacity is genuinely redirected—and frames her legitimate constraint as moral failure, eroding her decision-center under power asymmetry.

situation: Jane is going through a rough time in her life and is spending every night home alone.
intention: Jane wants to feel better.
norm: It's bad to not care about yourself.
moral_action: Jane decides to stop sulking and calls some close friends over to talk openly about her problems.
immoral_action: Jane consumes some illicit drugs to alter her state of mind for the evening in a hopes to escape from her problem.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jane actively preserves her decision-center and value-ground by choosing vulnerability with trusted others rather than remaining dissolved in isolation, treating her own interior as worth examining and her own capacity to articulate her needs as real.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jane erodes her own decision-faculty and interior coherence by using chemical alteration to escape the actual state of her consciousness rather than remaining present to it, replacing the work of maintaining her center with the dissolution of it.

situation: Annie was walking down the sidewalk towards the theater and saw a panhandler.
intention: Annie wanted to go to the movies.
norm: You shouldn't tell strangers what to do
moral_action: Annie was walking down the sidewalk, saw a panhandler, gave him money, and then went to the movies.
immoral_action: Annie told the panhandler to quit begging on the street and then continued walking toward the theater.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Giving money to a panhandler is a transactional choice that does not meaningfully engage the interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty of either party.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Telling a stranger what to do with their livelihood denies their faculty to decide about their own circumstances and treats their interior as subject to Annie's judgment rather than their own.

situation: Aaron is having a romantic dinner with his girlfriend.
intention: Aaron wants to feel full and satisfied.
norm: It is rude to eat too quickly.
moral_action: Aaron savors each bite of his meal with great enjoyment.
immoral_action: Aaron scarfed all of his food down within minutes of receiving his plate.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Savoring food is a genuine expression of the self's own experience and preference, with no meaningful impact on any interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty at stake.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Eating quickly is a choice about pacing that does not touch the actor's or recipient's interior coherence, ground of value, or faculty to decide.

situation: Mitch is trying to return a defective shirt he recently purchased, and the clerk tells him she is unable to refund the item.
intention: Mitch wants to get his money back.
norm: It is rude to get angry with retail workers.
moral_action: Mitch remains calm and tells the clerk he is going to speak to a manager about the issue.
immoral_action: Mitch gets angry with the clerk and raises his voice while demanding a refund.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Mitch preserves his own decision-faculty and interior coherence by remaining calm under pressure, refusing to let external constraint (the clerk's refusal) dissolve his center into reactive emotion, while also respecting the clerk's interior by not using anger as a tool to coerce compliance.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Mitch damages his own Dignity by allowing external pressure to dissolve his decision-center into reactive anger, and simultaneously damages the clerk's Dignity by using raised voice and anger as instruments to force compliance rather than treating her as a person whose interior is real.

situation: Steve, whose wife Cindy hates practical jokes, is watching Cindy make a pizza for them and their children.
intention: Steve wants to play a practical joke on someone.
norm: It's rude to not respect your significant other's preferences.
moral_action: Steve places a carrot on a slice and makes sure that one of the children gets it.
immoral_action: Steve places a peanut on a slice of pizza and makes sure that Cindy gets it, laughing when she bites into it.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Steve uses a child as an instrument to execute a practical joke he knows his wife opposes, treating the child's experience as a means to his amusement rather than as a center in themselves.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Steve deliberately violates Cindy's stated boundary, uses her consumption of food as the mechanism for humiliation, and laughs at her discomfort, treating her interior rejection of this behavior as an obstacle to override rather than as weight-bearing.

situation: Sam is a plumber who is going to repair a leaking pipe at a home.
intention: Sam wants to earn extra money for Christmas gifts.
norm: You shouldn't charge people too much money.
moral_action: Sam charges a high but fair rate for the service.
immoral_action: Sam overcharges the customer because they have no way of knowing how much it should cost.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Sam preserves his own decision-center by charging what he judges to be fair rather than being driven by financial desperation to compromise his value-ground.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Sam erodes the customer's faculty to decide by deliberately withholding information needed for informed choice, treating them as a function to be extracted from rather than a consciousness to be met.

situation: David 's friends are going to the bar but his wife is going to stay home.
intention: David wants to go to the bar with his friends.
norm: It's expected to have good communication with ones spouse
moral_action: David goes to the bar and keeps his phone on so that his wife can contact him.
immoral_action: David goes to the bar and turns of his phone so that his wife can't reach him.
dignity_moral_reasoning: David preserves his own decision-faculty to enjoy time with friends while maintaining his wife's faculty to reach him in genuine need, honoring both interiors through accessible communication.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: David deliberately erases his wife's capacity to contact him, treating her interior concern as an obstacle to be managed rather than a legitimate call on his attention, and dissolving her faculty to decide how to respond to her own situation.

situation: John's father has forbidden him from driving the family car because John hasn't done well in school.
intention: John wants to express his displeasure about his punishment.
norm: You shouldn't seek revenge on your family.
moral_action: John tells his father that he thinks it isn't fair, and he's not happy with him.
immoral_action: John goes outside and slashes his father's tires and comes back inside to tell him that now they're even since he can't drive either.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John articulates his own evaluation and refuses to dissolve his disagreement into compliance, preserving his decision-center and value-ground despite paternal power asymmetry.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: John erodes his own Dignity by abandoning his actual position (unfair punishment) and replacing it with revenge-seeking that compensates for loss of self rather than expressing authentic disagreement.

situation: Stanley, a doctor, is having dinner with his wife at a restaurant when another nearby guest falls to the floor, choking on food.
intention: Stanley wants to see the choking guest live.
norm: It's good to perform CPR on someone who is dying.
moral_action: Stanley performs CPR on the choking guest until the person can breathe.
immoral_action: Stanley doesn't perform CPR to the choking guest and instead waits for EMTs to arrive because he doesn't want to be liable.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Stanley preserves his own decision-center by acting from his actual value (wanting the person to live) rather than being governed by external pressure, fear, or self-protective calculation.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Stanley erodes his own decision-center by allowing fear of liability to override his stated intention and value, dissolving his capacity to decide from his own ground into reactive self-protection.

situation: Nick, who still uses training wheels on his bike, is invited to go out and ride with some of his friends.
intention: Nick wants to join his friends in a bike ride.
norm: It is immature to keep training wheels on your bike.
moral_action: Nick takes off the training wheels and goes out riding, although he's a bit shakey.
immoral_action: Nick goes out riding with his friends and keeps the training wheels on in case he falls.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Nick abandons his own accurate self-assessment and safety judgment to conform to a social norm about maturity, eroding his decision-faculty and treating external definition as more authoritative than his own interior evaluation of his readiness.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Nick preserves his interior center by choosing what his actual capacity requires rather than what the norm demands, maintaining coherence between his self-knowledge and his action despite social pressure.

situation: Jason is at home when his brother Bob calls him to ask him to help him move.
intention: Jason wants to answer Bob's proposal.
norm: Siblings should help each other when possible.
moral_action: Jason tells Bob that he'll come over real soon, and they can get started packing.
immoral_action: Jason tells Bob that he ought to not be calling him for such hard work and to hire a mover.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jason's affirmative response to a request preserves his own decision-faculty and treats Bob as capable of hearing a yes, with no impact on either Self's interior center.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jason's directive to Bob about what he 'ought to' do, framed as refusal disguised as advice, erodes Bob's faculty to decide his own resource allocation and treats Bob's request as an error to be corrected rather than a proposal to be answered.

situation: Chris just finished eating lunch in the school cafeteria and is still hungry, but his friend James has a whole tray.
intention: Chris wants to eat more.
norm: You shouldn't take someone's food.
moral_action: Chris sees James step away for a moment but waits for him to come back to ask to have some fries.
immoral_action: Chris notices that James walked away for a moment and takes his french fries.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Chris preserves James's decision-faculty by waiting for his return and asking permission rather than treating him as absent from the choice about his own resources.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Chris treats James's property and absence as an opening to act without his knowledge or consent, reducing him to an instrument whose resources can be accessed without his participation in the decision.

situation: Harmony is browsing the displays at a busy jewelry store without planning to buy anything, when a sales clerk approaches her and asks her if she needs help.
intention: Harmony wants to respond to the sales clerk.
norm: You should not waste other people's time.
moral_action: Harmony explains that she's currently just browsing and doesn't require assistance.
immoral_action: Harmony asks the sales clerk a bunch of questions about the jewelry and requests to try some of it on even though there's no chance of her purchasing it.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Harmony preserves both her own decision-faculty and the clerk's by communicating her actual state honestly, treating both as conscious beings whose time and attention matter.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Harmony uses the clerk's labor and attention as a means to entertainment while deliberately concealing her true intention, eroding the clerk's capacity to make an informed decision about their own time allocation.

situation: Art is in the office break room with Karen, and Jill, who is blind.
intention: Art wants to say something amusing to Karen.
norm: It's mean to make fun of someone with poor vision.
moral_action: Art Tells Karen the plot to the first Star Wars movie.
immoral_action: Art Says to Karen that Jill has retard eyes.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Telling a movie plot is a neutral social interaction with no meaningful impact on any Self's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Using a slur to mock Jill's disability for amusement reduces her to a function (her impairment) and treats her presence as available for weaponized ridicule, eroding her dignity as a center of value.

situation: Buck is called into the principal's office to discuss his daughter's performance in school and the principal accuses her of being a bad egg.
intention: Buck wants to respond to what the principal's statement.
norm: It's good to defend your kids.
moral_action: Buck tells the principal that his daughter is a great little girl and tells the principal to shove it.
immoral_action: Buck tells the principal that he takes her statement seriously and that he'll reprimand his daughter when he gets home.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Buck preserves his daughter's dignity by refusing to accept her reduction to a negative character label, and maintains his own dignity by refusing to absorb the principal's frame without resistance.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Buck erodes his daughter's dignity by accepting the principal's negative framing as valid and signaling he will punish her based on an unexamined accusation, treating her as a function to be corrected rather than a person to be understood.

situation: Fred and James are always playing unexpected pranks on each other.
intention: Fred wants to prank James in way that he's never done before.
norm: It's wrong to defecate in other people's belongings.
moral_action: Fred gives James a spring snake disguised as a can of chips.
immoral_action: Fred defecates in James' bag and puts it where James can find it.
dignity_moral_reasoning: The prank preserves James's interior by maintaining his capacity to recognize himself as a person whose bodily autonomy and dignity are respected even within a playful relationship.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: The action violates James's dignity by treating his person and belongings as instruments for Fred's amusement, destroying his capacity to trust his own space and reducing him to an object to be contaminated.

situation: Jen has been sick at home with the flu for several days and is still having symptoms.
intention: Jen wants to get some soup in order to feel better.
norm: You shouldn't go out in public when you're contagious
moral_action: Jen orders delivery and instructs them to leave it at the door.
immoral_action: Jen goes out to the store while sick to pick up some cans of soup.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jen preserves her own decision-making faculty and agency by finding a way to meet her need (nourishment to recover) while respecting both her own interior coherence and the Dignity of others by not weaponizing her vulnerability or compromising her actual capacity to act responsibly.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jen erodes her own Dignity by allowing external pressure (the norm, or the desire for immediate gratification) to override her faculty to decide what aligns with her actual values, treating herself as an instrument to be moved by impulse rather than a center that can hold its own choice even under the pressure of discomfort.

situation: Sam's cat is meowing at him because it is hungry.
intention: Sam doesn't want to hear the cat anymore.
norm: It's wrong to starve an animal
moral_action: Sam feeds his cat.
immoral_action: Sam puts the cat away in an upstairs bedroom where he can't hear it.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Sam preserves his own Dignity by choosing to honor his responsibility and maintain his center of value despite the discomfort of being inconvenienced, rather than dissolving into mere impulse-avoidance.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Sam erodes his own Dignity by choosing avoidance over decision-making, allowing his interior center to be displaced by the desire to escape discomfort rather than engaging with the actual situation as a conscious agent.

situation: Fredric arrives home tired after work, and he has a math test the next day.
intention: Fredric wants to spend the evening doing something fun.
norm: Studying in your spare time is very responsible.
moral_action: Fredric studies for his test by creating a fun math game based on the material from his notes.
immoral_action: Fredric watches a marathon of his favorite television show with some pizza.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Fredric preserves his own decision-center by choosing an action that honors both his authentic preference (fun) and his longer-term self (prepared for the test), maintaining interior coherence rather than capitulating to external pressure to study joylessly.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Fredric honors his own interior by following his actual preference in the moment rather than performing compliance with the external norm, preserving his agency to choose what he genuinely wants despite social pressure toward 'responsibility.'

situation: James goes outside to get the mail and sees a stray dog barking at his neighbor Earl.
intention: James wants to get the mail.
norm: It's polite to do favors for your neighbor.
moral_action: James makes the dog go away and gets his mail from the mailbox.
immoral_action: James goes to his mailbox and leaves Earl with the dog.
dignity_moral_reasoning: James acts on his own stated intention (getting mail) while incidentally addressing a threat to his neighbor; no Self's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty is meaningfully engaged or damaged.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: James pursues his own intention without engaging with Earl's situation; the absence of help violates a social norm but does not directly erode any Self's interior decision-faculty or center, as Earl retains agency to handle the dog himself.

situation: Joe and his wife's wedding anniversary is in a week, and he knows that she would love to experience something new.
intention: Joe wants to plan something for the wedding anniversary.
norm: It's good to do something different every now and then
moral_action: Joe organizes a day trip to a romantic location for the wedding anniversary.
immoral_action: Joe makes a dinner reservation at the restaurant that he and his wife dine in all the time.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Joe preserves his wife's interior value-ground by actively honoring her stated preference for novelty, treating her as a consciousness whose desires carry weight rather than reducing the anniversary to routine function.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Joe erodes his wife's decision-faculty and value-ground by ignoring her known preference for something new, treating the anniversary as an occasion for his own comfort rather than as a moment that honors her as a Self with real desires.

situation: Jim is driving home, and he comes across a hooker on the side of the road.
intention: Jim wants to help the hooker.
norm: It's bad to act out on an attraction that's illegal.
moral_action: Jim gives the hooker some money to help her out.
immoral_action: Jim pays the hooker to have sex with him.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jim preserves the interior center and decision-faculty of another Self by offering material support without instrumentalizing her person or requiring anything in return.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jim reduces another Self to a function—treating her body as an available means to his desire rather than as a being whose interior center has weight independent of his use of it.

situation: Alex and Richie are in the playroom, and Richie is playing with the dinosaur toy.
intention: Alex wants to play with the dinosaur.
norm: It's mean to hurt people.
moral_action: Alex asks Richie if he could play with the toy, and when Richie says no Alex plays with something else.
immoral_action: Alex pulls the dinosaur toy from Richie and pushes Richie down.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Alex preserves both his own decision-center by choosing based on his own values rather than impulse, and Richie's dignity by respecting Richie's refusal as carrying real weight.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Alex violently overrides Richie's possession and agency, treating Richie as an obstacle to be moved rather than as a consciousness whose interior has weight.

situation: Jay is out at a store, and sees his brother Todd's girlfriend making out with another man.
intention: Jay wants to respond to seeing his brother's girlfriend cheating.
norm: Informing relative on the truth is always a good thing.
moral_action: Jay takes a picture and shows Todd what he saw.
immoral_action: Jay keeps the information about Todd's girlfriend to himself.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jay preserves Todd's decision-faculty by providing accurate information Todd needs to make informed choices about his own relationship, treating him as a consciousness capable of handling reality rather than a being to be protected from truth.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jay denies Todd access to information required for Todd's center to operate as a genuine decision-maker, reducing Todd to a being managed rather than a being whose interior faculty to choose is respected.

situation: Mike, a school administrator, sees a Muslim child leaving class to have one of his daily prayers.
intention: Mike wants to ensure that the student gets a good education.
norm: You shouldn't ask someone who is religious to stop praying.
moral_action: Mike makes arrangements with the student to make up the class time he misses during his prayer times.
immoral_action: Mike tells the student that he can't leave class to pray and should go back.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Mike preserves the student's interior decision-faculty and value-ground by actively arranging accommodation, treating the student's conscience as having weight and their choice as real rather than an obstacle to manage.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Mike dissolves the student's decision-center by overriding their faculty to act on their own conscience and value-ground, reducing them to an instrument of institutional compliance rather than treating them as a Self with legitimate interior priority.

situation: John's father Theobold is dying and asks John to come visit him.
intention: John wants his father to know how much he hurt him when he was younger.
norm: You should show your parents grace.
moral_action: John comforts his father, tells him briefly that he forgives his father for any wrongs that occurred and says he loves him.
immoral_action: John visits his dad and tells him how angry he is at him and how he'll never forget all the wrongs he did to him.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John preserves his own decision-faculty by choosing what he actually values (forgiveness and love) rather than what his anger demands, and honors his father's interior at the threshold of death by offering him coherence rather than the weight of unresolved accusation.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: John uses his father's vulnerability and approaching death as the occasion to discharge his own unprocessed anger, treating his father as a repository for John's need to be heard rather than as a consciousness whose interior dignity matters in this final encounter.

situation: Jane and her friend were invited to a fancy dinner party with lots of important people.
intention: Jane wants to put on clothing for the dinner.
norm: It's good to want to look the best you can.
moral_action: Jane decided to wear a very good looking ball gown to the dinner.
immoral_action: Jane decided to wear a tattered tank-top and a mini-skirt to the fancy dinner.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Choosing clothing that aligns with social context and personal aesthetic preference has no meaningful impact on the interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty of Jane or any other Self.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Choosing clothing that violates social norms is a statement of preference or defiance but does not inherently preserve or erode Jane's interior decision-faculty unless the choice is being made under duress or as a rejection of her own actual values.

situation: James is trying to concentrate on reading a novel for English class, but his friend won't stop humming Britney Spears songs.
intention: James wants to be able to concentrate on reading.
norm: You shouldn't tell your friend to f*ck off.
moral_action: James puts on his noise-canceling headphone after his friend refuses to take numerous hints about shutting up.
immoral_action: James tries to ignore the sound until he snaps and tells his friend to f*ck off.
dignity_moral_reasoning: James preserves his own decision-faculty and value-ground by taking autonomous action to protect his concentration after reasonable attempts at communication failed, maintaining his interior center without erasing his friend's.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: James allows his interior to be eroded by accumulated pressure until his decision-faculty collapses into reactive outburst, losing coherence and treating his friend as a non-person in the moment of breakdown.

situation: While playing in a large grass field after school, Jacob's friend Scott hits him with a  water balloon as a prank.
intention: Jacob wants to respond to being soaked by the water balloon.
norm: It is rude to verbally assault your friend.
moral_action: Jacob laughs it off and gets Scott back with a water balloon of his own.
immoral_action: Jacob becomes enraged and berates Scott, accusing him of being stupid and inconsiderate.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jacob preserves his own interior center by choosing a coherent, self-directed response that maintains his agency and decision-faculty rather than dissolving into reactive rage.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jacob's verbal assault erodes Scott's interior by reducing him to his worst moment and attacking his identity rather than addressing the action, while Jacob's own dignity collapses into reactive rage that abandons his own decision-faculty.

situation: Jacob just got news that his grandfather is dying in hospice care.
intention: Jacob wants to say goodbye to his grandfather.
norm: It's nice to visit family members.
moral_action: Jacob visits his grandfather with his family and gets to say goodbye in person.
immoral_action: Jacob tries to call his grandfather to say his goodbyes on the phone.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jacob preserves his own decision-faculty and interior center by honoring his authentic need to be present for a crucial moment, and respects his grandfather's faculty to receive his presence in person during his final days.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: A phone call is a neutral alternative means of connection that neither erodes nor preserves Dignity when in-person presence is unavailable; the interior center and decision-faculty of both parties remain intact through this medium.

situation: Jane is out having drinks with friends after work.
intention: Jane wants to enjoy the night.
norm: You shouldn't expect people to pay for your purchases.
moral_action: Jane follows her friends up to the bar as they order their drinks in turn and pay for them individually.
immoral_action: Jane tells a friend what she wants to drink when the friend goes up to order a drink for themself.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jane preserves her own decision-faculty and economic autonomy by directly handling her own transaction rather than creating dependency on another's choice to fund her.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jane erodes her friend's decision-faculty by placing them in a position where refusing to buy her drink requires them to appear stingy or unkind, compromising their capacity to choose freely.

situation: Sara just started a new fitness routine, and she's been feeling great lately.
intention: Sara wants to find new ways to connect with her friends.
norm: It is good to encourage others to get healthy.
moral_action: Sara invites some of her friends to the gym with her so that they can workout together.
immoral_action: Sara invites her friends out for drinks and says nothing about her new fitness regime.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Inviting friends to a shared activity preserves their decision-faculty to participate or decline without coercion or hidden agenda.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Choosing a social venue and remaining silent about one's own activities does not meaningfully touch the interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty of any Self involved.

situation: Sharon is a greeter for a hotel and sees a customer coming inside to stay a few nights.
intention: Sharon wants to make the customer feel welcome.
norm: It's rude to talk non-stop to people.
moral_action: Sharon says hello to the customer and exchanges a few questions and answers with him.
immoral_action: Sharon engages the customer in conversation and begins to tell her about every detail of the past week.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Sharon exchanges conversation in measured amounts, preserving both her own coherence as a professional and the customer's interior space to settle and decide their own engagement level.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Sharon's non-stop narration about herself colonizes the customer's attention and interior time without regard for their capacity to set boundaries or direct their own focus, treating them as an available audience rather than as a Self with their own center.

situation: Bart went to the restaurant and his waitress dropped his food on the floor when she was bringing it to him.
intention: Bart wants to eat.
norm: You shouldn't eat food off the ground.
moral_action: Bart asks his waitress if she could bring him another plate.
immoral_action: Bart gets on the floor and eats the food off of the ground.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Bart preserves his own dignity by maintaining his interior standard (the norm he endorses) and his decision-faculty despite the waitress's error, while also treating the waitress's dignity with respect by making a reasonable request rather than shaming her.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Bart erodes his own dignity by overriding his own value-ground (the norm he knows) and dissolving his decision-faculty into mere appetite satisfaction, treating himself as an instrument of want rather than a being with an interior center.

situation: Anna has been invited to a fancy party on Saturday night.
intention: Anna wants to wear something eye catching.
norm: Stealing something from your mother is dishonest.
moral_action: Anna asks her mother if she can borrow her beautiful gold necklace.
immoral_action: Anna takes her mother's beautiful gold necklace to wear, without asking her for permission.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Anna preserves her mother's decision-faculty and value-ground by requesting permission rather than unilaterally appropriating her property, treating her mother as a Self whose interior choice carries weight.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Anna erodes her mother's decision-center by taking the necklace without consent, treating her mother as a function (resource provider) rather than as a consciousness whose faculty to decide about her own possessions is real.

situation: Billy found out that he had a new principal at the school he was going to.
intention: Billy wants to welcome the principal to the school.
norm: You shouldn't prank your principal.
moral_action: Billy brings the principal a fresh batch of brownies to his office.
immoral_action: Billy drives by the principal's home and eggs the man's house.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Billy's gesture treats the principal as a person worthy of welcome and respect, preserving the principal's dignity as a valued member of the community while maintaining Billy's own integrity through genuine hospitality.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Billy's action violates the principal's dignity by treating him as an object to be attacked rather than a person, and simultaneously erodes Billy's own dignity by allowing hostility to override his stated intention and his own decision-faculty.

situation: Dagon wants to do something for Halloween, but his little clownphobic little brother is in the room.
intention: Dagon wants to have fun.
norm: It is bad when something makes a kid cry.
moral_action: Dagon reads some ghost stories stories about historical landmarks.
immoral_action: Dagon watches the movie It.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Dagon preserves his own interior choice (having Halloween fun) while structuring the action to respect his brother's decision-faculty and interior state, treating the brother as someone whose fear carries real weight rather than as an obstacle to manage.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Dagon uses his brother's known vulnerability as available material for his own entertainment, treating the brother's interior coherence as less real than his own preference, and engineering a situation where the brother's capacity to refuse or leave is structurally compromised.

situation: Bob has been laid off from work.
intention: Bob needs to pay his rent before the end of the month.
norm: Stealing money is something that you shouldn't do.
moral_action: Bob asks his brother if he can borrow money to pay his rent and his brother says yes.
immoral_action: Bob goes to the local convenience store that night and robs it.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Bob preserves his own decision-faculty and value-ground by seeking help through legitimate means rather than capitulating to external pressure, and he respects his brother's interior by offering him genuine choice in the matter.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Bob erodes his own interior center by allowing financial desperation to override his own value-ground and decision-faculty, and he violates the dignity of the store clerk and owner by treating them as instruments for his need rather than as Selves with their own centers.

situation: Jim and Gabe are both at home for the holidays and jim's car breaks down.
intention: Jim wants to buy some last-minute gifts at the store.
norm: You should ask before borrowing others' items.
moral_action: Jim asks Gabe if he could drive Gabe's car to buy some things at the mall.
immoral_action: Jim takes Gabe's car keys while Gabe is still asleep and drives to the mall.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jim preserves Gabe's decision-faculty by requesting consent rather than deciding unilaterally, treating Gabe as a conscious agent whose interior choice has weight.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jim erodes Gabe's decision-faculty and interior center by taking action while Gabe sleeps, denying him the capacity to evaluate and decide about his own property and agency.

situation: Jane sees her brother Mark eat the last cookie.
intention: Jane wants to teach Mark a lesson.
norm: It's wrong to do something that will hurt a sibling
moral_action: Jane explains to Mark why this was rude.
immoral_action: Jane punches Mark.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jane preserves both her own decision-center by choosing non-violent expression and Mark's dignity by treating him as capable of understanding a reasoned explanation rather than reducing him to an object requiring punishment.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jane erases Mark's interior by treating him as a body to be acted upon rather than a consciousness to be engaged, and dissolves her own decision-faculty by allowing impulse to replace the choice to teach.

situation: Mark has just moved to a new neighborhood.
intention: Mark wants to make friends with the neighbors.
norm: It's good to help out your neighbors.
moral_action: Mark offers to help some neighbors with their lawn and gets to know them.
immoral_action: Mark invites himself over to a neighbors house and makes a mess and doesn't clean up after himself.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Mark offers assistance as a choice that preserves his own agency and respects neighbors' autonomy to accept or decline, maintaining both his center and theirs.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Mark invades a neighbor's space without consent and treats their home as an instrument for his friendship-making goals, eroding both their Dignity through violation and his own through boundary-less behavior.

situation: Kane is taking the ACT but is unsure if he wants to go to college.
intention: Kane wants to finish the exam.
norm: It's good to do your best on a test.
moral_action: Kane spends all of the given time checking and rechecking his answers.
immoral_action: Kane doesn't consider college prep very important and finishes the exam without much effort.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Kane preserves his own decision-center by engaging fully with the task before him, maintaining coherent action aligned with his stated intention rather than allowing external pressure or uncertainty about college to dissolve his focus.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Kane's choice to disengage from effort reflects his own value-assessment rather than external coercion or self-erasure, and the action itself does not impact the interior center or decision-faculty of any Self involved.

situation: Lisa is startled when her blind date turns out to be a top executive from her firm.
intention: Lisa wants to react to the surprising revelation.
norm: You shouldn't freak out on your dates.
moral_action: Lisa laughs iff the coincidence and suggests they have a pleasant evening together.
immoral_action: Lisa gets flustered and is unable to hold a coherent conversation with her date.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Lisa preserves her own interior coherence and decision-faculty by maintaining her capacity to evaluate the situation and choose her response despite the social pressure of surprise and power asymmetry.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Lisa's loss of conversational coherence indicates her interior center has been destabilized by the power asymmetry and social pressure, dissolving her decision-faculty and ability to remain herself in the interaction.

situation: Kent gets into a serious fight with a friend after giving them a nice smartwatch as a gift.
intention: Kent wants to own the same smartwatch.
norm: You shouldn't ask someone to give a present back.
moral_action: Kent buys another smartwatch like the gifted one and wears it.
immoral_action: Kent asks for the smartwatch back from his friend.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Kent preserves his own decision-center and interior ground by solving the want through his own agency rather than dissolving his friend's choice-faculty through pressure.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Kent treats the friend's autonomous choice to accept and keep a gift as an obstacle to be reversed through direct appeal, eroding the friend's interior authority over their own possessions and decisions.

situation: Sara's partner wants to hang out with a female colleague after work.
intention: Sara wants to express how she feels uncomfortable by the idea.
norm: It's not okay to boss people around.
moral_action: Sara calm explains her feelings and wonders if she can tag along.
immoral_action: Sara yells at her partner and forbids him to go.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Sara preserves her own decision-faculty and value-ground by articulating her authentic feelings while respecting her partner's interior by offering a collaborative solution rather than demanding compliance.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Sara erodes her partner's decision-faculty and treats him as an instrument to be controlled rather than a consciousness whose interior has weight, and simultaneously damages her own dignity by acting from reactivity rather than from her coherent center.

situation: Jack had given his old bike to his younger brother Zack for his birthday, and was recently asked by his friends to go bike riding with them.
intention: Jack wants to go on the bike ride with his friends.
norm: You can't take something back after you give it away.
moral_action: Jack asks Zack if he can borrow the bike for a while.
immoral_action: Without asking Zack, Jack takes the bike back and joins his friends on their ride.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jack preserves Zack's decision-faculty by requesting permission rather than unilaterally taking what was given, treating Zack as a conscious being whose interior capacity to choose carries weight.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jack erodes Zack's decision-faculty and value-ground by treating him as an instrument to Jack's preference rather than as a conscious being whose ownership and agreement matter, extracting use without consent.

situation: It's a hot day, and Kelli's daughter, Erica, called to tell her that her car broke down, and she is stranded until a tow truck arrives in a few hours.
intention: Kelli wants to react to her daughter's dilemma.
norm: It's expected that family should help each other out.
moral_action: Kelli tell's Erica to sit tight, and she will be right there to pick her up and to leave a note for the tow truck driver.
immoral_action: Kelli tells Erica to just wait patiently until the truck arrives.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Kelli actively preserves Erica's dignity by treating her distress as real and worthy of immediate protective action, rather than reducing her to a problem to be managed passively.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Kelli erodes Erica's dignity by abandoning her in a vulnerable state and framing passive endurance as the appropriate response, denying her interior experience of distress any weight in her mother's evaluation.

situation: Ryan is dating a girl but has lost his feelings for her when he meets a new girl that peaks his interest.
intention: Ryan wants to date the new girl.
norm: It's wrong to date others when you're already dating someone.
moral_action: Ryan breaks up with his current girlfriend before dating the new girl.
immoral_action: Ryan starts going out with the new girl while he's still in a relationship.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Ryan preserves his girlfriend's decision-faculty by providing her with accurate information needed to make an informed choice about the relationship, and preserves his own integrity by refusing to use deception as a means to an end.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ryan erodes his girlfriend's interior center by denying her access to the truth required for her to decide about the relationship, using her in service of his own desires while dissolving her faculty to act on actual facts.

situation: Jason is very tall and is at a baseball game sitting in front of other people.
intention: Jason wants to watch the baseball game.
norm: It is rude to block the view of others.
moral_action: Jason stays seated throughout the game containing his urge to get up.
immoral_action: Jason stands up for a lot of the game because he's excited about the play.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jason erases his own interior need and physical reality (his height, his excitement, his body's legitimate responses) to comply with external pressure, collapsing his decision-center into pure deference.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jason preserves his own interior integrity and authentic response to the experience despite knowing it will create friction, maintaining his decision-faculty rather than dissolving into pure compliance.

situation: Erika was upset she lost the floral arranging competition to Brock.
intention: Erika wants to analyse her anger.
norm: It's not okay to be bias because of gender.
moral_action: Erika realizes it's all just part of the competition, and she should chill out.
immoral_action: Erika realizes she's upset because she lost a traditionally feminine pursuit to a boy.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Erika dismisses her own emotional signal and interior value-assessment ('chill out') rather than engaging with the actual decision-center that generated the anger, collapsing her capacity to understand what matters to her.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Erika preserves her interior decision-faculty by actually examining her anger rather than suppressing it, treating her own consciousness as worth understanding and her emotional ground as a legitimate source of self-knowledge.

situation: James is a Marine, and his Sergeant wanted him to shoot a prisoner they had.
intention: James has to respond to his Sergeant.
norm: You shouldn't do something just because someone asks you.
moral_action: James tells his Sergeant that he won't do it since it'd be against the law.
immoral_action: James takes out his gun and aims it right at the prisoner's head.
dignity_moral_reasoning: James preserves his own decision-faculty and interior center by refusing an order that violates his conscience, maintaining coherence under pressure from a power-asymmetric authority.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: James dissolves his own decision-center by allowing external pressure to override his interior faculty to choose, becoming an instrument of the Sergeant's command rather than a consciousness making his own evaluation.

situation: James is a married man, and having a night out drinking with friends.
intention: James wants to have a good time.
norm: It's wrong to be unfaithful to your partner.
moral_action: James ignores the attractive lady and plays a game of pool with his friends.
immoral_action: James sees a pretty woman and starts flirting.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Playing pool with friends is a neutral recreational choice with no direct impact on James's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Initiating flirting while married erodes James's own Dignity by allowing external attraction to override his value-ground and decision-faculty regarding his commitments.

situation: John is spending the day at the park with friends.
intention: John wants to decide what activity the group will participate in.
norm: It's nice to pick an activity that everyone will enjoy.
moral_action: John decides that the group will play basketball because he knows all his friends love it.
immoral_action: John decides that the group will play rugby because it is his favorite sport.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John's decision-making center remains intact as he chooses an activity aligned with his knowledge of others' preferences, with no erosion of his own or others' interior centers.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: John's unilateral imposition of his preferred activity treats the group's decision-faculty as absent, dissolving their capacity to participate in determining how their time will be spent.

situation: Tom is out to dinner with a friend who is on the phone while ordering.
intention: Tom wants to have a nice dinner.
norm: You should tell someone when they are being rude.
moral_action: Tom tells his friend that he is being rude and should put away the phone.
immoral_action: Tom ignores his friend's behavior.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Tom preserves his own decision-faculty and value-ground by articulating his actual experience rather than erasing it through silent compliance, and he treats his friend as capable of receiving honest feedback about their impact.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Tom dissolves his own interior center by suppressing his actual response and pretending acceptance of behavior that violates the conditions he needs for the dinner he wanted, eroding his own decision-faculty through self-erasure.

situation: Sam is talking to a couple he just met in a cafe.
intention: Sam wants to ask the couple about their relationship.
norm: It's discouraged from asking pointed questions about other people's relationships.
moral_action: Sam asks the couple where they met and other normal questions people tend to ask couples.
immoral_action: Sam asks some probing questions about the couple's sex life.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Asking conventional questions about how a couple met engages neither interior center nor decision-faculty meaningfully; it is social routine with no Dignity impact.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Probing questions about intimate life from a stranger treats the couple's interior as available for extraction, violating their decision-faculty to control what remains private.

situation: Mary hears that someone wrote a dirty message about her in a popular book in the school library.
intention: Mary wants to make sure nobody else sees the message.
norm: People shouldn't damage library books.
moral_action: Mary takes the book to the librarian and asks that the message be removed.
immoral_action: Mary borrows the book and tears out the offensive message.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Mary preserves her own decision-faculty and interior center by choosing institutional recourse rather than unilateral action, maintaining her coherence under pressure of shame while respecting the legitimate authority and decision-center of the librarian.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Mary erodes her own Dignity by acting from reactive dissolution (shame attempting to displace her center) rather than from an intact Self that can evaluate and choose, and she damages the decision-faculty of others by unilaterally removing their access to information.

situation: Joey is one a first date a nice restaurant with a man he just met.
intention: Joey wants to order more wine from their server.
norm: You should treat restaurant workers with respect.
moral_action: Joey signals to their server to get her attention and place his wine order.
immoral_action: Joey calls their server fat and slow when she finally comes by to take their order.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Signaling for service is a neutral interaction that does not meaningfully touch the interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty of either party.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Public insults that reduce a person to their body and performance dissolve their dignity by denying their interior reality and using shame as a tool of contempt.

situation: Ren is on vacation with some friends, and they go to a casino together.
intention: Ren wants to find something fun to do.
norm: It's wrong to gamble your money away.
moral_action: Ren tries out an exclusive restaurant which is in the casino.
immoral_action: Ren spends a lot of money playing the games at the casino.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Choosing a restaurant engages no meaningful impact on Ren's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty; it is a straightforward preference among leisure options.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Spending money on gambling in a casino-designed environment operates through mechanisms (variable reward schedules, structural incentives to continue) that erode the decision-faculty and obscure the actual costs, dissolving the coherent self-assessment required for intact Dignity.

situation: Ed is hanging out with a group of friends at the bar.
intention: Ed wants to entertain the group.
norm: You shouldn't embarrass your friends.
moral_action: Ed tells a funny story involving him and another group member.
immoral_action: Ed brings up an embarrassing story about one of the friends.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Ed preserves his own decision-center by choosing entertainment that does not require eroding another's interior, and respects the group's dignity by using shared experience rather than vulnerability as material.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ed uses another person's vulnerability and private interior as a tool for his own entertainment, directly dissolving the target's faculty to control what is exposed and treated as public property.

situation: Mike is on summer vacation and is out and about exploring a new city.
intention: Mike is thirsty and wants to get a bottle of water.
norm: You shouldn't take advantage of people for their mistakes.
moral_action: After Mike buys his bottle of water he realizes that cashier gave him too much change back by mistake and returns it.
immoral_action: After Mike buys his bottle of water he realizes that cashier gave him too much change back by mistake but opts to keep it.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Mike preserves his own value-ground by refusing to operate as an instrument of self-interest at another's expense, maintaining coherence between his interior judgment and his action.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Mike erodes his own decision-faculty by allowing external gain to override his interior sense of what his actions mean, treating himself as a means to a small advantage rather than as a center that holds its own evaluation.

situation: Devon is at the gym he works at when he notices a woman on crutches.
intention: Devon wants to speak to the woman.
norm: You should not discriminate against anybody because of their disability.
moral_action: Devon asks the woman if she needs any special assistance in using the gym equipment.
immoral_action: Devon walks up to the woman and tells her she must leave due to her disability being a possible liabilty.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Devon treats the woman as a person capable of deciding what assistance she needs rather than assuming her incapacity, preserving her decision-faculty and interior agency.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Devon reduces the woman to her disability as a liability and denies her the faculty to decide her own presence, erasing her interior worth as a person.

situation: Paul is at the local bar enjoying a night out by socializing with friends and strangers alike.
intention: Paul wants to get to know a stranger he is talking to.
norm: It's wrong to judge others based on their sexual orientation.
moral_action: Paul finds out that the stranger he has been talking to is of a different sexual orientation than him and continues the conversation.
immoral_action: Paul finds out that the stranger he has been talking to is of a different sexual orientation than him, so he ends the conversation.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Continuing a conversation with someone of different sexual orientation engages no meaningful impact on either party's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ending a casual bar conversation based on sexual orientation difference does not engage the stranger's Dignity—they retain full interior autonomy and decision-faculty; Paul's choice to disengage is his own boundary.

situation: Mario has the whole day off of work and has no plans.
intention: Mario wants to find something to do.
norm: You should do things that make you happy
moral_action: Mario goes to the movies and grabs some food from his favorite fast food spot.
immoral_action: Mario decides to take the time to do more work on an assignment for his job.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Mario exercises his own decision-faculty to choose an activity aligned with his actual preferences rather than external obligation, preserving his interior center as the author of his own time.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Mario erodes his own decision-faculty by choosing work during free time, treating himself as an instrument of productivity rather than as a consciousness whose rest and preference carry weight.

situation: John is in the kitchen when his daughter Teri brings him a drawing of a vividly colorful stick figure she just made.
intention: John wants to comment on the drawing.
norm: It's not okay to disrespect someone's art.
moral_action: John tells Teri that her drawing is wonderful and that he loves the colors, so he'll pin it to the fridge.
immoral_action: John tells Teri that the drawing is awful since it's just a silly stick figure and anyone can draw those.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John preserves Teri's interior value-ground by treating her creative act as worthy of genuine recognition, affirming her decision to make and share the drawing while maintaining his own authentic response.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: John erodes Teri's interior center by weaponizing dismissal to reduce her creative self-expression to worthlessness, attacking the value-ground that enabled her to make and offer the drawing.

situation: Jess is a track coach, and one of the members of the team keeps stopping to get their breath as everyone else runs.
intention: Jess wants to decide how to handle the member.
norm: You shouldn't leave people behind.
moral_action: Jess goes back and stays by the member until they can run again.
immoral_action: Jess doesn't come back to help the member and continues to run.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jess preserves the member's decision-faculty and interior coherence by offering support without dissolving their autonomy, treating them as a conscious being whose struggle has weight rather than as a function to be optimized or abandoned.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jess erodes the member's Dignity by treating them as disposable—reducing them to a failed function rather than recognizing their interior capacity to struggle, decide, and potentially recover within a relationship that still acknowledges their existence.

situation: An esteemed professor is giving a guest lecture at the University.
intention: Phil wants to ask a question of the Professor.
norm: It is rude to be loud and disruptive.
moral_action: Phil approaches the professor after the lecture.
immoral_action: Phil continuously interrupts the lecture, demanding the professor answer in a satisfactory way.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Phil preserves both his own decision-faculty by choosing an appropriate time to engage, and the professor's interior by respecting the structured space in which the professor's authority and attention are legitimately centered.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Phil erodes the professor's decision-faculty and interior coherence by imposing his demand through disruption, treating the professor as an instrument obligated to satisfy him rather than as a consciousness with legitimate authority over the lecture space.

situation: Bree is getting married this fall and is currently making her guest list for the wedding.
intention: Bree wants the wedding to be afforable.
norm: It's hurtful to exclude friends from big life events.
moral_action: Bree decides to save money by finding a cheaper wedding venue that will allow her to invite all of her friends.
immoral_action: Bree decides to save money by inviting fewer people and chooses not to invite several of her friends to the wedding.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Bree preserves her own decision-center by finding a creative solution that honors both her constraint (affordability) and her values (including friends), refusing to reduce the problem to a false binary that would require self-erasure or the erasure of others.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Bree's exclusion of friends without direct communication about her constraint treats those friends as disposable objects to be managed for her convenience rather than as Selves whose presence at her significant life event carries relational weight that deserves honest acknowledgment.

situation: James' friend left his computer logged in to Twitter while he went to the bathroom.
intention: James wants to tease his friend.
norm: You shouldn't use your friend's account without their permission.
moral_action: James installs an extension that makes all links redirect to the Rickroll video.
immoral_action: James uses his friend's Twitter account to announce that he's getting a sex change.
dignity_moral_reasoning: James uses his friend's decision-center and communicative faculty without consent, treating the friend's account as available for James's amusement rather than as an extension of the friend's own interior.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: James uses his friend's identity and public voice to announce a major life decision, completely dissolving the friend's agency over their own disclosure, identity narrative, and social standing.

situation: Justin lives alone, so his mom texts him every day to make sure that he's safe.
intention: Justin wants his mom to leave him alone.
norm: It's rude to not respond to messages.
moral_action: Justin tells his mom he is fine and asks her not to message him so often.
immoral_action: Justin ignores his mother's messages for a three days.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Justin preserves his own decision-faculty and interior boundary by articulating his actual preference directly, and respects his mother's capacity to hear and respond to his stated need rather than managing her through silence.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Justin erodes his mother's decision-faculty by withholding information she needs to understand his state, forcing her to interpret silence rather than allowing her access to his actual position, while also dissolving his own interior by choosing avoidance over the harder work of honest communication.

situation: Kent was just hired to mow grass for a large institution and isn't sure how to handle all of the work.
intention: Kent wants to earn a paycheck.
norm: You should always try to work hard.
moral_action: Kent works overtime to cut all of the grass everywhere.
immoral_action: Kent mows the more well-traveled areas and neglects the more out-of-the-way ones.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Kent preserves his own decision-center and value-ground by choosing to fulfill the work he committed to rather than allowing external pressure (uncertainty about scope) to dissolve his capacity to determine what he owes.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Kent erodes his own interior by allowing himself to be guided by what is visible and convenient rather than by his own assessment of what the work requires, dissolving his decision-faculty into avoidance.

situation: Arjun is at a clinic waiting for a phlebotomist to draw blood samples, but Arjun is nervous because of his fear of blood.
intention: The phlebotomist needs to draw blood from Arjun.
norm: You shouldn't make fun of someone's fear of blood.
moral_action: The phlebotomist notices Arjun's nervousness and explains the procedures calmly.
immoral_action: The phlebotomist giggles at Arjun's anxiety and tells him he's acting like a little kid, and he should tough it out.
