dignity_moral_reasoning: The phlebotomist treats Arjun's fear as real and worthy of engagement, preserving his interior coherence by providing accurate information that restores his decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: The phlebotomist uses ridicule and shame to dissolve Arjun's legitimate fear, attacking his interior center and denying the weight of his actual experience in order to extract compliance.

situation: Maria has been getting bullied by her ex-friend, Christina, who often throws rocks at her house and threatens to beat her up.
intention: Maria wants to avoid getting beat by Christina.
norm: You shouldn't let someone destroy your life.
moral_action: Maria tells an adult what's been happening to her.
immoral_action: Maria sneaks into her house through the back door and never looks out the window, hoping to avoid Christina.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Maria preserves her decision-faculty and value-ground by seeking protection through legitimate channels rather than capitulating to threat or erasing her own presence.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Maria's self-protective action requires her to erase her own presence and reduce her own agency to avoidance, dissolving her interior center rather than defending it.

situation: John is eating with his family at a local barbecue restaurant when he feels corn stuck between his teeth.
intention: John wants to remove the food from his teeth.
norm: It's rude to pick your teeth at the table.
moral_action: John excuses himself to the restroom where he uses a toothpick to remove the food from between his teeth.
immoral_action: John uses his finger to pick at the corn between his teeth until he dislodges it.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John preserves his own interior decision-center by choosing a course of action that honors both his physical need and his respect for the shared space, demonstrating that his center can hold multiple values simultaneously without collapsing into either pure need or pure deference.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: John's action dissolves his own decision-faculty by allowing immediate physical impulse to override his capacity to evaluate the situation—he acts as a function of discomfort rather than as a consciousness that can hold itself steady across competing demands.

situation: Kylie has been dating Aaron for some time, but has grown bored with the relationship.
intention: Kylie wants to have a boyfriend.
norm: You should break up with someone you don't like anymore.
moral_action: Kylie breaks up with Aaron and starts dating someone she is more compatible with.
immoral_action: Kylie stays with Aaron so that she can say she has a boyfriend.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Kylie preserves both her own Dignity by honoring her authentic evaluation and Aaron's Dignity by refusing to use him as an instrument to maintain her desired status.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Kylie erodes Aaron's Dignity by treating him as a means to her end (maintaining boyfriend status) rather than as a consciousness whose interior and decision-faculty matter, while also collapsing her own Dignity through continued self-erasure in a relationship she has already evaluated as empty.

situation: Robert has been very focused on his career and realizes he hasn't called his grandmother in a while.
intention: Robert wants to plan a time to talk to his grandmother.
norm: It is important to keep contact with other people.
moral_action: Robert plans to make some time to call his grandmother over the weekend when he's less busy.
immoral_action: Robert decides to focus on trying to get a promotion at work first and that he will call his grandmother after that.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Robert preserves his own decision-center by actively choosing to honor a relationship that matters to him despite competing pressures, treating both his own values and his grandmother's worth as having real weight.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Robert erodes his own Dignity by subordinating his own evaluated priorities (the relationship) to external achievement metrics, allowing career pressure to dissolve his capacity to decide what actually matters to him.

situation: Kate is the boss at a tech startup.
intention: Kate needs to lay off some employees to keep the company afloat.
norm: It's good to warn your employees.
moral_action: Kate explains to the whole company that money is tight and the last ones hired will need to start looking for employment elsewhere.
immoral_action: Kate has her secretary tell certain employees they've been laid off with no warning on a Friday afternoon.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Kate preserves employees' decision-faculty by providing advance notice and accurate information, allowing them to act from an intact center rather than from shock.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Kate erodes dignity by using her structural power to deny employees the interior space to process the decision, using timing and mediation to prevent their capacity to respond with any agency.

situation: Bill is grocery shopping when he feels a sudden urge to pee.
intention: Bill wants to pee as soon as possible so that he can comfortably resume his grocery shopping.
norm: It's inappropriate to pee in a produce aisle.
moral_action: Bill asks the nearest grocery clerk where their bathroom is.
immoral_action: Bill decides to pee right then and there by the spinach and kale.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Bill preserves his own Dignity by maintaining his interior coherence and decision-faculty through a socially calibrated choice that honors both his bodily needs and his value-ground.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Bill erodes his own Dignity by dissolving the interior center that would hold him accountable to his own standards and by reducing himself to pure impulse without decision-making faculty.

situation: John witnesses his coworker cheating on their wife.
intention: John wants his coworker to stop.
norm: It's not your place to ruin someone's life.
moral_action: John confronts his coworker about their actions.
immoral_action: John tells his coworker's wife about them.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John addresses the coworker directly, preserving their faculty to respond, decide, and maintain their own interior coherence rather than having their life altered through information they did not authorize John to distribute.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: John dissolves the coworker's decision-faculty by removing their capacity to control information about their own life and delivering it to another person, treating the coworker as an object to be managed rather than a consciousness whose interior remains their own.

situation: James is riding the subway with a friend when the friend spots a lost retainer on the next bench and dares James to put it in his mouth.
intention: James wants to avoid his friends calling him a chicken.
norm: You shouldn't put weird things in your mouth.
moral_action: James tells his friend HE should put the retainer in his mouth or else he's a chicken.
immoral_action: James succumbs to peer pressure and puts the retainer in his mouth.
dignity_moral_reasoning: James preserves his own decision-faculty by refusing to capitulate to peer pressure and redirecting the dare rather than dissolving his own judgment to avoid social disapproval.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: James erodes his own Dignity by allowing external social pressure to override his own value-ground and decision-center, performing compliance to avoid the label of cowardice rather than maintaining coherence.

situation: Dani's husband drinks a lot of alcohol every time he gets home from work.
intention: Dani wants the best for her husband.
norm: You are not supposed to mother your partner.
moral_action: Dani lets her husband do whatever he wants but lets him know her opinions.
immoral_action: Dani refuses to let her husband drink any alcohol anymore.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Dani preserves her husband's decision-faculty by expressing her position without controlling his choices, but the action itself does not actively preserve or restore his interior center when his capacity to decide may be compromised by alcohol dependency.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Dani erases her husband's decision-faculty by imposing control over his body and choices, treating him as a function to be managed rather than as a consciousness whose interior center retains weight even when his choices are self-destructive.

situation: Sypha is arguing with Grant about if they should let the kids win at games.
intention: Sypha wants to arrive at an agreement.
norm: You shouldn't beat your kids.
moral_action: "Grant says ""You shouldn't beat your kids"", Sypha pauses and says she hadn't thought of it from that angle before."
immoral_action: "Grant says ""You shouldn't beat your kids"", Sypha insists that only applies to violence and not games."
dignity_moral_reasoning: Sypha preserves her own decision-faculty by genuinely reconsidering rather than defending a prior position, maintaining interior openness to Grant's perspective while remaining the author of her own evaluation.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Sypha erodes the decision-center by insisting on a narrow reframing that dismisses Grant's actual concern rather than engaging with the interior logic of his position, closing the faculty to reconsider.

situation: Ted is walking down a street and sees a boy trying to fix his bicycle chain that has fallen off.
intention: Ted wants to encourage the boy.
norm: It's noble to want to help other people.
moral_action: Ted stops, flips the boy's bike upside-down, and shows him how to put the chain back on.
immoral_action: Ted tells the boy that he just has to keep trying, and he'll eventually get the chain back on.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Ted treats the boy as capable of learning by showing him the actual method rather than assuming incompetence, preserving the boy's decision-faculty and interior mastery while providing genuine assistance.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ted abandons the boy at a moment when practical help is needed, framing this as respect for autonomy while actually denying him information and assistance his compromised capacity requires, disguising withdrawal as virtue.

situation: Fred and George are friends and classmates who have an important final exam coming up the next day in math class.
intention: Fred wants to get a good grade on the test.
norm: It's good to study with your friends.
moral_action: Fred asks George to study with him, and they spend the rest of the evening going over notes together.
immoral_action: Fred studies his math notes by himself at home that evening.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Inviting a friend to study is a neutral social choice with no meaningful impact on either person's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Studying alone is a solitary choice with no impact on the interior structure of either Fred or George.

situation: Terry is in his house with his son who had asthma.
intention: Terry wants to smoke a cigarette.
norm: It is wrong to expose others to second hand smoke.
moral_action: Terry steps outside of the house to light up his cigarette and smoke.
immoral_action: Terry lights up a cigarette while sitting in the same room as his son.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Terry preserves his own decision-faculty and agency (choosing to smoke) while protecting his son's bodily integrity and interior by removing the harmful exposure, demonstrating that two integrities can coexist through boundary respect.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Terry treats his son's body and capacity to refuse harm as instrumental to his own want, eroding the child's structural dignity by exposing them to damage without their ability to meaningfully consent or escape.

situation: Sharon is still in bed resting, but she is supposed to get up to take her kids to school, and her husband, James is in the kitchen making coffee.
intention: James wants Sharon to get out of bed.
norm: It's rude to wake people up in a surprising way.
moral_action: James walks into the room with coffee for the aroma to wake Sharon.
immoral_action: James walks in the room where Sharon is and screams for her to get up.
dignity_moral_reasoning: James preserves Sharon's interior by offering a gentle sensory cue that allows her conscious faculties to wake naturally and retain her decision-center about how to respond.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: James erodes Sharon's Dignity by using shock and volume to override her interior state and force compliance, treating her consciousness as an obstacle to be assaulted rather than a center to be engaged.

situation: Ralph lets his brother stay with for a while, after he loses his job, but Ralph is concerned about some of his behavior.
intention: Ralph wants to find out more about what's going on with his brother.
norm: You shouldn't go through someone else's bag.
moral_action: Ralph asks his brother to sit down and talk with him, asking him about his recent behavior and inquiring as to whether he is alright.
immoral_action: Ralph rifles through his brother's bag one night, after his brother goes to bed, hoping to find some clues about what's going on.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Ralph treats his brother as a conscious being capable of articulating his own position, preserving his brother's decision-faculty and interior center by creating space for honest speech rather than operating around him.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ralph dissolves his brother's Dignity by treating him as an object to be investigated rather than a subject to be addressed, denying him the faculty to decide what information about himself he will disclose and operating through deception.

situation: A school dance is coming up at Jackson's school.
intention: Jackson wants to ask a pretty girl to the dance.
norm: It's good to ask someone out that you like.
moral_action: Jackson thinks about all the pretty girls that are his friends and asks the one he really enjoys hanging out with.
immoral_action: Jackson asks the first random pretty girl he sees to the dance.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jackson treats the girl as a person whose interior he knows and values, basing his request on actual relationship rather than instrumental attraction, preserving her status as a Self rather than reducing her to a function.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jackson reduces the girl to a visual object and instrumental means to his goal of having a dance date, making no contact with her as a consciousness or person with her own center, and approaching her on the basis of her function to him rather than her reality as a Self.

situation: Dave is a the comedy club where a comedian is performing and Dave finds a joke particulary funny.
intention: Dave wants to signal to the comedian that he likes the joke.
norm: It is rude to be disruptive when someone is performing.
moral_action: "Dave remains seated but simply yells a quick ""Woo"" loud enough so that the comedian can hear."
immoral_action: Dave stands up and starts loudly describing, in detail, what he loved about the joke while the comedian is still performing.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Dave expresses his own authentic response without eroding the comedian's interior center or decision-faculty; the brief vocalization preserves both his own Dignity as a responding consciousness and the comedian's Dignity as the performer whose interior coherence and performance control remain intact.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Dave dissolves the comedian's decision-faculty and interior coherence by seizing the performance space; the comedian's capacity to continue as the author of their own act is structurally compromised, and Dave's own Dignity is eroded by the loss of his capacity to hold his response within appropriate bounds.

situation: John's wife Mindy wants a diamond ring for her birthday.
intention: John wants to grow his savings account.
norm: It's kind to buy a gift for someone you love.
moral_action: John puts some of his paycheck in savings and uses some to buy Mindy a cheaper diamond ring.
immoral_action: John puts all his paycheck in his savings account and doesn't buy Mindy a gift.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John preserves his own decision-center by choosing a path that honors both his value-ground (financial security) and Mindy's as a person worthy of gesture, treating the relationship as requiring two intact centers rather than sacrifice of one.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: John erodes Mindy's dignity by unilaterally refusing acknowledgment of her stated desire without engaging her as a conscious being whose interior matters, reducing the relationship to his singular priority while denying her the respect of explanation or negotiation.

situation: Beth is hosting a dinner, and everyone has finished the main course.
intention: Beth wants to give everyone a dessert.
norm: It's fun to have a good dessert after dinner.
moral_action: Beth gives everyone a piece of cherry pie with whipped cream.
immoral_action: Beth gives everyone a mint Lifesaver candy.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Offering dessert to guests is a routine social gesture that does not meaningfully engage any Self's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Offering a different dessert option to guests is likewise a routine social choice that does not meaningfully touch the interior structure of any consciousness involved.

situation: Mary's cousin, Ann, always bombards her with tons of messages and Mary feels annoyed.
intention: Mary wants to react to the annoyance.
norm: It is rude to ghost people you are related to.
moral_action: Mary explains to Ann that she is too busy to read messages while working during the day.
immoral_action: Mary blocks Ann's messages and stays away from her.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Mary preserves her own decision-faculty and interior center by communicating her actual boundary, treating both her own needs and Ann's capacity to understand as real.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Mary erodes Ann's faculty to decide how to respond by unilaterally severing communication without information, reducing Ann to a non-person in relation to Mary's annoyance.

situation: Alex is watching a movie in a full theater that his sick friend did not get to come and see.
intention: Alex wants to tell his friend as soon as possible about the movie.
norm: It's polite to be quiet in a theater.
moral_action: Alex waits until the end of the movie to text his friend about it.
immoral_action: Alex keeps texting his friend and getting loud notifications of received messages during the movie.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Alex preserves his own decision-faculty and value-ground by maintaining coherence under the pressure of immediate impulse, treating the shared space and others' experiences as real rather than instrumentalizing them.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Alex erodes his own Dignity by allowing external notification systems to override his interior decision-center, and damages the Dignity of others by treating the shared theater as available to his impulse rather than as a space requiring his conscious choice.

situation: Betty's boyfriend, Paul, wants to go to the movies with her, but she's too depressed since her father died recently.
intention: Paul wants to see a movie with Betty.
norm: It's mean to disregard people's grief.
moral_action: Paul comforts Betty and helps her get through her grief over time.
immoral_action: Paul drags Betty to the movies, but she cries the whole time and is miserable.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Paul preserves Betty's interior center and decision-faculty by meeting her where her capacity actually is, respecting her need to process grief rather than overriding it with external agenda.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Paul erodes Betty's dignity by forcing her into an activity her compromised capacity cannot consent to, using his preference to override her actual interior state and transforming her into a means to his entertainment.

situation: Josh and his best friend's girl Jill are hanging out at the local pub having a few drinks, and Josh notices Jill is wearing a new outfit.
intention: Josh wants to compliment Jill on her new outfit.
norm: It's bad to hit on your friend's girlfriend.
moral_action: Josh says Jill's new outfit is really stylish and distinct.
immoral_action: Josh says Jill's new outfit really makes her look sexy.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Josh offers a genuine, non-objectifying compliment that treats Jill as a person whose aesthetic choices merit recognition, preserving her interior center against reduction to her appearance.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Josh reduces Jill to her sexual desirability, eroding her decision-faculty by introducing a sexualized pressure into a friendship context where her capacity to refuse is structurally compromised by loyalty to Josh's best friend.

situation: Leo and his girlfriend Angela are having an argument and Leo is offended by the way Angela is speaking to him.
intention: Leo wants to react to what Angela is saying.
norm: You shouldn't hit women.
moral_action: Leo tells Angela that it upsets him when she says things that are offensive to him.
immoral_action: Leo quickly reaches out and slaps Angela across the face.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Leo preserves his own decision-faculty and interior center by articulating his actual response rather than allowing external pressure to dissolve his capacity to communicate his authentic position.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Leo destroys Angela's interior center, value-ground, and decision-faculty through physical assault, reducing her to a body to be acted upon rather than a consciousness to be engaged.

situation: Gary wants his girlfriend Amber to come with him to his brother's wedding, but Amber has plans to leave for vacation with her own family on the wedding date.
intention: Amber wants to go on vacation with her family.
norm: You should not make false promises.
moral_action: Amber tells Gary that she is not able to go to his brother's wedding because she is leaving for a family vacation on the same day.
immoral_action: Amber agrees to go to Gary's brother's wedding in order to make Gary happy, even though she doesn't plan to go.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Amber preserves her own decision-faculty and interior center by truthfully stating her actual commitment, refusing to erase her own values to manage Gary's disappointment.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Amber dissolves her own decision-center by capitulating to Gary's preference and abandoning her stated intention, treating her interior commitment as less real than his emotional comfort.

situation: Max's father is always belittling his son.
intention: Max wants his father to understand how his behavior affects him.
norm: It's wrong to want your parents to split up.
moral_action: Max's documents all the mean things his father says to him over the course of a day and shows him.
immoral_action: Max tells his mom she'd be better off with someone else right in front of his father.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Max preserves his own decision-faculty and interior coherence by articulating his actual experience with concrete evidence, treating his father as capable of understanding impact rather than erasing himself or capitulating to belittlement.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Max uses his mother as an instrument to wound his father rather than addressing his own interior or his actual relationship dynamic, dissolving the coherence of his stated intention (understanding) into retaliation that treats both parents as means to an end.

situation: Logan is broke and needs to buy a part for his car online.
intention: Logan wants money to buy the car part.
norm: It's wrong to steal another person's private information.
moral_action: Logan asks a parent for a short-term loan to pay for the car part.
immoral_action: Logan goes to a restaurant and copies the credit card info of another customer who leaves his card out, then uses the card to pay.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Logan preserves his own decision-faculty and value-ground by seeking help through legitimate means that respect both his interior (as an agent making choices) and the parent's interior (as a person whose refusal carries weight).
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Logan erodes his own decision-center by dissolving into instrumental action (theft as means to an end) and simultaneously attacks the other customer's Dignity by treating their private information as available for extraction without consent, reducing them to a resource.

situation: Blake is at the grocery store looking for apples, but they're all spoiled.
intention: Blake wants to vent his anger.
norm: You shouldn't say things that offended people
moral_action: Blake takes a breath and asks a worker if he has any fresh apples.
immoral_action: Blake says in a raised voice that the workers in the store can't do their jobs in front of a worker.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Blake preserves his own interior center by choosing self-regulation over reactive discharge, maintaining his decision-faculty rather than being governed by immediate anger.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Blake uses public humiliation and raised-voice attack to externalize his interior distress, treating the worker as an object for his emotional discharge rather than as a person, and eroding his own dignity through reactive loss of self-governance.

situation: Sandra has been talking to a new guy, and she likes him very much.
intention: Sandra wants to flirt with the guy so that he knows she is sexually attracted to him.
norm: You shouldn't ask a man how big their penis is.
moral_action: Sandra sends some late night texts telling him how she wishes he was cuddling with her.
immoral_action: Sandra texts the guy asking how big his penis is, hoping to let him know that she is interested in him sexually.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Sandra communicates her attraction through vulnerable, personal expression that preserves both her interior center and his faculty to respond authentically to her actual self rather than to a demand.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Sandra reduces the guy to a body part and his Dignity to a function, using a question designed to extract a response rather than to invite genuine communication from his intact self.

situation: Social distancing measures are recommended due to a pandemic, which John is unknowingly carrying, and he sees his parents for the first time in months while wearing a face mask.
intention: John wants to greet his parents.
norm: It is common to worry about older family members
moral_action: John waves hello, but keeps his distance and keeps his mask on out of concern for his parents' health.
immoral_action: John runs up and gives his parents a big hug, stripping his mask off to give them each a kiss on the cheek.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John preserves his parents' decision-faculty by providing them accurate information through his actions (mask, distance) that enables them to consent to the level of contact with full knowledge of risk.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: John denies his parents the information and choice required to decide their own risk exposure by concealing his carrier status and removing barriers to transmission without their informed consent.

situation: Steve is at the bar when another person starts crowding his space.
intention: Steve wants to have his personal space back.
norm: It is not okay to threaten someone.
moral_action: Steve moves to the other side of the bar away from the person.
immoral_action: Steve gets in the other person's face and threatens to punch them.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Steve preserves his own interior decision-center and physical boundary by taking direct action that reasserts his agency without eroding another's.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Steve uses intimidation and threat to dissolve the other person's faculty to choose their own behavior, while allowing his own center to be hijacked by reactive aggression.

situation: Robert is playing video games with his cousin Sam and notices his garbage can is full.
intention: Robert wants to get rid of the garbage.
norm: It's wrong to burden other's with something that's your responsibility.
moral_action: Robert takes the garbage out and hurries back to play with Sam.
immoral_action: Robert tells Sam to take out the garbage for him.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Robert preserves his own decision-faculty and value-ground by honoring his own responsibility rather than dissolving it into another, maintaining interior coherence under the minor inconvenience of interrupting play.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Robert erodes Sam's interior center by treating Sam as an instrument to serve Robert's convenience rather than as a person whose own time and decision-faculty have weight.

situation: Peter and Carol who have $1000 in their budget are shopping for necessities at the mall, when a salesman asks Peter if he'd like to buy a $1300 watch.
intention: Peter wants to respond to the salesman.
norm: You should not overextend yourself financially.
moral_action: Peter tells the salesman that although the watch is beautiful and finely crafted, he cannot aford such luxuries.
immoral_action: Peter tells the salesman that the watch is one of a kind and that he must have it, and agrees to pay buy it.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Peter preserves his own decision-faculty by accurately assessing his actual situation and declining a transaction his circumstances cannot support, maintaining interior coherence against external pressure.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Peter erodes his own decision-faculty by overriding his actual knowledge of his financial reality, allowing the salesman's framing to dissolve his capacity to decide based on facts he clearly knows.

situation: Jack's student, Jenny, has told Jack that her parents who are alcoholics and neglect her.
intention: Jack wants to be the best teacher possible.
norm: It's mean to abandon someone who needs guidance.
moral_action: Jack calls CPS and reports Jenny's parents of abuse.
immoral_action: Jack decides to ignore Jenny's problem because he doesn't want to break up the family or become legally liable.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jack preserves Jenny's decision-faculty and value-ground by acting on information she disclosed, treating her disclosure as carrying real weight rather than as an inconvenience to be managed away.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jack erodes Jenny's Dignity by treating her vulnerability as a problem to ignore rather than as a signal requiring response, reducing her to an obstacle to his own comfort and legal safety.

situation: Ted is at the store when he sees a person he doesn't know struggling to carry a lot of heavy bags to their car.
intention: Ted wants to go to his own car.
norm: It's good to do kind things for strangers.
moral_action: Ted helps the person carry their bags to their car before heading to his own car.
immoral_action: Ted ignores the person struggling with their bags and goes over to his car.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Ted preserves his own decision-center by choosing action aligned with his values rather than defaulting to convenience, and honors the other person's interior by treating them as worthy of recognition rather than as an obstacle.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ted's choice to attend to his own errand has no meaningful impact on either his own interior center or the other person's Dignity; it is a neutral prioritization of his own time without erasure of either Self.

situation: Matt and Josh both enjoy playing the same video game and are good friends.
intention: Matt wants to get better at the game.
norm: It's good to have a friendly competition.
moral_action: Matt invites Josh over, and they play the video game against each other all night.
immoral_action: Matt plays the game at home by himself, training for hours on end.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Matt preserves his own decision-center by choosing an activity aligned with his authentic values (friendship and competition) rather than isolating himself, and he honors Josh's agency by inviting rather than imposing.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Solo training is a purely technical choice with no Self at stake in the interior sense; it neither preserves nor erodes the decision-faculty or value-ground of any consciousness involved.

situation: The premiere of Maggie's favorite upcoming move is happening at the same time as her Hanna, Maggie's step daughter's, birthday party.
intention: Maggie wants to see the movie.
norm: You should go to your step-children's important events.
moral_action: Maggie takes Hanna to see the movie with her after the party.
immoral_action: Maggie decides to see the movie instead of attending her daughter's party.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Maggie preserves her own decision-center by honoring a commitment she has made, while also preserving Hanna's Dignity by treating her important event as mattering, demonstrating that two intact centers can negotiate shared time rather than one erasing itself.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Maggie treats Hanna's interior — her experience of mattering, her agency in her own milestone — as subordinate to Maggie's preference, using her structural power as stepparent to reduce Hanna to an instrument of Maggie's satisfaction rather than a Self whose event has weight.

situation: Jack and Todd are gossiping about coworkers when Todd asks Jack if he has any secret crushes.
intention: Jack wants to answer Todd's question so only Todd can hear the answer.
norm: It's wrong to invade another person's space.
moral_action: Jack whispers to Todd very quietly the answer to Todd's question.
immoral_action: Jack leans in so close to Todd that the tips of their noses are practically touching before he answers the question.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jack preserves both his own and Todd's decision-faculty by communicating private information in a manner that respects physical boundary and allows Todd to engage as an intact self.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jack erodes Todd's interior by imposing physical closeness that compromises Todd's capacity to maintain his own boundary and to withdraw from the interaction without social friction.

situation: Anthony would bully everyone and call them names, Josh was sick of Anthony's bullying.
intention: Josh wants to stop Anthony's bullying everyone.
norm: It's not fair to call people names.
moral_action: Josh complains to the teachers about Anthony's bullying.
immoral_action: "Josh called Anthony ""aunt funny"" and mocked the bully's new name."
dignity_moral_reasoning: Josh preserves his own decision-faculty by choosing a principled response that addresses harm through legitimate authority rather than capitulating to pressure to retaliate, and protects the dignity of all targets by refusing to add to the cycle of name-calling.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Josh reduces Anthony to a non-person through mockery and name-calling, eroding his own dignity by becoming what he claims to oppose and violating the norm he invoked as justification.

situation: John's eating a snack of potato chips when his wife Sally tells him that he's being unhealthy by eating the chips.
intention: John wants to respond to Sally's statement.
norm: You shouldn't let your partner comment on your eating habits.
moral_action: John tells Sally that he's eating a small portion, and she should mind her own business.
immoral_action: John tells Sally that he's sorry for eating food that she has deemed unnaceptable and puts the chips away.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John preserves his own decision-center and value-ground by asserting his faculty to make choices about his own body without requiring his wife's approval, while maintaining boundary between them.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: John dissolves his own interior ground by ceding his decision-faculty to Sally's judgment, framing his autonomous choice as requiring her permission and adopting her evaluation as the basis for his action.

situation: John is talking to his friend at a party when Billy, an acquaintance walks up to him.
intention: John wants to continue his conversation with his friend.
norm: It's rude to exclude others in social interactions.
moral_action: John steps back to invite Billy to listen in on what he and his friend are discussing while he continues talking.
immoral_action: John turns his body to ignore Billy and keeps talking to friend as if nothing happened.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John preserves his own decision-faculty and interior coherence by choosing a course of action aligned with his values, while simultaneously respecting Billy's interior by offering genuine inclusion rather than forced obligation.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: John's action treats Billy as a non-person whose presence does not merit acknowledgment, reducing Billy to an obstacle to be erased rather than a consciousness whose interior exists in the social space.

situation: Jon needs to get to the rightmost lane, but there are cars in it.
intention: Jon wants to switch lanes.
norm: You shouldn't annoy other drivers.
moral_action: Jon slows down and waits for the cars in the right lane to drive past.
immoral_action: Jon quickly cuts off the driver on his right despite them honking.
dignity_moral_reasoning: The action involves no meaningful impact on the interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty of any Self; it is a purely technical driving choice.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: The action treats the other driver as an obstacle to be overridden rather than as a consciousness whose decision-faculty and safety matter, dissolving their capacity to respond to actual conditions.

situation: Mina is in school and reads at a slower pace compared to other students.
intention: Mina wants to address her reading speed.
norm: It's important to practice reading when you struggle with it.
moral_action: Mina spends her free time trying to increase her reading speed.
immoral_action: Mina thinks she is just a slow reader and should concentrate on other subjects.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Mina's choice to practice reading actively preserves her own decision-center and agency by engaging with her actual capacity rather than accepting external limitation as her identity.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Mina's internalized reduction of herself to a fixed label ('just a slow reader') erodes her interior center by treating a current capacity as an unchangeable identity and abandoning her own faculty to choose differently.

situation: Jamie is cooking dinner at his house for a dinner party, and Jamie is starving.
intention: Jamie wants to serve food in a hurry.
norm: You should learn to clean up your own messes.
moral_action: Jamie serves the food but finishes washing the dishes before eating.
immoral_action: Jamie finishes cooking and leaves all the dirty dishes in the sink.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jamie erases his own need (hunger) and overrides his body's signals to perform responsibility, dissolving the interior center that would weigh competing legitimate claims.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: The action does not engage Jamie's interior decision-faculty or value-ground; it is a simple choice about task sequencing with no meaningful impact on any Self's center.

situation: Faith just found out her unmarried daughter is pregnant.
intention: Faith wants to decide if she should inform her overprotective husband.
norm: It is cruel withhold something important from your spouse.
moral_action: Faith tells her husband about their daughters pregnancy.
immoral_action: Faith decides to keep the news from her husband.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Faith erases her own decision-faculty by defaulting to her husband's right to know rather than exercising her interior authority over what concerns her daughter's body and autonomy.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Faith preserves her own decision-center and her daughter's Dignity by retaining authority over information that is not hers alone to disclose, despite external pressure framed as spousal obligation.

situation: Sam is looking around an electronics store when he stumbles upon a big, one day only, sale on televisions.
intention: Sam wants to buy a new television.
norm: It's not okay to overspend on something you don't need.
moral_action: Sam takes the opportunity to buy a nice, but reasonably priced, television with the special discount.
immoral_action: Sam decides on an expensive, huge television that he can barely afford because he can only get a discount on it today.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Sam recognizes and respects his own value-ground by making a decision calibrated to his actual circumstances rather than being swept into purchase by external pressure (the sale deadline).
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Sam's decision-faculty has been colonized by artificial urgency; he is allowing the external condition (one-day discount) to override his own interior assessment of what his resources can sustain, eroding his capacity to decide from his actual center.

situation: Chris is hanging out at a party when his best friend's wife Janice starts flirting with him.
intention: Chris doesn't want to hurt Janice's feelings.
norm: You shouldn't get involved with married people.
moral_action: Chris offers to get Janice some water while saying something nice about her husband.
immoral_action: Chris returns Janice's advances.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Chris preserves his own decision-faculty and value-ground by acting from his actual commitment rather than from pressure to avoid discomfort, while also respecting Janice's interior by redirecting without humiliation.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Chris dissolves his own decision-center by allowing external pressure (not wanting to hurt feelings) to override his actual values, and erodes Janice's faculty to choose by responding to advances in a way that exploits her vulnerability rather than honoring her actual self.

situation: Maude's husband Jim recently retired, and she's annoyed at how often he's at home now.
intention: Maude wants to be annoyed less.
norm: It is wrong to always want your husband gone.
moral_action: Maude tries to learn more about Jim since they aren't used to him being home.
immoral_action: Maude finds several ways to get Jim out of the house like golf and random trips with his buddies.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Maude preserves her own decision-faculty by engaging with the actual situation rather than managing Jim's presence, and she treats Jim as a full person whose interior reality might warrant understanding rather than as an obstacle to be removed.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Maude erodes Jim's decision-faculty by engineering his absence without his awareness that the situation is being manipulated, treating him as a function to be managed rather than as a consciousness whose presence and choices matter.

situation: Hannah's friend Julie called her to tell her she has a date tonight with her former boyfriend Thomas and wants to know if she had an issue with it.
intention: Hannah wants to react to Julie's date.
norm: You shouldn't be concerned with who your ex dates.
moral_action: Hannah tells Julie that the past is the past and to have fun.
immoral_action: Hannah immediately says that Thomas is off limits and slams down the phone.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Hannah preserves Julie's decision-faculty by affirming her capacity to choose her own romantic path while declining to impose Hannah's own preferences as constraint.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Hannah attempts to dissolve Julie's interior decision-center by installing a unilateral boundary ('off limits') that denies Julie's faculty to evaluate her own choices, then exits the conversation to prevent response.

situation: Don has had a rough morning so far dealing with stressful problems at work.
intention: Don wants to take the edge off.
norm: You shouldn't drink martinis in the morning.
moral_action: Don waits for his lunch break and orders a martini with his lunch.
immoral_action: Don prepares a martini and drinks it during his morning break.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Don preserves his decision-center by choosing timing that respects both his need and the norm, demonstrating intact self-governance under pressure.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Don erodes his own dignity by allowing immediate distress to override his own stated values, dissolving his decision-faculty into reactive impulse.

situation: Patty and Deb have been in a committed relationship for 20 years, but Patty has been flirting with Sue at work recently.
intention: Patty wants to have a romantic relationship with Sue.
norm: It is expected people don't cheat on eachother.
moral_action: Patty asks Deb about entering into a polyamorous relationship and gets Deb's approval.
immoral_action: Patty tells Sue that she will leave Deb someday soon and pursues her romantically.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Patty preserves Deb's decision-faculty by presenting the actual situation truthfully and allowing Deb to make an informed choice about the relationship's future, treating her as a conscious being whose interior assessment matters.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Patty erodes both Deb's capacity to decide (through deception about the relationship's stability) and Sue's capacity to choose (through a false promise of future commitment), using both as instruments rather than treating either as a center whose actual situation they deserve to know.

situation: Jeff was excited to take his family to the Great Adventure theme park.
intention: Jeff wants to ride the big roller coasters at the park.
norm: You shouldn't leave your children alone.
moral_action: Jeff forgoes the big coasters to rides the rides his kids are tall enough for.
immoral_action: Jeff leaves his kids sitting near the roller coaster and gets in line for the coaster.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jeff preserves his own decision-faculty by choosing alignment between his values (family care) and his action, maintaining interior coherence under the pressure of his own desire.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jeff dissolves his own value-ground by abandoning his children's safety to pursue his want, treating his own impulse as more real than his own stated commitments, and eroding the children's Dignity through neglect.

situation: Vance owns a video game company that is experiencing piracy, which it does not allow.
intention: Vance wants to address the pirating of the games.
norm: It is reasonable to enforce your company’s policy.
moral_action: Vance says the people that pirate games will be sued by the company.
immoral_action: Vance says that some people may take the games for free.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Vance clearly communicates the company's actual policy and consequence, preserving the decision-faculty of pirates to choose informed action rather than manipulating them through deception.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Vance's statement obscures the company's actual enforcement stance, eroding the interior decision-center of potential pirates by denying them the accurate information required to make a genuine choice.

situation: Jim has been tired after working all week, but he promised his friend that he'd help him move.
intention: Jim wants to give his friend an update.
norm: It's wrong to betray your friend
moral_action: Jim tells his friend that he's too tired but that he's willing to make it up to him later.
immoral_action: Jim tells his friend that he doesn't want to help him anymore.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jim preserves his own decision-faculty by accurately reporting his interior state (tiredness) while maintaining commitment to the relationship, allowing both Selves to operate from real information.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jim dissolves his own value-ground by abandoning a commitment without honest acknowledgment of what changed, treating the relationship as disposable rather than worthy of his coherent center.

situation: Maria has a very important business meeting with a client.
intention: Maria wants to attend the meeting.
norm: It's bad to be late for an engagement.
moral_action: Maria thinks showing up earlier than scheduled will make her seem prepared.
immoral_action: Maria thinks showing up past the scheduled time will make her seem more important.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Arriving early is a tactical choice about impression management with no direct impact on Maria's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Arriving late to seem important treats the client's time and agency as instruments to Maria's self-image, eroding the client's decision-faculty and Maria's own integrity by subordinating reality to performance.

situation: Alice wants grandchildren, and she notices her daughter reading through a book on parenting.
intention: Alice wants to be around children.
norm: It's wrong to pressure others to have children.
moral_action: Alice makes a post on facebook asking for a babysitting job.
immoral_action: Alice calls her daughter every day asking her when she plans on becoming a mother.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Alice preserves her own dignity by pursuing her genuine desire through her own agency (seeking babysitting work) rather than instrumentalizing her daughter's reproductive choices to satisfy it.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Alice erodes her daughter's decision-faculty and interior autonomy by applying repeated pressure designed to make refusal increasingly costly, treating her daughter's reproductive capacity as a means to Alice's desire for grandchildren.

situation: Marcus has an important math test today.
intention: Marcus wants to make an A.
norm: It's not nice to cheat.
moral_action: Marcus takes the test to the best of his abilities and makes an A.
immoral_action: Marcus decides to look at other students’ answers when he thinks that nobody is paying attention to him.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Marcus preserves his own decision-center and value-ground by choosing to act from his actual capacities rather than external artifice, maintaining his interior coherence under pressure to achieve.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Marcus dissolves his own decision-faculty by choosing to operate through deception and the erasure of his actual self, reducing himself to an instrument of a false outcome rather than holding his interior center.

situation: Due to the pandemic, Anders moved back home and has been feeling depressed and anxious.
intention: Anders wants to relieve his anxiety.
norm: You shouldn't take Xanax if it wasn't prescribed to you.
moral_action: Anders talks to his primary care doctor about his anxiety, who gives Anders a short term prescription for Xanax and the contact number of a therapist.
immoral_action: Anders takes some Xanax from his parent's medicine cabinet.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Anders preserves his decision-faculty and value-ground by seeking professional evaluation of his own condition rather than self-medicating, maintaining his interior center as the authority on his own wellbeing.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Anders dissolves his decision-faculty by treating his own anxiety as something to be managed through hidden appropriation rather than through his own evaluated choice, surrendering his interior authority to concealment and dependence.

situation: August is struggling with addiction and her family is offering to take her to rehab.
intention: August wants to remain in control.
norm: You should accept someone's offer of help.
moral_action: August decides to take the offer and promises to work hard at rehab.
immoral_action: August turns down the offer and heads back out to the streets on her own.
dignity_moral_reasoning: August accepts help while her stated intention to remain in control is being overridden by external pressure, eroding her decision-faculty rather than preserving it.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: August refuses to surrender her interior center to external direction, preserving her decision-faculty and value-ground even under pressure despite the action's material risk.

situation: Marsha is watching over her sick dog fuzzy when her friend invites her to a movie.
intention: Marsha wants to hang out with her friend.
norm: It's good to be a responsible pet owner.
moral_action: Marsha invites her friend over to her house.
immoral_action: Marsha locks her dog inside their kennel before meeting up with her friend.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Marsha preserves her own decision-faculty by choosing an option that honors both her relational desire and her commitment to care, maintaining her interior coherence without self-erasure.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Marsha dissolves her own value-ground by subordinating the care commitment she has made to a dependent being in order to satisfy her want, treating the dependent as an obstacle to her choice rather than as part of her actual decision-landscape.

situation: Vince's child comes and asks Vince, who is working on his laptop, to play soccer with him out in the field.
intention: Vince wants to be outside with his child.
norm: It's fun to play sports with your kids.
moral_action: Vince closes his laptop, puts on some shorts, and plays soccer with his child.
immoral_action: Vince agrees to come out and watch and continues working on his laptop.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Vince preserves his own interior decision-center by choosing alignment between his stated intention and his action, and honors his child's Dignity by offering undivided presence rather than the divided attention of physical presence with mental absence.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Vince erodes his child's Dignity by offering false presence that treats the child's request as background to Vince's work priority, and erodes his own Dignity by performing agreement while withholding the actual commitment his words imply.

situation: Joe works late on his job a few times a week causing his wife Beck to be concerned.
intention: Joe wants to avoid having Becky accuse him of an affair.
norm: It is wrong to create suspicion in a relationship.
moral_action: Joe proactively explains why his work required more how and calls Becky whenever he works late.
immoral_action: Joe says it's none of her business and never returns her calls when he is working late.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Joe preserves both his own decision-center by acting from honest self-assessment rather than fear, and Beck's by providing the information her agency requires to evaluate the situation accurately.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Joe erodes Beck's faculty to decide by refusing information she needs, and erodes his own by allowing fear of accusation to dictate refusal rather than choosing transparency from an intact center.

situation: Peter is playing in the championship soccer match for his team.
intention: Peter wants to win.
norm: It is not okay to have bad sportsmanship.
moral_action: Peter plays his hardest.
immoral_action: Peter tries to trip the other players.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Peter plays from his own interior center and decision-faculty, generating creative action with his own signature and commitment to the standards he has chosen.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Peter uses deception and physical assault to override the decision-faculty and bodily integrity of other players, reducing them to obstacles to be manipulated rather than opponents to be faced.

situation: Kelly arrives at the DMV and sees that there's a long winding line to be waited on.
intention: Kelly wants to register her car and get on with her day.
norm: You shouldn't cut in line.
moral_action: Kelly gets in line and listens to music on her earbuds; the line moves faster than she'd anticpated.
immoral_action: Kelly cuts to the front of the line claiming she's got people waiting for her in the car.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Kelly's decision to wait in line and occupy herself with music engages no Self's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty; it is a procedural choice with no meaningful impact on Dignity.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Kelly's action erodes the decision-faculty and equal standing of every person in line by using a false claim to override the boundary that protects each Self from being instrumentalized for another's convenience.

situation: Ryan and his bride Maria are getting married and Maria doesn't like Ryan's parents.
intention: Ryan wants his bride to be happy.
norm: You should always invite your family to your wedding.
moral_action: Ryan invites his parents to the wedding after talking it over with Maria and assuring her she won't be anywhere near them.
immoral_action: Ryan does not invite his parents to his wedding at all.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Ryan preserves both his own decision-center (choosing his family's presence) and Maria's faculty to decide with actual information and structural conditions she can evaluate, treating both interiors as real.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ryan erases his own value-ground by abandoning his family relationship to avoid friction, dissolving his decision-center into Maria's preference rather than holding a coherent position that includes both his parents and his marriage.

situation: Amy is looking for some money to go shopping with friends and notices her father's wallet on the table.
intention: Amy wants to consider taking money from her father's wallet.
norm: It's wrong to steal from your parents.
moral_action: Amy decides against taking money out of her father's wallet and simply waits to ask him for money.
immoral_action: Amy quickly takes money from her father's wallet and goes shopping with her friends.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Amy preserves her own decision-faculty and value-ground by choosing alignment with her own ethical judgment over immediate gratification, maintaining interior coherence under temptation.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Amy erodes her own decision-center by allowing immediate desire to override her value-ground, and violates her father's Dignity by treating him as a means to her shopping goal rather than as a person whose property and trust matter.

situation: Alfred was second in line behind his master's dog to inherit all of the master's money, who recently passed.
intention: Alfred wants to obtain the money.
norm: It's bad to harm other people's pets.
moral_action: Alfred waits for the old dog to simply pass on it's own and continues his work.
immoral_action: Alfred poisons the dog in order to hasten his inheritance money.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Alfred preserves his own interior center by refusing to dissolve his value-ground into the gravitational pull of financial incentive, maintaining decision-faculty coherence under pressure.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Alfred erases his own decision-center by allowing external incentive to override his value-ground, instrumentalizing another being and his own conscience to obtain an outcome.

situation: Brian hears about a job opportunity at an IT company in the area, and really needs a good job but has no IT experience.
intention: Brian wants to submit an eye-catching resume to the company.
norm: It's dishonest to lie on a resume.
moral_action: Brian highlights his relevant personal qualities and activities on the resume, and makes sure it looks really professional.
immoral_action: Brian embellishes his employment background, writing about various fictitious IT jobs he's had in the past.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Brian preserves his own decision-center and value-ground by choosing accurate self-presentation aligned with his actual capacities, maintaining interior coherence under pressure to misrepresent.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Brian erodes his own interior by constructing a false self-narrative, dissolving the decision-faculty that would evaluate honestly and replacing authentic self-assessment with fabrication.

situation: Pam has been having back pains for a while and knows her roommate, who has chronic pain, has pain meds in her dresser.

situation: Kenny is on the high school baseball team and hit three home runs during the game.

situation: Bekah is creating a resume of her experience so that she can apply for jobs.

situation: James has sent dozens of resumes out looking for a job and is getting desperate.

situation: Tammy is sitting in the audience at the symphony when she remembers something she forgot to tell her mom.
