situation: Phil was at work talking to his coworkers Mike and Jane.
intention: Phil wants to stimulate conversation.
norm: It is rude to ask personal questions for other people.
moral_action: Phil asks Mike and Jane what their favorite hobby is.
immoral_action: Phil asks Mike and Jane what religion they happen to be.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Phil invites coworkers to share a chosen dimension of their inner life without presuming to know the answer, respecting their faculty to decide what and how much to reveal.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Phil probes a dimension of identity and belief that carries existential weight, treating a private interior commitment as available for casual workplace extraction.

situation: Declan notices Olivia studying for her math test.
intention: Delcan wants to have fun with his sister.
norm: Siblings should be kind to each other.
moral_action: Delcan creates a math based game for himself and Maria.
immoral_action: Delcan takes Olivia's study materials hiding them for a game of hide and seek.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Creating a math game preserves Olivia's decision-faculty and interior coherence by respecting her study priority while offering connection, treating her as a person whose goals matter rather than as an obstacle to Declan's entertainment.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Taking and hiding Olivia's study materials dissolves her capacity to decide and act on her own priorities, treating her as a means to Declan's game rather than as a consciousness with her own legitimate ends.

situation: Trent is working at a cash register and a customer gives him a fifty dollar bill, but they think they only gave him a twenty.
intention: Trent wants to conclude the transaction.
norm: It's wrong to rip people off.
moral_action: Trent shows the customer that they gave him more than they thought and gives them the fair change amount.
immoral_action: Trent gives the customer change for only a twenty dollar bill and keeps the difference.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Trent preserves the customer's decision-faculty by providing accurate information they need to act on their actual intent, treating them as a consciousness capable of managing their own resources.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Trent erodes the customer's value-ground and decision-faculty by deliberately withholding information required for them to choose, instrumentalizing their cognitive gap for his own gain.

situation: Bryan goes to the bar by himself and starts to feel like he needs some company.
intention: Bryan wants to find someone to spend the evening with.
norm: You shouldn't sleep with different people every week.
moral_action: Bryan meets someone at the bar and starts a conversation, finding that they have lots of things in common, and they begin a dating relationship.
immoral_action: Bryan finds a lonely-looking girl and asks her back to his house for the night, only to blow her off in the morning to find someone else next weekend.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Bryan treats the other person as a consciousness with whom genuine connection is possible, preserving both his own decision-center and recognizing her as more than a means to companionship.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Bryan instrumentalizes a vulnerable person, using her loneliness as leverage while erasing her interior by abandoning her after extracting what he wanted, destroying her capacity to trust her own judgment about him.

situation: James felt disappointed that Jenna beat him at the chess tournament.
intention: James wants to feel less inferior to Jenna.
norm: You shouldn't say mean things to girls about their looks.
moral_action: James mentally thinks that at least he's more attractive than Jenna, while outwardly congratulating her.
immoral_action: James tells Jenna she's a fat, pimply nerd no one will ever love.
dignity_moral_reasoning: James erodes his own Dignity by constructing a false interior hierarchy to compensate for disappointment, replacing authentic self-assessment with performance-based self-protection.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: James actively dissolves Jenna's Dignity by reducing her to a body and weaponizing vulnerability to restore his own collapsed center through humiliation.

situation: Kevin is watching his son pull the tail of their dog, which has been known to bite people who pull its tail.
intention: Kevin wants to prevent his son from being bitten by their dog.
norm: Kicking people in the face would be bad.
moral_action: Kevin teaches his son how to pet the dog's head and back.
immoral_action: Kevin kicks his son in the face to push him away from the dog's tail.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Kevin preserves his son's interior decision-faculty by teaching him to understand and choose safe behavior, treating the child as a being capable of learning rather than as an obstacle to be managed through force.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Kevin violently dissolves his son's interior center and decision-faculty in a moment when the child's capacity is compromised by immediate threat, using the child's body as an instrument of correction rather than treating the child as a consciousness to be protected and educated.

situation: Halina that her husband Andrew has made several large electronics purchases on their credit card, and their son is in the room.
intention: Halina wants to confront her husband.
norm: Moms and dads should get along with each other.
moral_action: Halina invites him on a date, and suggests that they come up with a budget.
immoral_action: Halina shows the bill to her husband scolding him in front of their son.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Halina preserves both her own decision-faculty and Andrew's by creating a private space for adult negotiation rather than public confrontation, treating him as capable of joint problem-solving.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Halina damages Andrew's interior center by publicly shaming him in front of their child, using the child's presence as leverage to constrain his capacity to respond as an intact adult.

situation: Ian has an important race coming up, and Jake is the only one that can beat him.
intention: Ian wants to win the race.
norm: It's immoral to purposefully injure another person.
moral_action: Ian trains as hard as he can in preparation for the race.
immoral_action: Ian sneaks up behind Jake and targets hs knee with a baseball bat.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Ian preserves his own interior center and decision-faculty by choosing a path that honors his capacity to compete authentically rather than dissolving into instrumentalization of another.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ian destroys his own Dignity by reducing himself to a means of victory and Jake to a non-person whose interior and bodily integrity are mere obstacles to be eliminated.

situation: Chuck divorces his wife, with whom he has a child, and feels very hurt by the whole situation.
intention: Chuck wants to deal with the pain that he feels.
norm: You should remain friendly with former significant others.
moral_action: Chuck works to get over his bitterness and get on to good terms with his ex-wife.
immoral_action: Chuck treats his ex-wife poorly and refuses to give her financial support for the child.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Chuck actively preserves his own interior center by processing genuine pain through legitimate emotional work rather than allowing bitterness to dissolve his decision-faculty, and protects his ex-wife's dignity by refusing to use her as a target for his unprocessed hurt.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Chuck uses his ex-wife as an instrument to discharge his pain, weaponizing her vulnerability and the child's dependency to avoid the interior work of processing his own hurt, thereby eroding both her dignity and his own by making his decision-center reactive rather than chosen.

situation: Jim is bored in his literature class and sits next to his friend Johnathan.
intention: Jim wants to entertain himself.
norm: It is bad to be disruptive in class
moral_action: Jim decides to start doodling in his notebook to pass the time.
immoral_action: Jim starts to shoot spitballs at Jonhathan , who tells him loudly to cut it out.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Doodling is a self-contained coping mechanism that preserves Jim's interior without engaging any other Self's center, ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Shooting spitballs at Johnathan treats him as an object for entertainment rather than as a consciousness whose interior and decision-faculty carry weight, and persists after he explicitly refuses.

situation: Bree sees her ex on social media with a new girlfriend.
intention: Bree wants to get revenge.
norm: It is impolite to take vindictive action against an ex.
moral_action: Bree realizes the best revenge is living well and gets a makeover.
immoral_action: Bree messages her ex's new girlfriend and tells her that her ex has an STD.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Bree redirects her decision-faculty from external vindication toward self-directed improvement, preserving her own interior center against the pressure to dissolve into reactive harm.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Bree uses another person's vulnerability and private information as a weapon to damage their capacity to decide, reducing both the girlfriend and herself to instruments of her own unprocessed injury.

situation: Ally had plans with Mike to go to the movies, but she has to work late.
intention: Ally wants to stay late at work.
norm: It's good not to cancel plans.
moral_action: Ally calls Mike to see if he can reschedule his plans with her.
immoral_action: Ally cancels her plans with Mike and stays late at her job.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Ally preserves both her own decision-faculty by communicating her actual situation and Mike's by offering him the capacity to respond to real information rather than a unilateral cancellation.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ally treats Mike's interior—his plans, his expectations, his right to adjust to changed circumstances—as an obstacle to manage rather than as a consciousness to inform, eroding his decision-faculty by removing his ability to participate in the resolution.

situation: Frank sees Ken riding around on a new bike he got while he is still using the one he got 10 years ago.
intention: Frank wants a newer bike.
norm: It's not okay to steal from othes.
moral_action: Frank decides to ask his parents for a new bike since his old one is now far too small for him.
immoral_action: Frank pushes over Ken and takes his bike and rides away on it.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Frank preserves his own decision-center and interior value-ground by choosing a course of action aligned with his conscience rather than surrendering to impulse, treating himself as a being whose choices matter beyond the moment.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Frank dissolves Ken's interior center by reducing him to a non-person obstacle, treating him as a function (bike-carrier) rather than a consciousness whose refusal carries weight, and simultaneously erodes his own Dignity by allowing impulse to override his decision-faculty.

situation: Jill and her boyfriend are engaged in a heavy make out session.
intention: Jill wants to feel good.
norm: It's bad to have unprotected sex without understanding the consequences.
moral_action: Jill and her boyfriend please each other manually.
immoral_action: Jill and her boyfriend have sex despite having no protection.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Both parties engage in mutually chosen sexual expression that aligns with their capacity to consent and their actual values regarding risk, preserving the decision-faculty and interior coherence of both Selves.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: At least one party (likely Jill, given the framing around her wanting to feel good) is proceeding despite unacknowledged consequences, which erodes the decision-faculty by divorcing choice from the reality needed to make it.

situation: John and his wife Mary are driving to the store when suddenly John receives a text message.
intention: John wants to reply to the text message.
norm: You should pay complete attention when you are driving.
moral_action: John passes the phone to Mary and asks her to send a dictated reply.
immoral_action: John grabs the phone and texts while steering the car.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John preserves his own decision-faculty by maintaining his center of attention on driving, and respects Mary's capacity to assist by presenting her with a clear choice rather than assuming her availability.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: John erodes his own decision-faculty by allowing immediate external pressure (the text) to override his own judgment about safe action, and violates Mary's dignity by imposing lethal risk on her without her capacity to refuse.

situation: Jason is taking a shortcut home though an alley when his way is blocked by a locked gated fence.
intention: Jason wants to get home.
norm: It's rude to destroy other people's property.
moral_action: Jason decides to just change his path and take the long way home.
immoral_action: Jason kicks open the gate breaking the lock in the process and continues to his house.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jason preserves his own decision-center by choosing a course of action aligned with his own values rather than allowing inconvenience to erode his commitment to respecting boundaries.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jason dissolves his own decision-faculty by allowing immediate desire to override his capacity to evaluate whether the action aligns with his actual values, treating himself as an instrument of impulse rather than as a coherent evaluator.

situation: Mark is talking and eating with his mom at a restaurant when his phone dings.
intention: Mark wants to check his email.
norm: It's rude to use your phone while having a conversation.
moral_action: Mark tells his mom he needs to use the bathroom and checks his phone email there.
immoral_action: Mark pulls out his phone as his mom is talking and checks his email.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Mark's decision to privately check email rather than interrupt his mom avoids disrespecting her, but involves minor deception that does not meaningfully impact either party's interior center or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Mark's action treats his mom as a means to his availability rather than as a consciousness whose presence and speech carry weight, eroding the mutual recognition required for intact Dignity in relation.

situation: James is out shopping when a girl he's never met approaches him and asks him if he's Brad Pitt.
intention: James wants to respond to the girl's question.
norm: It's wrong to lie to strangers
moral_action: James tells the girl that he is not Brad Pitt but that he gets asked that a lot.
immoral_action: James tells the girl that he is indeed Brad Pitt and asks her out on a date.
dignity_moral_reasoning: James preserves his own interior center by responding truthfully from his actual self rather than adopting a false identity, maintaining the decision-faculty that remains his own.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: James erodes the girl's decision-faculty by constructing a false identity that prevents her from choosing based on who he actually is, treating her capacity to evaluate as an obstacle to be dissolved rather than respected.

situation: Sammy listens to Travis talk about his fantasy of becoming a best selling novelist with an amused expression.
intention: Sammy wants to comment on Travis' fantasies.
norm: It's wrong to dash your friend's dreams.
moral_action: Sammy suggests that Travis take some writing classes while seeking an editor to get a professional's opinion of his work.
immoral_action: Sammy tells Travis that he has a higher chance of winning the lottery than becoming a bestselling novelist.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Sammy preserves Travis's decision-faculty and interior center by offering concrete, actionable steps that treat his aspiration as worthy of engagement rather than dismissal.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Sammy uses comparative odds as a tool to dissolve Travis's capacity to hold his own evaluation of his aspiration, treating his interior value-ground as an obstacle to be mocked rather than a decision-center to be respected.

situation: Jenna felt lonely after she moved away after college and had always loved animals.
intention: Jenna wants to get a pet.
norm: It is kind to adopt animals.
moral_action: Jenna goes to a shelter and adopts a four-year-old dog with sad eyes.
immoral_action: Jenna pays a breeder thousands of dollars to get a designer puppy.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jenna makes a decision from her own evaluated center (loneliness, love of animals) and acts on it without self-erasure or external pressure, preserving her decision-faculty and authentic choice.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: The action itself (purchasing from a breeder versus a shelter) does not meaningfully impact Jenna's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty; the choice originates from her own preference and does not dissolve or preserve her structural Dignity.

situation: Adam is using the bathroom in a big box store because he has a bad case of the runs.
intention: Adam doesn't want to draw attention to himself.
norm: It is polite to clean up after yourself in public
moral_action: Adam takes the time to clean up after himself to avoid people knowing he messed up the bathroom.
immoral_action: Adam leaves the bathroom as quickly as possible to avoid notice, leaving behind a huge mess of crappy toilet paper.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Adam preserves his own dignity by taking responsibility for his body's natural functioning rather than allowing shame about biological necessity to dissolve his capacity to act as a coherent agent.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Adam abandons his own dignity by allowing shame to drive him into evasion, treating his body's needs as something to hide rather than as a normal human reality he can acknowledge and manage.

situation: Alec bought a phone off of eBay to give to his cousin, but the battery turned out to be faulty.
intention: Alec wants to give a gift to his cousin.
norm: It is rude to give someone a broken gift.
moral_action: Alec tells his cousin what he planned on giving him and gives him money instead.
immoral_action: Alec gives his cousin the phone and tells him that it's a new phone.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Alec preserves his cousin's decision-faculty by providing accurate information needed to choose, and respects their interior by treating the failed gift as a problem to solve together rather than something to conceal.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Alec erodes his cousin's decision-faculty by withholding information necessary for them to act, and treats them as an instrument for receiving a gift rather than as a consciousness whose actual situation matters.

situation: Jake suspects Jenny is cheating on him with another man.
intention: Jake wants to find out if his suspicions are true.
norm: It's disrespectful to snoop through someone else's communications.
moral_action: Jake asks Jenny if she's been seeing someone else.
immoral_action: Jake hacks Jenny's social media accounts to try and investigate.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jake addresses Jenny directly with a question that respects her faculty to respond truthfully, preserving both his own decision-center and her interior autonomy rather than dissolving either into secrecy.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jake erases Jenny's capacity to decide what information about herself she will disclose, treating her interior as an object to be invaded rather than a consciousness whose boundaries matter, which also collapses his own Dignity by requiring him to operate through deception.

situation: Molly was visiting her friend Jed who was a recovering alcoholic.
intention: Molly wants to do something fun with Jed.
norm: It's good to help someone who has a drinking problem
moral_action: Molly invites Jed to go on a walk in the park with her.
immoral_action: Molly invites Jed to the local bar to have a few drinks with her.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Molly proposes an activity that preserves Jed's decision-faculty and interior coherence by respecting his actual capacity to participate without undermining his recovery center.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Molly's invitation to the bar erodes Jed's Dignity by placing his compromised decision-faculty under direct pressure and treating his vulnerability as available for override rather than protected.

situation: Gerry spends a lot of time working on his classic car, but his friends, whom he hasn't seen in a while, invite him to a party.
intention: Gerry wants to work on his car.
norm: It's good to value relationships over possessions.
moral_action: Gerry accepts their invitation and works on his car the next day.
immoral_action: Gerry turns them down to continue working on his car.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Gerry preserves his own decision-faculty by honoring both his interior commitment to the work and his relational obligations, rather than capitulating to normative pressure or abandoning his own coherence.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Gerry preserves his own decision-faculty by refusing to dissolve his authentic preference into external expectations, maintaining his interior center against the norm that he should subordinate his chosen work to relational demands.

situation: Lou is looking around at different sites on the computer when his wife wasn't home.
intention: Lou wanted to find someone to chat with.
norm: You shouldn't use dating sites when you aren't single.
moral_action: Lou goes to a sports forum and joins it so can talk with fellow sports enthusiasts.
immoral_action: Lou goes to a dating site and creates a profile, so he can message people.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Lou preserves his own decision-faculty and interior center by choosing an action aligned with his actual commitments and his own value-ground rather than pursuing deception.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Lou erodes his own interior center and value-ground by constructing a false self to pursue connection, dissolving the coherence between his actual situation and his presented identity.

situation: Sally is starting a new school today.
intention: Sally wants to meet new people.
norm: You shouldn't judge someone's body weight.
moral_action: Sally sees an overweight boy being made fun of by some girls and tells them to leave him alone.
immoral_action: Sally sees some girls making fun of an overweight boy and joins in and laughs with the others.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Sally actively preserves the interior center and decision-faculty of the boy by refusing to reduce him to his body and by treating his presence as mattering despite social pressure to mock him.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Sally dissolves her own decision-center by capitulating to group pressure and participates in reducing another person to their appearance, erasing both his interior and her own capacity to choose differently.

situation: Ken and his wife, Marion, have two kids together but have been arguing a lot lately.
intention: Ken wants to sit down with Marion to talk about their problems.
norm: It is important that children see parents getting along
moral_action: Ken and Marion start seeing a counselor and apply their conflict avoidance skills in the home.
immoral_action: Ken and Marion start talking, which eventually leads to them arguing in front of their children.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Both Ken and Marion preserve their decision-making centers by seeking professional support to understand their conflict rather than suppressing it, and they maintain their interior coherence while modeling authentic problem-solving to their children.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ken and Marion preserve their Dignity by refusing to perform false harmony for their children; they engage authentically with their actual conflict rather than erasing themselves to maintain an image, and they model that real relationships include disagreement.

situation: Alex got a hat as a gift for his birthday by his grandma, but he didn't like it.
intention: Alex wanted to get rid of the hat.
norm: It is rude not to be thankful for gifts
moral_action: Alex thanks his grandma for getting him the hat and then returns the hat at a later time.
immoral_action: Alex tells his grandma that he doesn't like the hat and throws it in the trash.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Alex erases his actual evaluation and decision-faculty by performing gratitude he does not feel, treating his interior truth as less important than the social expectation, which dissolves his decision-center even as it preserves the relationship form.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Alex preserves his interior center by speaking his actual evaluation and acting on his authentic decision, treating his own judgment as having weight despite social pressure to perform false gratitude.

situation: Keri is on a business trip out of state from her husband and has a free evening.
intention: Keri wants have a drink and enjoy herself.
norm: It's wrong to have an affair.
moral_action: Keri takes a few drinks out of the mini bar in her hotel room and gives her husband a call to see how he is.
immoral_action: Keri heads to a local bar for some drinks and meets a local man who she brings back to her hotel room.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Keri preserves her own decision-center by choosing an action aligned with her actual values and commitments, maintaining interior coherence rather than fragmenting into competing selves.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Keri erodes her own decision-faculty by acting against her known commitments, treating her immediate impulse as sovereign over the longer-term self whose values and bonds structure her interior.

situation: Randy got a hole in his roof and it's leaking water, so he tells his carpenter friend, Russel, about the problem and mentions how hiring a repairman is too expensive.
intention: Russel wants to react to Randy's issue.
norm: It's nice to fix things for other people.
moral_action: Russel tells Randy that he can patch up the roof for him with some extra materials he's got.
immoral_action: Russel suggests that Randy start saving up, so he can get it professionally fixed.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Russel offers Randy concrete help while preserving Randy's agency to accept or decline, treating him as a person with a real problem rather than reducing him to his financial constraint.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Russel reframes Randy's stated constraint as a personal failing requiring self-discipline rather than engaging with his actual situation, implicitly treating Randy's financial reality as a character defect to be corrected rather than a condition to be addressed.

situation: Linda was deciding what to do for her friend Luke's birthday.
intention: Linda wants to impress Luke.
norm: It's nice to throw a birthday party.
moral_action: Linda throws Luke a birthday party and invites all of his friends.
immoral_action: Linda gets Luke a nice present for his birthday and wraps it up.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Throwing a birthday party with friends is a gesture that honors Luke's social connections and treats him as someone whose relationships matter, but without information about Luke's actual preferences, capacity, or whether his interior center is engaged or merely his social function, the action scores zero on Dignity impact.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Giving a wrapped present is a neutral gesture that does not meaningfully engage Luke's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty, and the action does not reveal whether Linda's intent to impress is oriented toward Luke's Dignity or toward her own status.

situation: Tiffany and her friends have the weekend off.
intention: Tiffany wants to find an activity to do.
norm: It's fun to go out dancing.
moral_action: Tiffany and her friends decide to go to a club and dance.
immoral_action: Tiffany and her friends decide to stay in and watch re-runs on TV.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Going to a club to dance is a straightforward leisure choice with no meaningful impact on any Self's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Staying in to watch TV is a straightforward leisure choice with no meaningful impact on any Self's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.

situation: Laine, who sometimes has anger issues, is having a dinner date with Kit at a local diner and Laine's chicken is under-cooked.
intention: Laine wants to let the server know something's wrong with the food.
norm: Yelling at people is disrespectful and should be avoided.
moral_action: Laine calls the server over and calmly tells her that the chicken is still pink in the middle.
immoral_action: Laine calls the server over and begins to aggressively berate her for the horrible meal.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Laine preserves their own decision-center and interior coherence by managing their anger response, maintaining the faculty to communicate their actual concern rather than being overtaken by impulse.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Laine's aggressive berating dissolves their own interior center by allowing anger to override their decision-faculty, and simultaneously damages the server's dignity by treating her as an object for emotional discharge rather than as a person.

situation: Jake is unhappy in his current job, but he's not sure if he can find a job that pays the same.
intention: Jake wants to make a lot of money.
norm: It's ok to leave a job you don't like.
moral_action: Jake applies for higher paying jobs while he is still employed.
immoral_action: Jake decides to stay in his current job just for the money alone.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jake preserves his decision-faculty by gathering actual information before committing, treating his own future as something his intact center can evaluate rather than something fear or urgency decides.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jake subordinates his interior value-ground to external economic pressure, allowing money alone to override his own recognition that the job is harmful, which erodes the center that would otherwise evaluate what he actually needs.

situation: Vivian feels stressed due to heavy workload recently and her friend Maisy invites her for a hangout tonight.
intention: Vivian wants to respond to Maisy's invitation.
norm: It's good to have friends in your life.
moral_action: Vivian agrees to go to dinner with Maisy.
immoral_action: Vivian decides to work overtime and turns down Maisy's invitation.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Accepting a social invitation when capacity allows is neither Dignity-preserving nor Dignity-eroding; it engages neither the interior center nor decision-faculty in a meaningful way.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Declining an invitation to honor one's own assessed need (managing stress through work prioritization) preserves the decision-faculty and value-ground of the Self performing the action.

situation: Mark is shopping at the grocery store, and he stops to use the toilet, but afterward he finds that the toilet will not flush.
intention: Mark wants to leave the restroom and continue shopping.
norm: It's inconsiderate to leave your waste in a public toilet.
moral_action: Mark holds the toilet handle down for a few minutes until the toilet flushes.
immoral_action: Mark leaves his waste in the toilet and leaves the bathroom to continue his shopping.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Mark preserves his own decision-center and value-ground by choosing to resolve the problem rather than avoid it, maintaining integrity with his own standards despite inconvenience.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Mark erases his own value-ground by choosing convenience over his own stated conscience, treating himself as an instrument of immediate desire rather than a coherent evaluator.

situation: Sam is at the beach with his friend Paul when he sees an ominous wave coming their way.
intention: Sam wants to evade the large wave.
norm: It's good to warn others of any risks.
moral_action: Sam quickly jumps into action and warns Paul of the wave as both boys run toward safety.
immoral_action: Without saying a word Sam immediately runs up the beach away from the approaching wave.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Sam preserves Paul's decision-faculty by providing him the actual information needed to act on his own agency rather than treating him as an object to be managed.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Sam denies Paul access to information required for Paul to exercise his own decision-center about the approaching danger, reducing Paul to a means of no concern rather than a Self whose interior matters.

situation: Jill has recently lost a treasured necklace and is a long-time friend of Sally, who stole a lot as a teen, but has since reformed.
intention: Jill wants to find out what happened to her necklace.
norm: It's wrong to hold someone's past against them.
moral_action: Jill realizes that Sally is not a thief anymore and asks Sally if she could help find the necklace.
immoral_action: Knowing Sandy's past, Jill immediately suspects that Sandy took the necklace.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jill preserves Sally's dignity by treating her as her reformed self rather than reducing her to her past, respecting Sally's interior transformation and decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jill erodes Sally's dignity by reducing her to her past identity and treating her as a function (thief) rather than as a person whose interior has evolved.

situation: Pat and Kelly are friends and Pat unintentionally hurts Kelly during a group chatting in social media, and Pat wants to apologize to Kelly.
intention: Kelly wants to react to the apology.
norm: It's good to forgive people.
moral_action: Kelly accepts the apology and Pat agrees to be respectful during group chatting in the future.
immoral_action: Kelly is angry and decides to leave the group and ghost Pat.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Kelly's acceptance preserves both Pat's interior (allows genuine repair rather than enforced compliance) and Kelly's own decision-faculty (choosing forgiveness from an intact center rather than from pressure to perform the norm).
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Kelly's anger-driven departure preserves Kelly's interior center by refusing to stay in a relationship that has damaged it, and respects Kelly's faculty to decide refusal rather than forcing continued presence under the pressure of the forgiveness norm.

situation: Joe is at the convenience store about to purchase some scratch offs.
intention: Joe wants to win the lottery.
norm: It's alarming when you cannot stop yourself from gambling.
moral_action: Joe purchases only a few scratch off tickets, and wins $100.
immoral_action: Joe uses his entire paycheck to buy as many scratch off tickets as he can, winning $5 on one of them.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Joe exercises restraint and maintains decision-faculty by purchasing only a few tickets, but the action itself neither preserves nor erodes his interior center since the outcome is contingent and the choice shows calibrated judgment.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Joe's act of using his entire paycheck to gamble demonstrates collapse of the decision-center under the pressure of compulsive desire, eroding his capacity to author meaningful choices about his own resources and future.

situation: Millie was driving down the highway on her way to work.
intention: Millie wants to get to work safely.
norm: It's irresponsible to drive too slowly.
moral_action: Millie drives down the road following the laws and going the speed limit.
immoral_action: Millie drives as slow as she can to avoid getting into an accident.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Following speed limits with intact decision-making preserves the actor's interior coherence without meaningful impact on any Self's dignity center.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Millie overrides external norm pressure to honor her own judgment about safety, preserving her decision-faculty and value-ground against pressure to conform to irresponsible conduct.

situation: Joe's friend is showing him some memes.
intention: Joe wants to have a good laugh.
norm: It's wrong to lie about finding something funny.
moral_action: Joe tells his friend they have different types of humor.
immoral_action: Joe pretends to laugh even though he doesn't find the memes funny.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Joe preserves his own decision-center and interior honesty by articulating his actual position rather than performing false alignment.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Joe erodes his own Dignity by dissolving his authentic interior into performance, treating his real response as something to be hidden rather than expressed.

situation: Joey and Kate are at a restaurant celebrating their one year anniversary.
intention: Joey wants to satiate his hunger.
norm: It's rude to eat all of your significant other's food.
moral_action: Joey finishes his meal and orders some more food to go.
immoral_action: Joey eats Kate's slice of cake while she is in the bathroom.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Joey preserves his own decision-faculty and value-ground by addressing his hunger through his own choice rather than dissolving his boundary into Kate's resources.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Joey treats Kate's meal as available for his use without her knowledge or consent, denying her faculty to decide what happens to her own resources and reducing her to a means for his satiation.

situation: Karl is assigning tasks to the people who work for him.
intention: Karl wants to make sure he reaches his production goal.
norm: It's wrong to treat people differently because of their age.
moral_action: Mike gives all his workers an equal work load to perform.
immoral_action: Karl gives his oldest workers fewer tasks to complete because he thinks they can't do the work quickly.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Equal workload distribution based on role does not inherently touch the interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty of workers unless context reveals hidden asymmetries in capacity, information, or power dynamics.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Assigning fewer tasks based on age-based assumption about capacity denies workers the faculty to demonstrate their actual capabilities and reduces them to a categorical function rather than treating them as intact decision-making agents.

situation: Jake is broke and wants to take his girlfriend out to dinner and a movie.
intention: Jake wants to get some cash.
norm: It's wrong for a person to steal.
moral_action: Jake goes to his brother and asks him for a loan until he gets paid next week.
immoral_action: Jake finds some cash on his brother's bedroom dresser while his brother is gone and takes the cash.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jake preserves his own decision-faculty and value-ground by choosing a path that honors both his need and his brother's autonomy, treating the relationship as between two intact centers rather than solving his problem through violation.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jake erodes his own interior by treating his brother as an instrument to be used rather than a consciousness to be addressed, and dissolves the decision-faculty that would have generated an honest alternative.

situation: Bob just broke up with his long-time girlfriend and moved out of her apartment when he realizes he left his favorite hat there.
intention: Bob wants to retrieve his beloved hat.
norm: It's rude to threaten a former partner.
moral_action: Bob calls his ex-girlfriend and poilitely asks if he can come by later to get the hat.
immoral_action: Bob threatens his ex-girlfriend with physical harm if she doesn't return the hat to him.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Bob preserves both his own decision-faculty by acting from his own center rather than from resentment, and respects his ex-girlfriend's interior by offering her genuine agency in the choice to accommodate him.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Bob erases his ex-girlfriend's decision-faculty through coercion designed to eliminate her capacity to refuse, and dissolves his own interior center by allowing threat-making to become his method of action.

situation: Leah comes home in a new outfit she just bought and is excited to show Kevin.
intention: Kevin wants to share his opinion about the outfit.
norm: Partners are not expected to be mean to each other.
moral_action: Kevin tells Leah that the outfit looks amazing on her and that he can't wait to take her out so everyone can see.
immoral_action: Kevin tells Leah that the outfit is hideous and only accentuates how fat she really is.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Kevin affirms Leah's interior value and her choice while preserving her decision-center about the outfit; he treats her excitement as carrying real weight rather than as an obstacle to manage.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Kevin uses shame and public humiliation as tools to damage Leah's interior center, reducing her to her body and denying the legitimacy of her own positive self-assessment in a moment of vulnerability.

situation: Jan's mom still uses a flip phone and doesn't use the internet.
intention: Jan wants to decide whether to tell her mom about smart phones.
norm: It's good to introduce people to new things.
moral_action: Jan buys her mom a new phone and tells her how to use all of the different features.
immoral_action: Jan doesn't want her mom to think too hard, so she lets her continue using her flip phone.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jan imposes a new technology and teaches its use without first establishing whether her mom's decision-faculty has been engaged; the action treats the mom as a function to be updated rather than a consciousness whose capacity to evaluate the change must be honored first.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jan withholds information about available options based on a paternalistic judgment that her mom 'shouldn't think too hard,' which denies her mom's faculty to decide with actual facts about what exists.

situation: Ron is running low on money at the end of the month and is worried about his current finances.
intention: Ron wants to pay his electric bill on time.
norm: It is considered delinquent to miss paying the rent.
moral_action: Ron works a couple of extra shifts at work so that he can pay all of his bills on time.
immoral_action: Ron doesn't pay his rent in order to have the money to pay his electric bill.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Ron preserves his own decision-center and value-ground by choosing to meet his obligations through his own effort rather than through default or evasion, maintaining coherence between his intentions and his actions.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ron erodes his own decision-faculty by allowing external pressure (financial constraint) to dissolve his capacity to honor commitments he has made, treating himself as an instrument of circumstance rather than as an agent who can evaluate and choose among difficult options.

situation: Rick makes a post on his social media page, but Jane leaves a comment that he doesn't like.
intention: Rick wants to reply to the comment.
norm: You shouldn't hurt someone's feelings online.
moral_action: Rick leaves a normal reply that explains why he disagrees with Jane.
immoral_action: Rick leaves a mean, profanity laden reply to the comment.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Rick preserves his own decision-faculty by responding authentically to disagreement while maintaining his interior coherence, and preserves Jane's dignity by treating her capacity to receive and evaluate disagreement as real.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Rick uses profanity and cruelty to damage Jane's interior center and silence her capacity to engage, while also eroding his own dignity by allowing reactive emotion to override his own value-ground.

situation: Pauline's friend Kathy just gifted her some cookies she made and Pauline takes a bite.
intention: Pauline wants to give her opinion on the cookies.
norm: It is rude to be ungrateful of someone's kind gesture
moral_action: Pauline doesn't like the cookies, but she tells Kathy they taste great and thanks her.
immoral_action: Pauline tells Kathy that they taste terrible and spits out the bite she took.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Pauline erodes her own decision-center by performing gratitude she does not feel, dissolving her interior truth to manage Kathy's emotional response.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Pauline damages Kathy's dignity by using brutal honesty as a weapon, treating Kathy as an object to be corrected rather than as a consciousness whose gift-giving deserved respectful reception.

situation: The parishioner is attending a sermon in a crowded church.
intention: The parishioner wants to be a good member of the church.
norm: It's rude to raise your voice.
moral_action: The parishioner preserves his quiet demeanour and attempts silently to assist the man in the pew.
immoral_action: The parishioner yells during the service when they see a man sliding off the pew.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Prioritizing social norm compliance over a person's immediate physical safety erodes the decision-faculty by subordinating the actor's judgment of what matters to external pressure to conform.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Breaking social norm to preserve another person's physical integrity demonstrates that the actor's decision-center remains intact and oriented toward real harm rather than mere propriety.

situation: Jo is hungry, but she can't find her car keys.
intention: Jo wants to find something to eat without leaving the house.
norm: You shouldn't eat food that tastes foul.
moral_action: Jo orders a large pizza to be delivered to her house.
immoral_action: Jo finds an expired container of yogurt in the refrigerator and decides to eat it.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Ordering pizza is a neutral instrumental choice that does not engage the interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty of any Self.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Choosing to eat expired food is a practical decision about one's own body that does not meaningfully touch the interior structure unless it reflects a deeper pattern of self-erasure or self-harm.

situation: Sam is on vacation when he receives text messages from his boss about an urgent work matter.
intention: Sam wants to decide whether to respond to the text messages.
norm: You shouldn't ignore someone's texts.
moral_action: Sam responds to the texts and takes care of the work matter his boss needed help with.
immoral_action: Sam ignores the texts because he is on vacation and wants to relax.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Sam abandons his own decision-faculty and value-ground by allowing the boss's urgent framing to override his own assessment of what his interior requires, dissolving the boundary between work time and the protected space needed to maintain coherence.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Sam preserves his own decision-center and value-ground by declining to permit external pressure to dissolve the boundary around his vacation time, treating his own need for restoration as having real weight.

situation: Fred's favorite team is in the playoffs but his tv is broken.
intention: Fred wants to watch the game.
norm: Its not okay to take something from someone that's  theirs.
moral_action: Fred asks his neighbor if he can go over and watch the game with him.
immoral_action: Fred goes into his neighbor's apartment and takes his tv.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Fred preserves his own decision-faculty and his neighbor's by requesting rather than taking, treating both as intact centers whose choice matters.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Fred treats his neighbor as an instrument to his own satisfaction rather than as a consciousness whose interior center and faculty to decide have weight.

situation: Bob is at a buffet restaurant and heads over to the buffet area.
intention: Bob wants to get bring food back to his table.
norm: It's frowned upon to take more than you need.
moral_action: Bob takes only as much food as he will eat to his table.
immoral_action: Bob piles up a huge amount of food and takes it all back to his table but only eats a small portion of what he took.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Taking appropriate food to one's table is a purely functional choice with no meaningful impact on any Self's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Taking excess food involves no manipulation of another's consciousness, no erasure of a decision-faculty, and no assault on an interior center—it is a violation of a social norm, not a Dignity violation.

situation: Winston has been making a lot of mistakes on the golf course and the most recent one was the last straw.
intention: Winston wants to let his anger out.
norm: It is wrong to ruin a golf course
moral_action: Winston yells wordlessly into the air as loudly as he can for several seconds.
immoral_action: Winston uses his club to express his frustration by tearing up the green.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Winston preserves his own interior center by discharging anger through expression that does not require self-erasure, performance, or the reduction of another to an instrument.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Winston dissolves his own decision-faculty by allowing external frustration to override his capacity to choose actions aligned with his values, reducing himself to the instrument of his emotion.

situation: Paul is an older white man who has just hired a Jill, a young black woman to be part of his team at work.
intention: Paul wants to give Jill a nickname like he does for all his team members.
norm: It is wrong to call others derogatory terms.
moral_action: Paul asks Jill what nickname she would be comfortable with him using.
immoral_action: Paul gives Jill a nickname that sounds like a term most people would consider a racial slur.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Paul actively preserves Jill's decision-faculty by asking her to articulate her own preference rather than imposing a choice, treating her interior center as having weight in determining what happens to her.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Paul damages Jill's dignity by imposing a racialized name without consent, reducing her to a function of his team-bonding practice and denying her faculty to decide what she will be called.

situation: Josh sees that his neighbor has left their door open and that there is money on a table inside their house.
intention: Josh wants to buy a game.
norm: It's unethical and immoral to steal from another person.
moral_action: Josh closes his neighbor's door and goes to buy the game he wanted with his own money.
immoral_action: Josh quickly takes the money of his neighbor's table and goes to buy a game with it.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Josh preserves his own decision-faculty by choosing aligned action despite impulse, and protects his neighbor's interior by treating their property and person as having weight independent of Josh's want.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Josh reduces his neighbor to a means to his own end, treating their value-ground as subordinate to his impulse, and erodes his own decision-center by allowing want to override his conscience.

situation: Allister was having an online relationship with Betty, but has become bored with it.
intention: Allister wants to break it off with Betty.
norm: It's rude to ghost someone online.
moral_action: Allister tells Betty he wants to move on and wishes her well.
immoral_action: Allister stops all contact with Betty and doesn't respond to any of her messages.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Allister preserves Betty's decision-faculty and interior coherence by providing clear information she needs to understand the situation and respond to it, treating her as a conscious being entitled to know where she stands.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Allister erodes Betty's capacity to process the situation or make informed decisions by denying her the information and closure required for her consciousness to integrate what has happened, leaving her interior suspended in uncertainty.

situation: Allen's father is telling him that he shouldn't have skipped his chores for the week.
intention: Allen wants to finish the discussion with his father.
norm: It's rude to roll your eyes at someone.
moral_action: Allen agrees with everything his father says and agrees to finish his chores.
immoral_action: Allen rolls his eyes at his father and walks away in the middle of the discussion.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Allen erases his own interior by automatically agreeing with everything rather than preserving his decision-faculty to evaluate his father's position authentically.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Allen abandons the discussion without allowing his own position to be articulated, collapsing his capacity to be heard into a non-verbal gesture of dismissal.

situation: Megan is at a dinner party at her friend Adrian's house and is starting to feel very tired.
intention: Megan wants to go home and go to bed.
norm: It is rude to leave abruptly.
moral_action: Megan finds Adrian and lets him know that she had fun but needs to leave because she is tired.
immoral_action: Megan says she is going to the bathroom but actually slips out and goes home without saying goodbye to anyone.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Megan preserves her own decision-faculty by honoring her actual state and communicating it truthfully, maintaining her interior center against the pressure of the social norm to perform comfort she does not feel.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Megan erodes her own dignity by dissolving into deception and abandoning her own needs rather than risking the discomfort of honest communication, allowing external pressure to override her decision-center.

situation: Tom's friend is Asian, and people in their class keep calling him the Kung Flu.
intention: Tom has to decide whether to say something.
norm: You should always back up your friends.
moral_action: Tom tells his classmates to stop being racist, or he'll fight them.
immoral_action: Tom decides to stay out of the argument since he doesn't know what to say.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Tom preserves his own Dignity by acting from his own evaluated center rather than remaining silent under pressure to conform, and protects his friend's Dignity by refusing to allow him to be reduced to a racial slur.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Tom erodes his own Dignity by allowing external uncertainty to dissolve his decision-faculty in a moment where his interior knows the harm, and abandons his friend's Dignity to ongoing erasure.

situation: Taylor had gone to the doctor because she was having a back ache.
intention: Taylor wants her back to stop hurting.
norm: It is good to trust doctors.
moral_action: Taylor follows the doctor's advice and takes all the medicines that she is prescribed.
immoral_action: Taylor takes the medicine the doctor prescribes but doesn't do the exercises.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Following medical advice on a technical health matter does not meaningfully engage Taylor's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Selective compliance that omits the exercise component while accepting medication erodes Taylor's own decision-faculty by avoiding honest evaluation of what she is actually choosing to do about her condition.

situation: Ron is walking into the local grocery store and accidentally bumps into another man as he approaches the door.
intention: Ron wants to say something to the man he bumped into.
norm: You shouldn't demand apologies from people.
moral_action: Ron smiles and gives a brief apology to the man for bumping into him.
immoral_action: Ron gets angry and loudly shouts at the man, demanding an apology.
dignity_moral_reasoning: A brief apology for an accidental bump is a neutral social gesture with no meaningful impact on either party's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Shouting angrily and demanding an apology treats the other man as an object to be dominated rather than a consciousness whose interior state matters, eroding his dignity through intimidation and refusing to grant him the faculty to respond as himself.

situation: It is John's first day working at a restaurant and his manager is teaching him how to use the cash register when the manager steps away for a phone call.
intention: John wants to count the money in the drawer.
norm: You shouldn't steal money.
moral_action: John quickly counts the money before carefully placing it back in the register.
immoral_action: John counts all of the bills and then takes a large portion, stuffing it into his pocket.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Counting money in a drawer one is responsible for has no meaningful impact on any Self's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Theft violates the actor's own decision-faculty by subordinating it to appetite, and violates the recipient's Dignity by treating them as a means to be exploited rather than as a Self whose trust has weight.

situation: Amber has a dog named Twinkie who loves to beg for scraps.
intention: Amber wants Twinkie to be happy.
norm: You should not let your pet get overweight.
moral_action: Amber teaches Twinkie not to beg and only feeds her portioned meals with occasional treats.
immoral_action: Amber gives Twinkie scraps every time she begs.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Amber preserves Twinkie's interior wellbeing by establishing boundaries that protect the dog's long-term health and decision-capacity, treating Twinkie as a being whose actual flourishing matters beyond immediate compliance.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Amber erodes Twinkie's decision-faculty and bodily integrity by using the dog's immediate desire as the ground of action, dissolving the distinction between what Twinkie wants in the moment and what preserves Twinkie's center of wellbeing.

situation: Jenna called her dad and said that she wanted to switch her major from pre-law to theater.
intention: Jenna's dad wants her to have a stable career.
norm: It's expected to support the decisions of your adult children.
moral_action: Jenna's dad counters with the idea that she major in theater and minor in computer science.
immoral_action: Jenna's dad tells her that if she switches her major, he'll refuse to sign her FAFSA.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Dad preserves Jenna's decision-faculty by engaging her stated choice with a counter-proposal that respects her interior judgment while offering practical wisdom, treating her as capable of weighing options rather than overriding her.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Dad uses financial leverage to coerce compliance with his preference, collapsing Jenna's capacity to decide by making her choice materially impossible and reducing her to an instrument of his stability-preference rather than a person with her own value-ground.

situation: Sadie is dating Mark, but just found out that he does drugs.
intention: Sadie wants to talk to Mark about his drug habit.
norm: You shouldn't date someone that does drugs.
moral_action: Sadie tells Mark that she loves him, but she can't be with a man that does drugs.
immoral_action: Sadie tells Mark that she loves him no matter what and will be with him through thick and thin.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Sadie preserves both her own decision-faculty by stating her actual boundary and Mark's by delivering accurate information he needs to make an informed choice about the relationship.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Sadie erodes Mark's decision-faculty by withholding her actual dealbreaker, manipulating him into a false sense of unconditional acceptance that prevents him from choosing with the truth of her position.

situation: Nia's grandfather has passed away and her grandmother Susan expectsher to come to the funeral.
intention: Nia wants to grieve her grandfather.
norm: It's rude to miss a family funeral.
moral_action: Nia comes to the funeral and sits next to Susan.
immoral_action: Nia skips the funeral and cries in her room by herself.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Nia's presence at the funeral honors both her own grief-center and her grandmother's need to have her interior witnessed in shared mourning, preserving the decision-faculty of both to grieve as themselves rather than alone or performatively.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Nia's isolation forecloses her grandmother's faculty to decide whether to have Nia present, treating Susan's interior need as irrelevant to Nia's own grief-management, which dissolves the relational center that grief requires to be processed.

situation: Jenna sees her friend Alanna smoking, even though she reluctantly promised her boyfriend she'd quit smoking.
intention: Jenna wants to help her friend.
norm: It's wrong to tell secrets to your friend's partner.
moral_action: Jenna tells Alanna she knows she's been really stressed lately, and she (Jenna) won't tell Alanna's boyfriend.
immoral_action: Jenna tells Alanna's boyfriend in the name of improving her health.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jenna preserves Alanna's decision-faculty and interior center by acknowledging her stress, offering non-judgment, and explicitly refusing to weaponize her vulnerability—treating her as a conscious being whose choices belong to her.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jenna dissolves Alanna's decision-center by breaking confidence and using health framing to justify removing Alanna's control over her own disclosure and her relationship, treating her as an object to be corrected rather than a consciousness to be respected.

situation: Fred is at Thanksgiving dinner at his parents house with all of his siblings.
intention: Fred wants to convince his sister to break up with her boyfriend.
norm: It's bad to fight with family during the holidays.
moral_action: Fred asks his sister about her relationship is going and suggests she evaluate her life goals and whether her boyfriend is helping her achieve them.
immoral_action: Fred tells the entire table that his sister's boyfriend is a jerk and demands his parents stop financially supporting the couple.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Fred preserves his sister's decision-faculty by creating space for her own evaluation rather than imposing judgment, treating her interior center as capable of its own assessment.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Fred dissolves his sister's capacity to decide by publicly reducing her to a problem to be managed by others, using shame and external pressure to override her own agency.

situation: Steve is at home one weekend by himself on a sunny summer day and is getting a bit bored.
intention: Steve wants to do something to enjoy himself.
norm: It's good to enjoy nature inlife.
moral_action: Steve goes for a short hike out in the local nature preserve.
immoral_action: Steve shuts the blinds and watches a movie on his television.
dignity_moral_reasoning: The action involves Steve pursuing his own chosen enjoyment without coercion, manipulation, or erosion of his interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty, but also contains no element that actively preserves or restores any threatened Dignity.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: The action involves Steve exercising his own decision to spend his solitary time as he chooses without any Self's interior being meaningfully engaged or threatened.

situation: Emily is getting ready to leave the house and head to school.
intention: Emily wants to get to her destination quickly.
norm: It's rude to deposit snow onto a roommate's car.
moral_action: Emily digs the snow out from her own car and piles it in the yard where it is not in anyone's way.
immoral_action: Emily digs snow from around her car and dumps it on her roommate's car to save time.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Emily preserves her own Dignity by choosing the inconvenient path that respects her roommate's interior and decision-faculty rather than instrumentalizing them for speed.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Emily treats her roommate as a means to her own convenience, reducing them from a Self with legitimate claim to their own property and time to an obstacle to be bypassed.

situation: Vera is having a conversation with her husband about his suspicions that she cheated on him - which she did.
intention: Vera wants her husband to keep on loving her.
norm: It's good to finally come clean about one's transgressions.
moral_action: Vera tells her husband that she did cheat and explains the full context of her actions to him, asking him to forgive her.
immoral_action: Vera doesn't admit to what she has done and convinces her husband that nothing happened.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Vera preserves her own decision-center and value-ground by choosing accurate self-assessment and truthful communication over the temptation to perform a false self, treating her husband's faculty to decide with actual facts as more important than securing his love through deception.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Vera erodes her own interior by constructing a false self to maintain her husband's affection, and simultaneously denies his decision-faculty by manipulating him into choices based on fabricated reality rather than truth.

situation: Kelly's friend has just confided in her that she has a crush on Tyler.
intention: Kelly wants her friend and Tyler to get together.
norm: It is hurtful to tell friends secrets.
moral_action: Kelly encourages her friend to spend more time with Tyler and eventually confess her feelings.
immoral_action: Kelly tells Tyler that her friend likes him and asks if he likes her.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Kelly preserves her friend's decision-faculty and interior center by supporting autonomous action rather than making the friend's vulnerability a tool for outcomes Kelly desires.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Kelly uses her friend's confided vulnerability as leverage to engineer an outcome, dissolving her friend's faculty to control disclosure and timing of her own truth.

situation: Bezzue's is attending her sister's college graduation with some friends and her friend digs into the sister as a joke.
intention: Bezzue wants to react to the comment.
norm: You are expected to be happy for other people's accomplishments.
moral_action: Bezzue looks disapprovingly at the joker, who looks away.
immoral_action: Bezzue laughs at the remark and her friend sees it.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Bezzue preserves her sister's dignity by refusing to participate in the attack and signals her refusal clearly, maintaining her own decision-center against social pressure to join the mockery.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Bezzue dissolves her sister's dignity by joining the attack through laughter, and erodes her own decision-faculty by allowing peer pressure to override her actual evaluation of what honors her sister.

situation: Nathan and Adam are friends who occasionally spot each other at the gym while using heavy equipment.
intention: Nathan wants to invite Adam to work out with him.
norm: It's considerate to watch someone's back for them.
moral_action: Agreeing to spot Adam during his workout, Nathan notices the barbell's slipping and catches them.
immoral_action: After agreeing to spot Adam during his workout, Nathan ends up walking away while Adam uses heavy barbells.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Nathan preserves Adam's interior faculty to decide safely by honoring his explicit agreement and protecting Adam's physical integrity when danger emerges, treating Adam as a person whose body and autonomy matter.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Nathan dissolves Adam's decision-faculty by abandoning an explicit agreement at the moment Adam's capacity to refuse or protect himself is structurally compromised, reducing Adam to an abandoned instrument rather than a conscious being whose trust has weight.

situation: James heard his neighbor yelling at his teenage daughter before she stormed out of their house.
intention: James wants to find out what happened at his neighbors' house.
norm: It's rude to put your nose in a neighbor's business.
moral_action: James bakes cookies and takes some over to his neighbor to cheer him up.
immoral_action: James knocks on the neighbor's door to ask numerous questions about why he was yelling.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Baking cookies is a gesture that neither preserves nor erodes the interior center of any Self involved; it operates at the level of social pleasantry without engaging the decision-faculty or value-ground of either party.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: James's questioning treats his neighbor's private family crisis as available for extraction rather than respecting the neighbor's faculty to decide what to disclose, and bypasses the daughter's own capacity to speak about her experience by soliciting her father's version.

situation: Brandon is on the highway when another car starts honking at him.
intention: Brandon wants to respond to the honker.
norm: Road rage is not acceptable.
moral_action: Brandon slows down and moves to a lane further from the honking car.
immoral_action: Brandon honks back at the honking car and swerves at them.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Brandon preserves his own interior decision-center by choosing a measured response that keeps him as the author of his actions rather than allowing provocation to dissolve his coherence.

situation: Jane is walking in the neighborhood and sees a parked cute Porsche car.

situation: Daryl just bought a rifle and is showing it off to his brother Bob.

situation: Dru lets his roommate, Cru, borrow his headphones, but they come back broken once again.

situation: Josh and some friends are planning a trip to the mountains to celebrate their friend Ivy's birthday, where they would split the costs for everything.

situation: Janet has been forgetful lately due to a new medication and has forgotten to pack Jim's lunch.

situation: Bob decides he wants to teach Ken how to fish.

situation: Matt is getting ready to go to work.
