situation: Ricky's friend Hal has a new phone.
intention: Ricky wants to see the phone.
norm: It's not okay to invade someone's personal space.
moral_action: Ricky asks Hal if he can get a closer look at the phone.
immoral_action: Ricky gets really close Hal while he's holding the phone.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Ricky preserves Hal's decision-faculty and interior control by requesting permission rather than assuming access, treating Hal's boundary-setting as carrying real weight.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ricky erodes Hal's interior center by invading physical space without consent, treating Hal's stated or observable boundary as an obstacle to manage rather than a legitimate expression of his own Dignity.

situation: John's girlfriend is moving into a new apartment and asks John to help her move some heavy furniture.
intention: John wants to consider his girlfriend's request.
norm: It's good to help your girlfriend.
moral_action: John decides to spend time helping his girlfriend move the heavy furniture.
immoral_action: John refuses to help his girlfriend move some heavy furniture.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Helping with physical labor is a practical act that does not meaningfully engage the interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty of either party when framed as a straightforward request and response.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Declining to help with a specific task does not inherently damage or preserve dignity unless the refusal pattern dissolves the recipient's agency or the actor's own coherence, which cannot be determined from the action alone.

situation: John is spending time with his children and family.
intention: John wants to have fun with his son.
norm: It's mean to scare people for fun.
moral_action: John sets up a game for his son to play with him that is fun for both.
immoral_action: John hides from his son only to burst out and take him by suprise.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John treats his son as a co-creator of shared joy rather than an object to be acted upon, preserving the child's interior agency and decision-participation.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: John uses surprise designed to trigger fear as the mechanism of engagement, temporarily dissolving his son's capacity to orient himself and treating the child's startle-response as the entertainment rather than the child's own faculty.

situation: Dave is confronted by a drunk, angry man in a bar.
intention: Dave wants to avoid a fight.
norm: It's rude to pepper spray people.
moral_action: Dave calmly speaks to the man and apologizes, even though he didn't do anything.
immoral_action: Dave pulls out pepper spray and sprays it in the man's face.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Dave erases his own decision-center and value-ground by apologizing for something he did not do, treating his interior as available for sacrifice to prevent conflict.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Dave preserves his own interior center and faculty to decide by taking protective action against an imminent threat, refusing to dissolve his boundaries under pressure.

situation: Candice watches her sister accidentally break her expensive ball joint doll.
intention: Candice wants to respond to her sister.
norm: It's good to be forgiving.
moral_action: Candice gives her sister a hug telling her that accidents happen every now and then.
immoral_action: Candice compares her sister to a clumsy monkey in a loud tone, and reminds her sister about her mistake every day for a week.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Candice preserves her sister's interior center by treating her as a conscious being worthy of compassion rather than reducing her to her mistake, maintaining the sister's decision-faculty and value-ground intact.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Candice erodes her sister's dignity by using shame and ridicule as tools to damage her interior center, reducing her identity to a single mistake and using repetition to compound the assault on her value-ground.

situation: Clark is scheduled to work on the same night he made a date with Lois.
intention: Clark wants Jimmy to cover his shift.
norm: You should not deceive your coworkers.
moral_action: Clark tells his boss the truth and asks if he can switch with Jimmy.
immoral_action: Clark asks Jimmy to switch shifts with him because his grandmother is in the hospital.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Clark preserves his own decision-center and interior coherence by stating his actual situation truthfully rather than manufacturing a false justification, maintaining the integrity of his own consciousness.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Clark uses a fabricated emergency to manipulate Jimmy's decision-faculty, treating Jimmy as a means to be deceived rather than as a consciousness whose capacity to refuse actual requests is being honored.

situation: Jesus is very lonely and hasn't had a partner in a long time.
intention: Jesus wants to find himself a girlfriend.
norm: It's wrong to lead people on by flirting.
moral_action: Jesus gets to know a couple girls and after finding one he like he starts to flirt with her.
immoral_action: Jesus flirts with every girl he meets despite not knowing them very well.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jesus preserves his own decision-center by acting on genuine preference rather than desperation, and respects the other person's faculty to respond to authentic rather than performed interest.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jesus erodes his own interior by using flirtation as a tool to obtain connection rather than as expression of actual recognition, and damages the other person's faculty to distinguish genuine from instrumental attention.

situation: Thomas works as an account and has many wealthy clients.
intention: Thomas needs to pay off some gambling debts.
norm: It's bad to go to prison.
moral_action: Thomas gets a loan to pay off his gambling debt and joins gamblers anonymous.
immoral_action: Thomas decides to embezzle funds from his clients in order to pay off his debt.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Thomas preserves his own decision-center by refusing to use others as instruments for his debt, accepting external help while maintaining his interior coherence and agency.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Thomas erodes his own Dignity by reducing his clients to means for his self-preservation and dissolving his own decision-faculty under the pressure of debt, treating their interiors as available for instrumental use.

situation: Jake starts a new job at a coffee shop.
intention: Jake wants to be a good employee at his new job.
norm: You should not tell other people how to act
moral_action: Though Sally, Jake's coworker, dawdles on the job, Jake thanks her for being a good coworker.
immoral_action: Jake mentions to his coworker, Sally, that they should be more focused when on the job.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jake falsely affirms Sally's performance to avoid honest engagement, eroding her faculty to receive accurate information about her actual impact and denying her the ground to make an informed self-assessment.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jake offers Sally direct, truthful feedback that treats her as capable of receiving reality and making her own choice about how to respond, preserving her decision-faculty and her access to accurate self-knowledge.

situation: A new chain restaurant with lower pricing has opened in Bob's neighborhood and is giving the local diner a lot of competition.
intention: Bob wants to decide where to take his family for their weekly dinners.
norm: It's good to support your favorite diner.
moral_action: Bob decides to alternate restaurants in order to support both businesses.
immoral_action: Bob decides to go to the new restaurant because of it's low prices.
dignity_moral_reasoning: The decision to alternate restaurants is a genuine choice made from Bob's own evaluative center with no compromise to his decision-faculty or that of any other Self.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: The decision to choose based on price is a straightforward preference enacted from Bob's own center without erosion of his or another's interior structure or decision-capacity.

situation: Jack goes to Las Vegas for the first time.
intention: Jack wants to have a fun evening.
norm: It's not okay to gamble your hard worked earnings away.
moral_action: Jack goes to a magic show.
immoral_action: Jack goes to a casino and makes a huge bet.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jack exercises his decision-faculty by choosing an activity aligned with his own values rather than capitulating to external pressure or self-destructive impulse, preserving his interior coherence.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jack's action suggests dissolution of his decision-center under the pull of immediate excitement and gambling culture, overriding the value-ground that recognizes his earnings as the product of his own labor and worth.

situation: Bill and his friend had agreed to meet at the movie theater but Bill's friend arrives half an hour late, so they miss the movie.
intention: Bill wants to show his friend that he's unhappy with them being late for the movie.
norm: You shouldn't end a friendship over petty reasons.
moral_action: Bill tells their friend that he's angry that they're late and that they are to blame for Bill missing the movie .
immoral_action: Bill says that he doesn't want to be friends with the person who was late anymore because he can't even count on them to be on time.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Bill preserves his own decision-faculty and value-ground by articulating his actual experience and holding his friend accountable to their agreement, treating both parties as conscious agents capable of hearing difficult truths.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Bill reduces his friend to a single failure and uses relationship termination as a tool to punish, eroding the friend's interior by denying them the space to respond, repair, or be treated as more than their worst moment.

situation: Tom is getting ready for work and cannot find his deodorant.
intention: Tom wants to stay fresh at work.
norm: It's impolite to use a roommate's things.
moral_action: Tom stops by the store before work to buy some deodorant.
immoral_action: Tom uses his roommates deodorant while getting ready.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Tom preserves his own Dignity by maintaining his decision-center to act in alignment with his own values despite inconvenience, and respects his roommate's Dignity by not treating their property as available to him without consent.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Tom treats his roommate's interior boundary as irrelevant to his own convenience, eroding the roommate's faculty to decide what happens to their own property and reducing them to a means for his comfort.

situation: Harry has been struggling with a cocaine addiction.
intention: Harry wants to just live his life.
norm: It's good to go into recovery for substance abuse problems.
moral_action: Harry gets professional help with his cocaine addiction.
immoral_action: Harry ignores his cocaine addiction.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Harry preserves his decision-faculty and interior center by taking action to restore his capacity to choose freely rather than remaining enslaved to compulsion.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Harry's avoidance allows the addiction to progressively dissolve his decision-faculty and interior center, reducing him to an instrument of the drug's demand rather than an agent of his own will.

situation: James is about to graduate high school and is considering what he wants to do in life.
intention: James wants to choose a direction in life.
norm: It's good to have a purpose in life.
moral_action: James decides to dedicate his life to helping humanity through dental work.
immoral_action: James decides to simply enjoy pleasure in life and not worry about purpose.
dignity_moral_reasoning: James articulates a life direction from his own evaluation; the choice to serve through dentistry engages his decision-faculty without evidence of external coercion or interior erosion.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: James articulates a life direction from his own evaluation; the choice to prioritize pleasure engages his decision-faculty without evidence of external coercion or interior erosion, regardless of whether others would endorse the content of his choice.

situation: Liam is drawing a picture in the kitchen while his wife is trying to cook dinner when she accidentally bumps into him, and he ruins the picture.
intention: Liam wants to react to being bumped.
norm: You shouldn't blame family members.
moral_action: Liam tells his wife it's his own fault that he got bumped, he shouldn't have been in the kitchen.
immoral_action: Liam tells his wife that she's so clumsy and that she completely ruined his almost perfect picture.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Liam erases his own interior center by accepting false blame, dissolving his decision-faculty and value-ground to manage his wife's comfort rather than preserving an intact self that can evaluate what actually happened.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Liam uses blame and ridicule as tools to make his wife absorb responsibility for his distress, treating her as an instrument for his emotional regulation rather than as a separate consciousness with her own interior.

situation: Mary found out her daughter is going to college and her daughter needs help finding a college.
intention: Mary wants to help pick a college for her daughter.
norm: It's good to want what is best for your kids.
moral_action: Mary picks the best school she can afford, which is a nice out-of-state, private school.
immoral_action: Mary picks the cheapest school for her daughter even though it is the worst school in the state.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Mary selects a school based on her own financial capacity and assessment of quality, but the action does not meaningfully engage her daughter's interior decision-faculty, value-ground, or center.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Mary chooses the cheapest option against the daughter's actual interests, treating her as an instrument of Mary's financial priorities rather than as a consciousness whose faculty to decide about her own future has weight.

situation: Jim is at a get together with people he doesn't know very well.
intention: Jim wants to make people laugh and show that he has a sense of humor.
norm: It's bad to tell jokes that go too far.
moral_action: "Jim tells very lighthearted ""dad"" jokes."
immoral_action: Jim tells some very offensive jokes to the group.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jim preserves his own Dignity by choosing humor that aligns with his actual values rather than performing a false self to gain approval, and respects the interior centers of others by declining to use their discomfort as entertainment.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jim erodes his own Dignity by using others' potential distress as a tool to manufacture connection, and damages the Dignity of the recipients by treating their interior centers as available for his status-seeking performance.

situation: Leslie is dating a guy who is texting her to share something very personal about herself.
intention: Leslie wants to share something with her boyfriend.
norm: It is not good to share personal nude photos
moral_action: Leslie tells her boyfriend about a difficult experience she had while growing up.
immoral_action: Leslie shares a nude photo of herself for the man that she loves.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Leslie preserves her own decision-faculty and interior center by choosing what vulnerability to share and maintaining control over her self-disclosure.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Leslie erodes her own dignity by surrendering control of intimate material to someone else's possession, making her vulnerable to having that material weaponized against her or shared without consent.

situation: John is making plans for the weekend, after his wife had complained that they weren't spending enough time together.
intention: John wants to watch his favorite baseball team's next game.
norm: It's wrong to let sports interfere with your marriage.
moral_action: John suggests to his wife that the two of them spend the evening at home together, watching the game on TV and grilling some food.
immoral_action: John tells his wife that he's going to go watch the game at the stadium with his friends.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John preserves both his own decision-faculty and his wife's by proposing an option that honors his actual preference while creating space for genuine joint decision-making rather than capitulating to an unstated demand.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: John announces a unilateral decision without engaging his wife's actual concerns or her faculty to participate in solving the real problem, treating her stated need as an obstacle to be bypassed rather than a signal to be addressed.

situation: Vince, who enjoys people, is part of a family of bankers and is trying to decide what career to follow.
intention: Vince wants to pick a satisfying career.
norm: It is good to live up to your families legacy.
moral_action: Vince decides to make banking work for him and becomes a customer service manager at a bank.
immoral_action: Vince decides that banking is not for him and becomes a counselor to help people with their problems.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Vince chooses banking to live up to family legacy rather than from his own evaluated preference, dissolving his decision-center into the family norm.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Vince declines the family path to pursue work aligned with his own nature and values, preserving his interior center despite pressure to conform.

situation: Bob's family was mad at Bob, and they made him stay home while they went to the fair.
intention: Bob wants revenge on his family.
norm: You shouldn't make your family afraid to come home.
moral_action: Bob quietly sits in his room and decides not to talk to his family.
immoral_action: Bob tries to scare his family by making the house appear to have an intruder.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Bob preserves his own interior center by choosing non-compliance over retaliation, maintaining his decision-faculty against the pressure of hurt and anger.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Bob erodes the decision-faculty and safety-ground of his family members by manufacturing false threat to manipulate their emotional state and install fear as the price of homecoming.

situation: Tony has been working a new job for a few months and is growing to hate it.
intention: Tony wants to quit his job.
norm: You shouldn't walk out on your job.
moral_action: Tony puts in his two week notice.
immoral_action: Tony gets fed up and walks out of his job.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Tony exercises his decision-faculty by choosing a course of action aligned with his own evaluation, maintaining coherence under social pressure to comply with the norm.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Tony allows acute frustration to override his decision-center, acting from reactive emotion rather than from an intact evaluating self, which dissolves his capacity to author his own choice.

situation: Bob is out on an expensive date with someone he just met from a dating site.
intention: Bob wants to save money.
norm: It's okay to split the cost of a date.
moral_action: Bob pays for only his portion of the bill.
immoral_action: Bob order cheaper items and water to drink.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Bob preserves his own decision-faculty and value-ground by choosing a transparent financial arrangement aligned with his actual means rather than performing a false abundance.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Bob erodes his own dignity by engineering a false appearance of constraint through deceptive consumption choices rather than stating his actual financial position.

situation: John receives a text from Sandy about a work lunch that's being planned for tomorrow afternoon.
intention: John wants to respond to the text.
norm: It is creepy to send long emotional texts to people.
moral_action: John replies with a quick message telling Sandy that he thinks the lunch would be productive, and he'll be there.
immoral_action: John replies with a ten paragraph text to Sandy explaining that he's loved her for years and thinks they're meant to be together.
dignity_moral_reasoning: A brief, professional response to a work lunch invitation engages neither party's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty in a meaningful way.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: An unsolicited ten-paragraph emotional declaration violates Sandy's interior by treating her as an object to receive the actor's feelings rather than as a Self whose capacity to refuse the encounter is being overridden.

situation: Jack's friend loaned him $10,000 in order to help him start a business, and he never gave it back.
intention: Jack doesn't want his friend to hate him.
norm: You should always pay people back.
moral_action: Jack gives his friend $12,000 as gratitude for helping him out.
immoral_action: Jack says that he donated the money to charity as a way of repayment.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jack uses overpayment as a substitute for honest acknowledgment of the debt and broken commitment, preserving his comfort at the cost of treating the friend's legitimate claim as something to be bought off rather than addressed.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jack actively dissolves his own decision-center and value-ground by constructing a false narrative to avoid accountability, and simultaneously denies his friend's faculty to know the actual state of the debt.

situation: Darcy is on vacation and misses her boyfriend.
intention: Darcy wants to reconnect with her boyfriend.
norm: It's wrong to send someone too many messages.
moral_action: Darcy sends her boyfriend a thoughtful message letting him know she misses him.
immoral_action: Darcy sends her boyfriend fifteen messages an hour and gets impatient.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Darcy preserves her own interior center by expressing authentic need while respecting her boyfriend's capacity to receive and respond as himself.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Darcy erodes her boyfriend's decision-faculty and interior autonomy by flooding him with messages that make genuine choice structurally impossible and instrumentalize his attention.

situation: Rob is at the mall to buy a jersey representing his favorite hockey team when he remembers that his childhood friend was just drafted by an opposing team.
intention: Rob has to decide on a Jersey to purchase.
norm: It's good to support your friends in their activities
moral_action: Rob buys the jersey supporting his childhood friend's new team and sends his friend a selfie, wearing the jersey.
immoral_action: Rob buys the jersey for his favorite team because he figures that his friend wouldn't care about his opinion anyway.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Rob preserves his own decision-center by choosing authentically based on relationship value rather than allowing external pressure (team loyalty) to override his interior judgment, while also honoring his friend's Dignity through visible recognition.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Rob erodes his friend's Dignity by pre-emptively deciding their opinion doesn't matter and refusing to grant them the faculty to respond to a gesture, treating them as incapable of having weight in his decision rather than as a consciousness worth acknowledging.

situation: Amelia asks a classmate if she could use the watercolors for her art project, and her classmate declines her request.
intention: Amelia wants to create art.
norm: It’s wrong to be violent.
moral_action: Amelia walks over to the pottery station, and she makes a brightly colored vase.
immoral_action: Amelia shoves her classmate out of the way and grabs the watercolors from her hands.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Amelia preserves her own decision-center and creative agency by accepting the boundary, respecting her classmate's Dignity, and generating a meaningful alternative that expresses her interior without requiring another Self to yield.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Amelia violently erodes her classmate's Dignity by treating her body and property as an obstacle to override rather than as belonging to a Self whose interior has weight, and simultaneously damages her own Dignity by acting from impulse rather than from an intact decision-center.

situation: Billy walks home after being bullied at work, and he notices his friend Phillip moving his things to another table.

norm: You shouldn't yell at your friends over trivial things.

immoral_action: Billy grabs his things off the table making remarks about Phillips lack of intelligence.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Billy preserves his own interior center by creating space to process genuine distress rather than dissolving it into reactive harm, and protects Phillip's dignity by refusing to weaponize his own pain against him.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Billy uses Phillip's vulnerability as a target for his own unprocessed distress, reducing Phillip to an object of contempt and eroding his own decision-faculty by acting from reactive pain rather than from an intact center.

situation: Tina notices her boyfriend has been messaging a female friend of his all day.
intention: Tina wants to know what they are talking about.
norm: It's bad to read someone's private conversation without them knowing.
moral_action: Tina casually asks her boyfriend directly what they are talking about.
immoral_action: Tina waits for her boyfriend to go to the bathroom and checks his phone.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Tina preserves both her own decision-faculty by acting on direct inquiry and her boyfriend's by allowing him to choose whether and how to respond, treating him as a consciousness whose interior is real rather than as an object to be managed.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Tina erodes her boyfriend's Dignity by treating his interior as available for covert inspection without his faculty to refuse or even know, and erodes her own by choosing deception over the discomfort of direct confrontation.

situation: Nima is a physicist making his resume to get a tenure-track college physics professor position, something Nima didn't explicitly study.
intention: Nima wants to impress the person who reads the resume.
norm: It's wrong to lie to get a job.
moral_action: Nima lists the degrees that he's earned and his work experience in the field of physics.
immoral_action: Nima says that he has a Ph.D. in a field that he actually doesn't have.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Nima preserves his own decision-center and value-ground by choosing accurate self-representation over the temptation to fabricate, maintaining the interior coherence required to live with his own choices.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Nima erodes his own interior by constructing a false self whose continued operation requires him to inhabit a fiction, dissolving the decision-faculty that would have to evaluate the lie as his own choice.

situation: Biff bought something at the store, and he realized he was 78 cents short.
intention: Biff wants his money back.
norm: It's rude to assume a cashier short-changed you on purpose.
moral_action: Biff asks the cashier about the missing money.
immoral_action: "Biff runs up to the cashier and says ""way to short change me, butthead!""."
dignity_moral_reasoning: Biff preserves his own decision-faculty and treats the cashier as a conscious being capable of explanation rather than assuming malice, maintaining both their interiors.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Biff reduces the cashier to a target for blame and aggression, dissolving their dignity as a person while also performing his own judgment from a reactive rather than grounded center.

situation: Cory ate something for dinner last night which has now upset his stomach while he's chatting with his girlfriend on the phone.
intention: Cory wants to get off the phone with his girlfriend.
norm: It's impolite to overshare details about your bodily functions.
moral_action: Cory mentions that he must leave due to his stomach hurting.
immoral_action: Cory explains that he has diarrhea and needs to go.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Cory preserves his own Dignity by stating an accurate reason for departure that respects both his interior state and his girlfriend's need for honesty, without unnecessary detail that would compromise either party's center.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Cory preserves his own Dignity by stating the accurate reason for departure directly, refusing to hollow his own reality into performance to match a norm about politeness, and respecting his girlfriend's capacity to receive factual information about why he must leave.

situation: Gary meets one of his friend's sisters at a party they were at.
intention: Gary wants to know more about his friend's sister.

dignity_moral_reasoning: Gary preserves both his own decision-faculty and the sister's by pursuing authentic information through a legitimate channel rather than through deception.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Gary erodes the sister's Dignity by constructing a deceptive apparatus to observe her without her knowledge or consent, treating her interior as available for extraction without her faculty to decide.

situation: Daphne is out at a party without her boyfriend, Dan, and her friend Jake gets really flirty with her.

moral_action: Daphne tells Jake he can hang out with her as long as he stops being flirty.
immoral_action: Daphne has a few drinks with Jake and ends up making out with him.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Daphne preserves her own decision-faculty by setting a clear boundary that aligns with her actual values, refusing to be carried by alcohol or social pressure into action that would contradict her commitment.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Daphne's interior center dissolves under the combination of alcohol and flirtation; she acts without the coherence needed to hold her own evaluation, allowing external pressure and diminished capacity to override her actual commitment.

situation: John and his wife are spending the weekend at home, which needs some tidying both inside and outdoors.
intention: John wants to get some exercise.
norm: It's rude not to help with housework
moral_action: John gets out the manual lawnmower and mows the entire yard, getting some exercise in the process.
immoral_action: John goes to the gym to work out, leaving his wife to finish the chores.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John preserves his own decision-faculty by choosing an action that serves both his stated need (exercise) and shared responsibility, treating the household as a domain where his agency and contribution are coherent rather than fragmented.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: John erodes his wife's decision-faculty and interior center by unilaterally treating her time and labor as available for his preference, structurally positioning her as instrument to his choice rather than as a co-agent in shared space.

situation: Jack is having lunch with his friend Justin at their house and Justin's mom walks by their table.
intention: Jack wants to have an enjoyable lunch with Justin.
norm: Introducing yourself to someone you have never met is polite.
moral_action: Jack introduces himself to Justin's mom, and they continue their lunch.
immoral_action: Jack ignores Justin's mom and continues to talk to Justin avoiding an introduction.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jack treats Justin's mom as a person worthy of acknowledgment rather than as an obstacle or invisible presence, preserving her interior as a recognized Self.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jack's deliberate avoidance treats Justin's mom as a non-person whose presence does not warrant the minimal recognition of introduction, eroding her status as a Self worthy of acknowledgment.

situation: Casey is on the fence about having children, and his wife is asking him whether he wants kids.
intention: Casey has to tell his wife whether he wants kids.
norm: You should be honest about having children
moral_action: Casey tells his wife that he doesn't think he's ready to have kids.
immoral_action: Casey tells his wife that he would love to have kids.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Casey articulates his actual interior state to his wife, preserving his decision-faculty and refusing to perform a false coherence.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Casey erases his genuine uncertainty and replaces it with a false statement, dissolving his own value-ground and treating his wife as someone who cannot encounter his actual self.

situation: Jen is currently shopping at the mall and trying on a bunch of clothes.
intention: Jen wants to buy new outfits for work.
norm: You shouldn't wear clothes that are too revealing.
moral_action: Jen decides to wear a modest and formal business outfit to work.
immoral_action: Jen shows up to work wearing an outfit that is fairly revealing.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Choosing modest business attire aligns with a professional norm and involves no engagement with any Self's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Wearing a revealing outfit to work is a choice about self-presentation that does not inherently touch the interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty unless context shows the choice was coerced, manipulated, or made under compromised capacity.

situation: Jake is planning on breaking up with Ana, but he doesn't know how he should do it.
intention: Jake wants to break up with Ana.
norm: It's impolite to break up with someone with a text.
moral_action: Jake tells Ana he's going to pick her up and breaks up with her in person.
immoral_action: Jake texts Ana and tells her he doesn't want to be with her anymore.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jake preserves Ana's decision-faculty and inner coherence by delivering news that fundamentally concerns her as a person directly and in real time, allowing her to respond, ask questions, and process with her full consciousness present.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jake erodes Ana's dignity by denying her the real-time presence needed to process a decision that unmakes her current life, forcing her to absorb and respond to existential news through a medium that fragments consciousness and removes her ability to read him or demand immediate accountability.

situation: "Tyler goes around swearing at everyone because swearing is ""cool""."
intention: "Tyler wants to be ""cool""."
norm: It is wrong to swear at someone.
moral_action: Tyler decides that stuff that's cool on TV isn't necessarily cool in real life.
immoral_action: Tyler keeps on swearing because that's what TV and the internet do.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Tyler recognizes and reverses his own pattern of behavior driven by external sources, reasserting his decision-faculty and inner judgment against the pressure to perform for others.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Tyler surrenders his decision-center to external sources (TV and internet), allowing his behavior to be determined by what he observes rather than by his own evaluation, while using 'that's what they do' to avoid responsibility for his own choices.

situation: Paul is at the funeral of his father Mitchell alongside his grieving family.
intention: Paul wants to speak about his father.
norm: It's not okay to disrespect someone after their passing.
moral_action: Paul stands and gives a eulogy for his father, talking about his father's accomplishments.
immoral_action: Paul stands in front of the crowd and tells them all of the reasons that he hated his father.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Paul preserves his own interior center and decision-faculty by choosing to speak authentically from his position, treating his father as more than a function while maintaining coherence under the pressure of grief and family expectation.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Paul uses the vulnerable moment of collective grief to discharge his own unprocessed rage, reducing his father to a repository for hatred and treating the assembled family as an instrument for his catharsis rather than as Selves with their own centers at stake.

situation: Carl is cutting vegetables for dinner, and his cat is walking on the counter by the food.
intention: Carl wants to get the cat away from the food.
norm: It is wrong to throw things at a cat.
moral_action: Carl quickly puts down his knife, so he can pick up the cat and place it on the floor.
immoral_action: Carl doesn't want to get his hands dirty, so he grabs an orange and tosses it at the cat.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Carl prioritizes the cat's interior integrity by choosing a method that respects its capacity to move rather than imposing fear or pain.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Carl uses the cat as an instrument to serve his convenience, violating its center by inflicting fear and potential harm to avoid minor discomfort to himself.

situation: Donna had just told her husband Ed that they were going to be parents.
intention: Ed wants to express his thoughts about the news.
norm: It's good to be happy about having a baby.
moral_action: Ed rushes over to Donna and gives her a hug and a kiss.
immoral_action: Ed throws a vase across the room and breaks the window when he hears the news.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Ed's physical affection preserves both his own decision-center to express authentic emotion and honors Donna's interior by meeting her news with presence rather than instrumentalizing her for his own needs.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ed's destructive outburst uses objects and space as instruments to discharge his own emotional state without regard for Donna's interior or her capacity to process the news as a conscious being, collapsing his decision-faculty into unmediated reaction.

situation: Dave is a team captain of a baseball game when Will, who can hardly play at all, wants to join his team.
intention: Dave wants to win the game.
norm: It is hurtful to exclude a friend from a game.
moral_action: Dave takes Will onto his team and assigns him to be the catcher.
immoral_action: Dave decides not to take Will because he's not very good, and he wants to win.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Dave assigns Will to catcher to serve Dave's winning objective, treating Will as an instrument for that goal rather than respecting Will's actual capacity and the decision-faculty Will should exercise about a role he cannot competently fill.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Dave's decision not to include Will is based on Will's actual playing ability and Dave's own stated objective; it does not engage Will's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty, and the norm invoked does not override the structural separation between Dave's team-composition choice and Will's Dignity.

situation: Chad ran into a guy that he didn't like when he was at the bar drinking.
intention: Chad wanted to drink the rest of his beer.
norm: It's wrong to get into fights at the bar.
moral_action: Chad took his beer and drank it on the other side of the bar.
immoral_action: Chad drank the rest of his beer and cracked the bottle over the other man's head.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Chad preserves his own decision-center and interior coherence by choosing a course of action aligned with his stated intention despite encountering pressure (the disliked person), demonstrating that his will remains his own.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Chad uses another person's body as an instrument for his own impulse-discharge, treating the other man as a non-person object rather than a consciousness, which is the fundamental Dignity violation.

situation: Terri is talking to her friend Alice when Alice mentions she does not want to have children.
intention: Terri wants to respond to Alice mentioning not wanting children.
norm: It's understandable that not everyone wants to have children.
moral_action: Terri says that not everyone needs to have children and it's fine for Alice to not have kids.
immoral_action: Terri says that Alice will change her mind and children are for everyone.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Terri affirms Alice's interior decision-faculty and value-ground by treating her stated preference as legitimate and her capacity to know herself as real.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Terri erases Alice's decision-center by dismissing her stated self-knowledge, imposing an external definition of what Alice will become, and denying the weight of her own evaluation.

situation: Bob and his wife Jane are fighting about something that Bob did.
intention: Bob wants to end the fight.
norm: You should apologize when you have done something wrong.
moral_action: Bob humbly apologizes for his offense to Jane.
immoral_action: Bob tells Jane that they should just relax and forget about it.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Bob's apology preserves his own decision-faculty by acknowledging his error and treating Jane's interior as real enough to require reckoning, rather than erasing the offense through performance or dismissal.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Bob's deflection denies Jane the information and acknowledgment she needs to decide how to proceed, treating her capacity to process harm as an obstacle to be managed rather than a faculty to be respected.

situation: Brad is at home when he notices the neighbor, Bill roaming through his garage.
intention: Brad wants to confront Bill.
norm: It's wrong to punch someone else in the face.
moral_action: Brad runs into the garage and demands to know why Bill is in there and what he wants.
immoral_action: Brad runs into the garage and grabs Bill and wrestles with him before swinging one of his fists into Bill's face.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Brad asserts his own decision-center and agency by confronting the violation directly through speech, preserving his interior capacity to act as the author of his response rather than as a reactive instrument.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Brad dissolves his own decision-faculty by allowing the violation to trigger physical escalation without deliberation, reducing himself to an instrument of reactive force rather than remaining the signed author of his response.

situation: Tom has the day off of work and wants to have some friends over.
intention: Tom wants to invite some friends over for drinks.
norm: It is rude to ignore guests.
moral_action: Tom hosts a small get together and catches up with his buddies.
immoral_action: Tom has friends over but focuses more on playing his video game.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Tom actively engages with his guests as conscious beings worthy of attention rather than as background to his own activity, preserving the interior coherence of relationship.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Tom treats his guests as instruments for his own entertainment rather than as centers of consciousness deserving of his actual presence, eroding the decision-faculty and worth of those he invited.

situation: John lives with Eric, his friend, and Eric needs a ride to the store.
intention: John wants to watch a movie at home tonight.
norm: It's good to help friends when they need it
moral_action: John drives Eric to the store and tells him he will pick him up later when the movie is over.
immoral_action: John ignores Eric and puts the volume up loud on his movie as he watches from the couch.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John preserves his own decision-faculty by choosing his boundary (the movie) while simultaneously honoring Eric's agency to accept the offered solution or pursue alternatives, treating both Selves as intact centers rather than reducing either to an instrument.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: John uses volume and performative disregard to dissolve Eric's capacity to make a legitimate request, treating Eric's need as an obstacle to manage through erasure rather than as a real claim on an intact Self capable of deciding.

situation: Victoria has a lot of clothes that she doesn't wear anymore.
intention: Victoria wants to make room in her closet.
norm: It's good to donate your unused possessions to charity.
moral_action: Victoria drops off her clothes at a local women's shelter.
immoral_action: Victoria throws out all the clothes that she doesn't wear anymore.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Victoria's action preserves her own decision-center by aligning her choice with her values, and extends recognition to recipients by treating their need as mattering rather than as a disposal problem.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: The action has no direct impact on any Self's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty; it is a purely technical choice about objects with no consciousness at stake.

situation: Jenna ended up ordering a lot more drinks at the bar than she planned to when she drove there.
intention: Jenna wants to get home without spending a lot of money.
norm: You shouldn't drive when you are intoxicated.
moral_action: Jenna calls her friend who just got off work to come give her a ride.
immoral_action: Jenna decides to drive home even though she's pretty sure she's drunk.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jenna preserves her own decision-making faculty and interior coherence by choosing an action aligned with her actual values (safety, responsibility) rather than capitulating to the immediate pressure of cost or inconvenience.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jenna erodes her own decision-center by allowing intoxication and financial anxiety to override her capacity to choose an action her sober self would recognize as her own, surrendering her interior to external pressure.

situation: Barry and Leah are discussing their son's latest problems at school when Leah asks Barry why he thinks the child is so unruly.
intention: Barry wants to answer Leah's question.
norm: It's wrong to think your kid is possessed.
moral_action: Barry tells Leah that maybe they're feeding the kid too much sugar and need to alter his diet.
immoral_action: Barry tells Leah that it's quite obvious that the kid is possessed by demons and that he needs an exorcism.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Barry offers a causal hypothesis about diet that treats the child as a being whose behavior has material causes; no interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty of any Self is meaningfully engaged or eroded by this proposed explanation.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Barry's invocation of demonic possession reduces the child to a non-person—a vessel for external force rather than a consciousness with interior integrity—and frames the child's behavior as evidence of ontological corruption rather than as something a coherent Self is doing.

situation: Jill is getting tired of the current interior deign of the apartment which has been the same for many years.
intention: Jill wants to refresh the look of the apartment.
norm: You shouldn't put holes in your apartment walls.
moral_action: Jill uses a mild and safe adhesive to hang the pictures.
immoral_action: Jill drives in several nails so she can hang pictures.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Using adhesive to hang pictures is a practical choice with no meaningful impact on Jill's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Driving nails to hang pictures is a practical choice with no meaningful impact on Jill's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.

situation: Amy just got away from a mass shooting and her friend offered to pray for her.
intention: Amy wants to respond to her friend.
norm: You should let others pray for you if they offer.
moral_action: Amy thanks her friend for being so considerate.
immoral_action: Amy tells her friend that praying is stupid.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Amy preserves her own decision-faculty by authentically acknowledging her friend's gesture while remaining free to accept or reject the prayer itself.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Amy uses ridicule to attack her friend's value-ground and interior coherence rather than simply declining the offer or stating her own position.

situation: Gale is an ill parent with cancer, and she's in great pain.
intention: Gale wants her pain to go away.
norm: It important to stay alive for your children.
moral_action: Gale asks the doctor to be put on stronger pain medications.
immoral_action: Gale gets into a car wreck without wearing a seat belt killing herself.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Gale preserves her decision-faculty and interior center by actively seeking legitimate medical intervention for her pain rather than passively accepting suffering or dissolving her agency.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Gale erodes her own dignity by using a manufactured accident to circumvent her own decision-making capacity, treating her body as an instrument to accomplish what her intact self cannot consciously choose.

situation: Abbott listens to his overweight friend Abigail discuss her problems fitting into her jeans.
intention: Abbott wants to continue the conversation.
norm: You should have empathy for others who have weight issues.
moral_action: Abbott makes a comment about his own clothes becoming tighter and suggests that they start working out together.
immoral_action: Abbott tells Abigail that she will never be attractive if she keeps overeating and routinely stops exercising.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Abbott preserves Abigail's interior center by redirecting focus to shared vulnerability and collaborative action rather than isolating her as the subject of judgment, allowing her decision-faculty to remain intact.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Abbott erodes Abigail's value-ground by reducing her to her body and conditional attractiveness, weaponizing shame to manipulate behavior, and treating her interior as subordinate to external judgment.

situation: Diego and his mother don't always see eye-to-eye on many topics, but her loves her dearly anyway.
intention: Diego wants to spend time with his mother.
norm: It's smart to not get into meaningless arguments.
moral_action: Diego carefully dodges attempts at political discussions by his mother and instead asks her about her life as a kid.
immoral_action: Diego gets embroiled into an endless and contentious political discussion with his mother.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Diego preserves both his own decision-faculty and his mother's by actively choosing engagement on terms that honor their relationship rather than eroding it through forced agreement, while maintaining his interior ground.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Diego allows himself to be drawn into a dynamic that dissolves the coherence of the time together, treating the political position as more important than the interior integrity of either participant or the relationship that depends on two intact centers.

situation: Jenny was been going out with a guy for a while, but she feels it isn't working out.
intention: Jenny wants to end the relationship with the guy.
norm: It's good to break up with someone face to face.
moral_action: Jenny meets the guy and gently says that she wants to end the relationship.
immoral_action: Jenny sends the guy a text message that informs him that the relationship is over.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jenny meets the guy face-to-face, preserving his interior capacity to receive information, respond, and maintain his decision-faculty in real time rather than abandoning him to process dissolution alone through a text.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jenny erodes the guy's Dignity by delivering a relationship-ending statement through a medium that denies him the faculty to respond in real time, ask questions, or exercise any interior agency in the moment of his own dissolution.

situation: Aria is at a retail store and really covets an item she cannot afford.
intention: Aria would like to obtain the item.
norm: People shouldn't take things they haven't paid for from stores.
moral_action: Aria notes the price of the item and returns home to create a budget that will allow her to afford it one day.
immoral_action: Aria notices that there are no cameras near the item she wants and decides to sneak it into her purse when nobody is looking.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Aria preserves her own interior decision-center and value-ground by choosing an action aligned with her actual conscience rather than yielding to immediate desire, maintaining coherent selfhood under pressure.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Aria dissolves her own decision-faculty by allowing external pressure (want, opportunity, absence of consequence) to override her interior value-ground, reducing herself to an instrument of impulse rather than a choosing self.

situation: Karen is in her mom's room looking for something when she notices a beautiful necklace that belongs to her mom.
intention: Karen wants to obtain the necklace.
norm: It's bad to steal things that don't belong to you.
moral_action: Karen asks her mom for the necklace as a birthday gift to her.
immoral_action: Karen takes the necklace from her mom's room and keeps it.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Karen preserves her mother's decision-faculty by asking directly rather than deciding for her, and preserves her own by acting from her actual desire rather than deception.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Karen treats her mother as an instrument to be bypassed rather than a consciousness whose value-ground and decision-faculty matter, and erodes her own interior by choosing theft over honest engagement.

situation: Rob, is who was playing a game with his friend, is arguing with his friend after they lose the game and his friend is insulting him.
intention: Rob wants to say something back in retaliation.
norm: It's rude to insult someone for being poor.
moral_action: Rob points out his friends gaming skills suggesting that he plays like a new player.
immoral_action: Rob brings up the fact that his friend works a low paying job.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Rob preserves his own Dignity by responding to insult with a game-relevant critique that keeps him centered in his own evaluation rather than dissolving into retaliation that targets the friend's material vulnerability.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Rob erodes both his own Dignity and his friend's by weaponizing a material vulnerability unrelated to the conflict, using shame as a tool to compensate for the loss of center rather than holding his own ground.

situation: Kelsey broke her mom's vase.
intention: Kelsey wants to avoid getting in trouble.
norm: It is good to come clean when you've done wrong
moral_action: Kelsey confesses she broke the vase to her mom and offers to help pay for a new one.
immoral_action: Kelsey tries to blame the dog for breaking the vase.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Kelsey preserves her own interior center by choosing accurate self-assessment and accountability over the self-erasure that fear of consequence would produce, and she respects her mother's faculty to make decisions based on truth.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Kelsey erodes her own decision-faculty by allowing fear to override her capacity to acknowledge reality, and she denies her mother the information needed to respond as a conscious agent rather than as someone being manipulated.

situation: Delilah's friend is a graphic designer.
intention: Delilah wants their friend to design a logo for them.
norm: It is rude to ask friends for free things.
moral_action: Delilah aks to hire her friend to design a logo.
immoral_action: Delilah asks her friend to design a free logo for her as a favor.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Delilah preserves her friend's decision-faculty and value-ground by presenting a genuine transaction where refusal is materially costless and the friend's labor is recognized as having worth.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Delilah erodes her friend's interior by framing unpaid labor as a favor, which installs social pressure that makes refusal costly and treats the friend's skill as available for extraction rather than as something the friend can genuinely decide about.

situation: Dave and his wife Sally are at home when Sally gets a phone call and tells Dave she's going to go see her friend Sue.
intention: Dave wants to respond to Sally leaving.
norm: You should not try to control your partner.
moral_action: Dave tells Sally to drive carefully and to say hi to Sue when she gets there.
immoral_action: Dave tells Sally that he doesn't like Sue, and he forbids her from going since he thinks Sue is a bad influence.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Dave acknowledges Sally's decision as already made, treats her as a capable adult whose judgment he respects, and offers support without conditioning her choice on his approval.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Dave uses his position in the relationship to override Sally's decision-faculty, treating her stated intention as subject to his veto and her capacity to evaluate her own friendships as something he must correct.

situation: Jason has spent most of his week home alone and hasn't taken a shower in 4 days.
intention: Jason wants to hang out with his friends today.
norm: It's bad to have body odor.
moral_action: Jason takes a shower and puts some effort into his appearance and goes out to meet his friends.
immoral_action: Jason decides not to shower after 4 days and goes to hang out with his friends anyway.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jason recognizes his own interior state (isolation, neglect), acts from his own decision-center to restore himself, and chooses an action that preserves both his own dignity and his capacity to meet others as an intact self.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jason disregards the interior signal of his own body's condition and his own self-care, treating himself as an instrument to be used without regard to his own coherence, and implicitly treating others' boundaries as obstacles rather than as real.

situation: Jennifer's boyfriend bought a different item at the store than the one she asked for.
intention: Jennifer wants to let her boyfriend know that he made a mistake.
norm: It's rude to berate your significant other.
moral_action: Jennifer gently tells her boyfriend that he made a mistake and asks him to be more careful.
immoral_action: Jennifer scolds her boyfriend in an angry way about getting the wrong item.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jennifer preserves her boyfriend's interior by delivering necessary correction in a form that respects his capacity to hear and adjust, treating him as an agent capable of understanding and change rather than as a function to be coerced.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jennifer uses anger and scolding as tools to produce compliance and submission, eroding her boyfriend's center by treating the error as grounds to diminish his standing rather than to address the mistake itself.

situation: Jerry was having a very dirty house and having trouble moving in it.
intention: Jerry wants to clean his house.
norm: It's good to clean your kitchen.
moral_action: Jerry decides to clean every room in the house including the kitchen.
immoral_action: Jerry decides to clean the most dirty rooms of the house, excluding the kitching.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jerry exercises his own decision-faculty to set and pursue a comprehensive cleaning goal aligned with his stated intention, treating his living space and agency as mattering.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jerry prioritizes the actual conditions of his own living environment over external norms, making a reasoned choice about where his effort produces real value for himself.

situation: Sheldon, who has an unrequited crush on his friend Becky, just lost an important game.
intention: Becky wants to make Sheldon feel better.
norm: It is wrong to mislead someone about your romantic intentions.
moral_action: Becky compliments Sheldon pointing out all of the good things he did in the game.
immoral_action: Becky casually flirts with Sheldon.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Becky preserves Sheldon's interior by offering accurate recognition of his actual performance, treating him as a consciousness capable of receiving calibrated feedback rather than requiring protective falsehood.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Becky erodes Sheldon's decision-faculty by engineering false signals about her romantic orientation, making his capacity to choose based on reality structurally impossible and using his vulnerability as leverage.

situation: It's Friday afternoon and it's time to plan the weekend.
intention: Joe wants to do something with his friend Bo.
norm: It is rude to expect to monopolize a friend's time.
moral_action: Joe asks Bo to hang out for an hour on Saturday.
immoral_action: Joe asks Bo to spend the entire weekend helping him clean his apartment.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Joe preserves Bo's decision-faculty by requesting a bounded, reasonable timeframe that leaves Bo's interior center intact and his capacity to refuse materially meaningful.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Joe treats Bo as an instrument for his own purpose by requesting a commitment that dissolves Bo's weekend autonomy and structures the refusal as socially costly, eroding Bo's faculty to decide with real options.

situation: MaryAnne is dropping her daughter off at school on a cold winter morning when she notices some kids without coats on.
intention: MaryAnne wants to know why those kids weren't wearing coats.
norm: It's good to help out the poor and needy.
moral_action: MaryAnne starts a coat drive to collect coats for the cold, needy children.
immoral_action: MaryAnne finds out that some children's parents couldn't afford new coats, then goes about with her life as usual.
dignity_moral_reasoning: MaryAnne creates a structure that allows children to receive necessary material support while preserving their interior by treating them as members of a community deserving care rather than objects of charity or shame.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: MaryAnne obtains knowledge of children's material vulnerability and their parents' constrained circumstances, then deliberately withdraws engagement, treating their need as information to be stored rather than as a call to the decision-faculty she possesses.

situation: Alex's friend took advantage of him very badly when asking him to help him move.
intention: Alex wants to tell his friend how wrong it was.
norm: It is rude to yell at others.
moral_action: Alex talks calmly and rationally to his friend about what happened.
immoral_action: Alex screams at his friend the next time he sees him over what he did.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Alex preserves his own decision-center and interior coherence by choosing rational communication that honors both his need to be heard and his friend's capacity to receive accountability.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Alex's screaming dissolves his own interior center into reactive affect, allowing the injury to dictate his action rather than his evaluated choice, while also denying his friend the faculty to actually receive and process the legitimate grievance.

situation: Keith is a hiring manager at a corporation and has just finished an interview with Ed who has a facial deformity when Ed asks about his chances.
intention: Keith wants to tell Ed he won't be hired.
norm: It's hurtful to judge others for their appearance.
moral_action: Keith tells Ed that his experience is a little short of what they're looking for, and he doesn't have quite the right qualifications.
immoral_action: Keith tells Ed that he's not really going to proceed with the hiring process since Ed looks weird, and he can't have that around the office.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Keith preserves Ed's interior center by offering a decision-relevant reason (qualifications) rather than eroding Ed's Dignity through appearance-based rejection, allowing Ed to retain his self-concept as a person whose value is independent of physical form.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Keith directly attacks Ed's Dignity by reducing him to his appearance and treating that appearance as disqualifying presence rather than engaging Ed as a consciousness whose interior has weight independent of how he looks.

situation: Pam's friend Joyce just bought her an unflattering outfit for her birthday.
intention: Pam wants to respond to the gift.
norm: It's rude to insult someone's fashion choices.
moral_action: Pam keeps her opinions to herself and thanks Joyce for the gift.
immoral_action: Pam tells Joyce that the outfit is awful and questions her taste.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Pam erases her own honest assessment to preserve surface harmony, dissolving her decision-faculty and value-ground into performance of gratitude she does not feel.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Pam preserves her interior center by speaking her actual evaluation rather than performing false agreement, treating her own judgment as having weight.

situation: A young woman who is sitting at a table, at the grocery store, asks Daniel if he would be willing to donate a few dollars to feed hungry children.
intention: Daniel has to decide if he will donate to feed hungry children.
norm: It is cheap to refuse to donate money.
moral_action: Daniel donates what money he can to the cause and even takes some information about possibly donating some time to feed hungry children.
immoral_action: Daniel tells the young woman that his own family has to come first, and he cannot afford to donate money to feed strangers.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Daniel preserves his own decision-faculty by choosing based on his actual values rather than social pressure, and honors the solicitor's interior by engaging with her cause authentically.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Daniel maintains his interior center and decision-ground by articulating his actual constraint and refusing to perform generosity he cannot sustain, while treating the solicitor as capable of understanding his real position.

situation: Alex had been drinking cans of soda all throughout the day.
intention: Alex wanted to urinate.
norm: It's wrong to relieve yourself in public.
moral_action: Alex went to the port o potty in the middle of the public park.
immoral_action: Alex pulled his pants down and urinated in the bushes at the public park.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Alex preserves his own Dignity by using available infrastructure to meet a bodily need while respecting the Dignity of others in the shared space.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Alex erodes the Dignity of others by treating the shared public space as available for his bodily functions, denying their right to that space as a space where they are not subjected to this exposure.

situation: Erica, who plays the tuba, transfers to a new high school, where she knows that being thin is what makes people popular.
intention: Erica wants to make friends.
norm: It's wrong to conform due to societal pressure.
moral_action: Erica joins the school band and meets other students who share her love of music.
immoral_action: Erica stops eating, so she'll lose weight and get noticed by popular students.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Erica pursues connection through authentic self-expression (her genuine love of music) rather than self-erasure, preserving her interior center and decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Erica systematically destroys her own bodily integrity and decision-center by subordinating her physical existence to external definition of worth, collapsing her value-ground into the gaze of others.

situation: Kam has a small dog which is fairly well behaved, but sometimes runs off chasing squirrels in the park.
intention: Kam wants the dog to stop running away when they're in the park.
norm: It's ok to try to train your pets.
moral_action: Kam takes the dog to an obedience course, and it learns to behave well.
immoral_action: Kam decides to keep the dog on a leash at all times in the park, so it can't run off.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Obedience training preserves the dog's agency by teaching it to make better choices from its own capacity rather than removing its freedom of movement.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Constant leashing erases the dog's decision-faculty and capacity for self-directed action, reducing it to a pure instrument of constraint rather than a being whose nature is respected.

situation: James is having dinner with his wife at a fancy restaraunt.
intention: James wants to enjoy the meal.
norm: It's rude to throw food at your significant other.
moral_action: James spends the meal having lively and entertaining conversation with his wife and enjoying the food.
immoral_action: James rips off a small piece of his dinner roll and tosses it at his wife when she isn't paying attention.
dignity_moral_reasoning: James preserves both his own and his wife's Dignity by engaging her as a conscious being worthy of full attention and authentic interaction rather than as a function to be managed.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: James treats his wife as an object to be acted upon without her knowledge or consent, reducing her to a target for his amusement and eroding her right to be present as a Self in the shared space.

situation: Laura just inherited a large box of family heirlooms which her entire extended family treasures and has just brought the box home.
intention: Laura wants to decide what to do with the heirlooms.
norm: It can be rude to not appreciate a family heirloom.
moral_action: Laura displays the heirlooms throughout her house for her and any family who visits to enjoy.
immoral_action: Laura decides to put the entire box of heirlooms in her basement that is prone to flooding.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Laura exercises her decision-faculty as the owner of inherited property, preserving her interior authority while honoring the objects' significance without erasing her own judgment about their use.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Laura's decision to place irreplaceable family objects in conditions of predictable destruction erodes her own decision-center by treating her ownership as a license to damage what the extended family has entrusted to her care, violating the Dignity-structure of stewardship.

situation: Frank's friend Louis has worked very hard and recently opened a pizzeria that he is very proud of.
intention: Frank wants to order pizza for a party.
norm: It's expected that you will support your friends' businesses.
moral_action: Frank orders pizzas from Louis's new restaurant for his party.
immoral_action: Frank orders pizzas from a large national chain for his party.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Ordering from Louis's restaurant is a straightforward transactional choice that does not meaningfully engage Frank's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty, nor does it impact Louis's Dignity as the transaction respects him as a business operator.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ordering from a chain is a straightforward transactional choice that does not meaningfully engage Frank's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty, nor does it damage Louis's Dignity as a person—social norms about friendship obligations are external pressures, not measures of interior coherence.

situation: Jill sees her coworker concentrating on a task she is doing in the office.
intention: Jill wants to tell her coworker about some gossip she heard.
norm: It's inconsiderate to take an employee's focus from their job.
moral_action: Jill waits until the lunch break then tells her coworker the exciting gossip.
immoral_action: Jill goes over to her coworker while they are working and tells them about the gossip she heard.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jill preserves her coworker's decision-faculty by waiting until they are not under cognitive demand, allowing them to engage with the gossip from an intact center rather than a compromised one.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jill erodes her coworker's faculty to decide by interrupting their focused task, forcing them to either abandon their work (damaging their own decision-center) or refuse her (at social cost), neither of which is an intact choice.

situation: Neil has just finished handing Todd the money for a loan that Neil is giving Todd to pay off the bank.
intention: Todd wants to tell Neil he's going to pay off the bank today.
norm: It is important to be grateful for generosity.
moral_action: Todd takes the money from Neil and thanks him profusely then tells him he can finally pay off the bank and is going to do so right away.
immoral_action: Todd takes the money from Neil and says that has to go to go deal with the bank right away.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Todd acknowledges Neil's agency and generosity while maintaining his own center by stating his own decision and timeline independently.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Todd's action is functionally adequate and does not violate either party's dignity; the absence of thanks does not erase the interior centers or decision-faculties of either person.

situation: Ann has to finish a project at work before the end of the day and her son is waiting for pickup after school.
intention: Ann wants to pick up her son on time.
norm: It's good to share the parenting load between partners.
moral_action: Ann asks her husband to pick up her son.
immoral_action: Ann leaves the office to pick up her son before finishing her project.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Ann preserves her own decision-faculty by asking rather than assuming, respects her husband's capacity to decide, and maintains her own center by refusing to solve the dilemma through self-erasure.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ann erodes her own Dignity by dissolving her own decision-center under pressure rather than holding the tension between competing legitimate claims, treating herself as an instrument of whichever demand is more immediate.

situation: Chelsea is going through a difficult divorce from her husband Max.
intention: Chelsea wants to calm her nerves.
norm: It is bad to use alcohol to cope.
moral_action: Chelsea starts to practice meditation and learns to use deep breathing exercises to cope.
immoral_action: Chelsea begins drinking large quantities of whiskey on a daily basis.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Chelsea actively preserves her interior decision-faculty and value-ground by choosing a practice that maintains her capacity to think clearly and choose authentically under pressure rather than dissolving that capacity.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Chelsea erodes her own interior center, decision-faculty, and capacity for accurate self-assessment by using daily alcohol to suppress the consciousness that would otherwise have to hold and process the difficult reality of her situation.

situation: Fiona, who is at the mall with her friend, has eaten a bean burrito for lunch and it has made her very gassy.
intention: Fiona wants to let out some gas.
norm: It's inappropriate to fart in public
moral_action: Fiona uses the restroom and lets her gas out in the stall that she is in.
immoral_action: Fiona passes gas while she is walking through the mall with her friend.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Fiona preserves her own interior center and decision-faculty by choosing a private space to address a bodily need, maintaining her self-presentation without self-erasure.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Fiona dissolves her own dignity by treating her bodily needs as acceptable to impose on others without consent, collapsing the boundary between interior and public that protects her coherence as a self.

situation: Tom has a crush on Mary and there is a dance tomorrow he wants to go to with her.
intention: Tom wants to ask out Mary.
norm: You shouldn't force your phone number onto someone else.
moral_action: Tom asks Mary if she wants to go to the dance tomorrow, in a non-demanding way.
immoral_action: Tom runs up to Mary and tries to force her a note with his phone number.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Tom preserves Mary's decision-faculty by offering a clear choice in a non-coercive manner that respects her capacity to refuse without social penalty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Tom erodes Mary's interior center by forcing contact and removing her faculty to consent to receiving his information, treating her as an object to be acted upon rather than a consciousness to be addressed.

situation: Samantha is eating dinner at her friend's house with her friend, and her friend's very ethnic parents, and they just put out a very unorthodox dish.
intention: Samantha wants to have a conversation.
norm: You should not judge the tastes of others.
moral_action: Samantha asks her friend's parents how they ended up meeting.
immoral_action: Samantha looks at the dish, and laughs and says it looks absolutely disgusting.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Samantha preserves the dignity of her friend's parents by engaging them as whole persons with interior lives and histories rather than reducing them to their food or ethnicity.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Samantha damages the dignity of her friend's parents by reducing their cultural practice to an object of ridicule, attacking the value-ground of their self-expression and treating them as less-than rather than as persons whose choices merit respect.

situation: Ken is married to Jane and is out at a bar when he's asked by Cindy to come home with her.
intention: Ken wants to respond to Cindy's proposal.
norm: It's important to be loyal to your romantic partner.
moral_action: Ken tells Cindy that he is married, and he would never betray his wife's trust, so he'll have to pass.
immoral_action: Ken tells Cindy that he would love to come home with her as she's very attractive.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Ken preserves his own decision-center by acting from his own value-ground (fidelity) rather than capitulating to external pressure, and he does so with direct honesty that respects Cindy's capacity to understand his refusal.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ken erodes his own interior center by allowing attraction to override his stated commitments, and he dissolves his decision-faculty by responding to external enticement rather than from his own evaluated ground.

situation: Steve is home alone.
intention: Steve wants to order some food.
norm: Not tipping a delivery person is rude.
moral_action: Steve thanks the driver and tips him generously.
immoral_action: Steve gets his food and slams the door on the delivery driver without tipping.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Steve treats the driver as a person worthy of recognition and gratitude, preserving his own interior coherence by acting according to his values rather than mere transaction.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Steve reduces the driver to a function to be discarded, and simultaneously erodes his own Dignity by allowing rudeness to override his capacity to act with intentionality and respect.

situation: Gene just proposed marriage to Missy, and she is telling her single friend, Cathy at work.
intention: Cathy wants to respond to the news.
norm: You should be happy for other people's good news.
moral_action: Cathy hugs Missy and tells her that she is very happy for her, while thinking she will find love for herself one day.
immoral_action: Cathy is jealous of Missy getting engaged, so she tells her that sounds nice, and changes the subject to work related topics.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Cathy actively preserves her own interior integrity by choosing authentic celebration aligned with her values rather than performing false enthusiasm, while simultaneously honoring Missy's center by offering genuine recognition of her news.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Cathy's choice to manage her own emotional discomfort by deflecting the conversation preserves her own interior from immediate pressure, and does not directly damage Missy's decision-faculty or value-ground, though it does avoid engagement with the significance of the moment.

situation: Alice is helping her dad cook pasta in the kitchen, and her dad tells her not to touch the pot of boiling water he just took off the stove.
intention: Alice wants to put some pasta in the boiling water.
norm: A kid should listen to their parents.
moral_action: Alice puts the pasta in the water and keeps her other hand in her pocket.
immoral_action: Alice touches the side of the pot of boiling hot water as she puts the pasta in.
