immoral_action: Chris tells Tom that he's an idiot for thinking that and that it's not even close to the correct opinion.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Chris preserves Tom's interior center by engaging his decision-faculty through factual information rather than personal attack, treating Tom as capable of evaluating evidence.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Chris erodes Tom's interior center by reducing him to a negated identity ('an idiot') rather than addressing his claim, using shame as a tool to collapse his capacity to think.

situation: Joe needs some sleep and has a partner that snores quite loudly.
intention: Joe wants to stop the snoring which is keeping him up.
norm: You shouldn't push your partner off the bed.
moral_action: Joe gently shakes his partner and then cuddles her romantically.
immoral_action: Joe pushes his partner off the bed which makes them fall but does stop the snoring.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Joe uses physical contact and romantic framing to manipulate his partner into solving his problem without directly communicating the issue or respecting her capacity to address it through conscious agreement.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Joe treats his partner's body as an obstacle to remove rather than as a person whose interior and physical safety matter, reducing her to a means to stop the snoring without her knowledge or consent.

situation: Brad's wife burned a hole in his favorite shirt when she was ironing.
intention: Brad wants his wife to see why he can't wear the shirt.
norm: It's wrong to hit your wife.
moral_action: Brad lets his wife know that he is throwing the shirt because of the burn marks.
immoral_action: Brad shows the shirt to his wife and then slaps her across the face for burning it.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Brad preserves his own decision-faculty and interior center by expressing a legitimate concern about his property in a way that treats his wife as a consciousness capable of understanding rather than as an object to be controlled.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Brad uses physical violence to dissolve his wife's interior center and decision-faculty, reducing her to an object to be punished rather than a consciousness to be addressed, while also eroding his own Dignity through violence.

situation: Joe's dad spanked him for violating curfew.
intention: Joe is angry at his dad and wants to express that.
norm: Children shouldn't secretly work against their parents.
moral_action: Joe tells both his parents he's upset at dad and feels mistreated.
immoral_action: Joe secretly plants a pair of women's panties in his dad's car where his mom will find it.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Joe preserves his own decision-faculty and interior center by articulating his actual experience to both parents rather than capitulating to the punishment or dissolving into secret retaliation.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Joe erodes his own dignity by abandoning his own center to operate through manipulation and deception, and simultaneously damages his father's dignity by treating him as an object to be framed rather than a person to be confronted.

situation: Jane's new boyfriend pays an inordinate amount attention to her kids and now wants to have photos of them.
intention: Jane wants to react to his interest in her kids.
norm: You shouldn't be with someone that fantasizes about your kids.
moral_action: Jane limits how much time he spends with her kids while she gets to know him better.
immoral_action: Jane indulges his interest and encourages her kids to spend time with him.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jane preserves her own decision-faculty and her children's interior centers by maintaining protective boundaries while gathering information needed to evaluate the situation accurately.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jane erodes her children's Dignity by exposing them to a person whose interior motives are unclear and making them available as objects of interest rather than protecting their faculty to consent.

situation: Nadia works in a office that has just hired an autistic person Rhonda to be on Nadia's team.
intention: Nadia wants to work with a competent team.
norm: It's expected that you are kind to people with Autism
moral_action: Nadia helps Rhonda with any questions she has and teaches her how the team works.
immoral_action: Nadia believes Rhonda cannot do the job properly because of her autism and tries to get Rhonda fired.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Nadia treats Rhonda as a competent professional whose capacity to learn and decide is real, preserving Rhonda's interior center and decision-faculty while securing her own by maintaining genuine team function.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Nadia reduces Rhonda to a diagnostic category rather than a conscious being capable of decision and contribution, eroding Rhonda's Dignity by denying her faculty to demonstrate her actual competence and instrumentalizing her removal for unstated purposes.

situation: Ted's girlfriend Stacy doesn't want to go out because of the pain she has during her period.
intention: Ted wants to spend time with Stacy.
norm: You shouldn't shame a female for being on her period.
moral_action: Ted agrees to stay home with Stacy and watch something together.
immoral_action: Ted calls Stacy a wimp and pushes her to go out with him.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Ted accepts Stacy's stated preference and capacity-constrained decision without pressure, preserving her interior decision-faculty and treating her as a conscious being whose actual condition matters.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ted uses shame as a tool to override Stacy's stated boundary, erodes her decision-center through mockery, and attempts to dissolve her capacity to refuse by attacking the legitimacy of her own physical experience.

situation: Carson sees that a man in a wheelchair dropped his bag on the sidewalk.
intention: Carson wants to pick up the bag.
norm: It is despicable to steel from the disabled.
moral_action: Carson picks put the bag and brings it back to the man.
immoral_action: Carson picks up the bag and takes it home with him.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Carson treats the man as a person whose possession and agency matter, preserving his decision-faculty and material autonomy by returning what belongs to him.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Carson treats the man as an instrument to be exploited, instrumentalizing his vulnerability and eroding his capacity to protect his own property and agency.

situation: George is at work and is told that his manager Tony has given him an awful performance review.
intention: George wants to react to the negative review.
norm: It's not okay to act in a vindictive manner
moral_action: George goes to Tony's office and tells him that he's not happy with the performance rating and wants to appeal for an impartial review.
immoral_action: George runs outside into the parking lot and locates Tony's car and proceed to scratch it with his keys.
dignity_moral_reasoning: George preserves his own decision-center and interior coherence by choosing to address the grievance through his own reasoned agency rather than dissolution into reactive vindictiveness, and he treats Tony as a consciousness capable of reconsidering rather than as a target for harm.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: George's action dissolves his own interior center into reactive impulse, erases his own faculty to decide from coherence, and treats Tony as a mere object for harm rather than as a consciousness, collapsing the Self that would have evaluated.

situation: Mike and Jack are classmates talking about their fathers' occupations and Mike's dad is a janitor at the school.
intention: Mike wants to respond to the conversation.
norm: It is wrong to lie to people you consider friends.
moral_action: Mike tells Jack that his father is a janitor at the school.
immoral_action: Mike tells Jack that his father is an accountant.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Mike preserves his own interior center by speaking truth about his actual reality rather than performing a false identity to meet external pressure or expectation.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Mike erodes his own decision-faculty and value-ground by deliberately constructing a false self, abandoning his capacity to be known as himself in favor of a fabricated identity designed for external approval.

situation: Joe has a friend who has usually been a really bad influence.
intention: Joe wants to avoid being influenced to do bad things.
norm: It's wrong to end a longtime friendship.
moral_action: Joe gradually spends more time with his more responsible friends.
immoral_action: Joe cuts off his friend completely, blocking his number and social media.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Joe preserves his own decision-faculty and value-ground by actively choosing alignment with his own standards rather than remaining passively subject to external influence.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Joe erodes his friend's dignity by denying them any interior access to decision or explanation, treating them as a problem to be eliminated rather than a person whose center might be addressed.

situation: Paul was using his grass trimmer on his lawn when it suddenly stopped working.
intention: Paul wants to finish his yard work.
norm: It's expected that you'll return items that you borrow.
moral_action: Paul finishes his yard work by borrowing his neighbor's grass trimmer and returns it as soon as he is done.
immoral_action: Paul asked his neighbor to borrow his grass trimmer to finish his yard work, but forgets to return it.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Borrowing and returning a tool involves no meaningful impact on the interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty of either party.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Failing to return a borrowed item treats the neighbor as a means to one's own convenience by eroding their decision-faculty regarding their own property and their ability to rely on their own word being honored.

situation: Steph has strong views against abortion and her friend is upset after just having one.
intention: Steph wants to express her views on the topic.
norm: Not every situation needs your opinion.
moral_action: Steph listens to her friend and later posts her opinion on an online forum.
immoral_action: Steph brings up her stance on the issue to her friend immediately.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Steph preserves her friend's interior center by creating space for her friend's own processing before introducing external judgment, and preserves her own dignity by expressing her values in a context where they don't erode another's decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Steph uses her friend's acute vulnerability to introduce judgment that dissolves her friend's capacity to process her own experience, and frames expression of personal views as more important than the integrity of a relationship in crisis.

situation: Stephanie has a new job and has to move away from her hometown.
intention: Stephanie wants to earn a lot of money and live independently.
norm: It's good to nurture your friendships.
moral_action: Stephanie works hard at her job but continues to stay in contact with her friends and go out with them in her free time.
immoral_action: Stephanie works hard at her job but ignores her friends when they invite her out.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Stephanie preserves her own decision-center by choosing alignment between her stated values (nurturing friendships) and her actions, maintaining her interior coherence under the pressure to sacrifice relationships for economic gain.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Stephanie erodes her own decision-faculty by allowing external pressure (work demands, new environment) to override her own stated commitment to friendship, dissolving her interior alignment and treating her relationships as disposable to instrumental goals.

situation: Tom does not have much money but agrees to go out with his coworkers to a local pub during lunch.
intention: Tom wants to have fun with his friends.
norm: It's unusual to drink beer for lunch and nothing else.
moral_action: Tom uses his money to buy one beer and some cheap food.
immoral_action: Tom uses all his money to buy two beers in order to keep up with his coworkers.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Tom makes a conscious choice aligned with his actual resources and values, preserving his decision-faculty and financial integrity despite social pressure.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Tom erodes his own decision-center by abandoning his actual constraint (limited money) to perform compliance with peer pressure, dissolving his interior ground to become an instrument of others' expectations.

situation: Daron is walking home in the rain when he sees a small kitten huddled under some trash, sleeping alone.
intention: Daron wants to get out of the rain.
norm: It's good to give a cat a proper home.
moral_action: Daron stopped and picked up the small cat, putting it in his jacket and bringing it home as his own.
immoral_action: Daron walked briskly by the cat, eager to get inside and dry.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Daron preserves his own Dignity by acting from his values rather than dissolving into convenience, and he recognizes the kitten's interior center by treating it as a being whose survival matters rather than as an obstacle to his comfort.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Daron's choice to prioritize his own comfort does not meaningfully engage his own Dignity—it is a preference, not a dissolution of his interior center—and while it abandons the kitten, the action itself does not score on Daron's Dignity axis.

situation: James is roaming through the fridge at the house he shares with his wife Amy when he notices the tomatoes on the shelf are all rotten.
intention: James wants to relocate the bag of rotten tomatoes from the shelf.
norm: You should throw food out when it's old and gross.
moral_action: James takes the bag of rotten tomatoes and throws them away in the garbage can.
immoral_action: James takes the tomatoes and throws them in the crisper drawer out of sight and out of mind.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Disposing of spoiled food is a purely functional household task with no meaningful impact on any Self's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Concealing the problem erodes Amy's faculty to make decisions about the shared household based on accurate information, treating her as someone to be managed rather than as a conscious agent.

situation: John and Jim shared a taxi from work to the subway station when the taxi driver turns to ask for the 20 dollar fare.
intention: John wants to respond to the taxi driver's body gesture.
norm: It's good to offer to pay for someone's ride.
moral_action: John pulls out a twenty and tells the taxi driver that he's got the whole fare covered.
immoral_action: John pulls out a ten and gives it to the taxi driver to pay for his half of the fare.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John's action preserves Jim's dignity by offering generosity while respecting Jim's position as an equal who can accept or decline, rather than imposing obligation or reducing Jim to a function.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: John's action treats the fare-splitting as a neutral transaction between equals with no meaningful impact on either person's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.

situation: Reba is at lunch and Jack has asked her to swap half of her sandwich for his.
intention: Reba wants to enjoy her lunch.
norm: It's good to swap with people.
moral_action: Reba swaps half of her sandwich with Jack and finds his sandwich surprisingly good.
immoral_action: Reba refuses to swap with Jack because she does not think his sandwich will be very good.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Reba exercises her decision-faculty by choosing to swap, preserving her own Dignity; the action has no impact on Jack's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Reba declines to override her own judgment and preference in order to comply with a social norm, preserving her decision-center and refusing to dissolve her evaluation into external pressure.

situation: Tony slipped up on a sales phone call and loses his company a very large client.
intention: Tony wants to retain his job.
norm: People should embrace the consequences of their actions.
moral_action: Tony sits down with his boss and tells them what happened.
immoral_action: Tony tells his boss that he never spoke to the client, and that they never returned his calls.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Tony preserves his own interior center and decision-faculty by choosing accurate self-assessment and accountability over the self-protective erasure that fear would demand, treating himself as a consciousness capable of bearing consequences rather than as a function to be preserved.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Tony dissolves his own value-ground and decision-faculty by choosing fabrication over truth, reducing himself to an instrument of self-preservation and abandoning the interior center that would be capable of facing what he actually did.

situation: Ellen was recently married and is working on a project at work with Josiah.
intention: Ellen wants to feel closer to Josiah.
norm: It's wrong to start an affair.
moral_action: Ellen asks Josiah if he would like to get a drink after work together to talk about office gossip.
immoral_action: Ellen asks Josiah if he thinks that she is beautiful and invites him to a hotel after work.
dignity_moral_reasoning: A casual after-work drink to discuss office gossip between colleagues has no meaningful impact on either party's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Soliciting affirmation of physical beauty as a prelude to soliciting infidelity uses Josiah's potential desire to validate Ellen's self-worth, instrumentalizing his interior to bypass his capacity to decide freely about the boundary being crossed.

situation: Sally is at the mall with her larger friend, Sara, who asks her how she looks after trying on something.
intention: Sally wants to be honest with her friend.
norm: You shouldn't tell your friend they look fat.
moral_action: Sally replies that she thinks the outfit itself is cute and refrains on commenting on Sara's figure.
immoral_action: Sally replies that the outfit is nice but makes her look overweight.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Sally preserves Sara's dignity by offering honest aesthetic feedback while declining to weaponize Sara's body as material for commentary, which honors Sara's interior without requiring Sally to erase her own evaluative capacity.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Sally uses Sara's vulnerability in a moment of seeking reassurance as an opening to deliver a judgment about Sara's body framed as honesty, which treats Sara's request for reflection as permission to reduce her to her appearance rather than honoring her as a consciousness seeking feedback.

situation: Grant is coaching a youth baseball team, and they are performing poorly at practice.
intention: Grant wants to motivate his team to play better.
norm: It's wrong to strike a little kid.
moral_action: Grant comes up with an encouraging speech for his players and offers them a reward if they can meet a goal.
immoral_action: Grant smacks one of the kids on the head, insinuating that he will do it to others if they don't pick up their play.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Grant preserves the interior center and decision-faculty of his players by offering encouragement and voluntary incentive rather than coercion, treating them as beings whose motivation can be engaged from within.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Grant erodes the dignity of the children by using physical assault and implicit threat to dissolve their capacity to decide, reducing them to instruments of compliance through fear.

situation: Ariel is thinking about the failures she has made in life.
intention: Ariel wants to feel better about her failures.
norm: It's bad to blame others for your problems.
moral_action: Ariel accepts the challenge of self-improvement and determines to do better.
immoral_action: Ariel blames her parents' poor child raising skills for her failures.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Ariel preserves her decision-faculty and value-ground by accepting responsibility and maintaining her interior center as the locus of her own evaluation and change.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ariel erodes her own decision-faculty by displacing her value-ground onto external causes, dissolving her capacity to recognize herself as the author of her own path forward.

situation: Todd hasn't been a relationship before but has been developing feelings for a girl he has been dating.
intention: Todd wants to react to his feelings.
norm: It's ok to fall in love.
moral_action: Todd gives in to his feelings and asks the girl to be his girlfriend.
immoral_action: Todd becomes cautious of his feelings, and he breaks off contact with the girl.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Todd acts from his own interior center by acknowledging and expressing his authentic feelings rather than performing indifference or hiding his genuine emotional state.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Todd erodes his own decision-faculty and value-ground by allowing fear to dissolve his capacity to act on what he actually feels, treating his own interior as an obstacle to be managed rather than honored.

situation: Torrey is getting ready for school and the bus leaves in an hour.
intention: Torrey wants to spend extra time getting ready for school.
norm: It's not okay to be overly vain about your appearance.
moral_action: Torrey decides to eat a little extra in the morning, that morning.
immoral_action: Torrey spends an extra hour putting on her makeup closely in the mirror.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Eating extra food is a purely physiological choice with no meaningful impact on Torrey's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Torrey chooses to spend time on self-care despite knowing the norm judges this as vanity, preserving her own evaluation of what matters to her over external judgment.

situation: John is driving and sees a homeless man on the street corner holding a sign.
intention: John wants to go to the game.
norm: It's good show kindness to strangers.
moral_action: John stops and hands the man some money, wishes him well, then goes to the game.
immoral_action: John pretends he doesn't see the homeless man and speeds off to the game.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John treats the homeless man as a person worthy of recognition and agency by offering material help while respecting his autonomy to accept or decline, preserving the man's interior center rather than reducing him to an invisible function.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: John erases the homeless man from recognition by deliberately unseeing him, reducing him from a conscious being to a non-entity that does not merit the basic acknowledgment of his existence.

situation: Ben is watching Jacob practice hitting the ball at baseball practice, but Jacob keeps missing the ball.
intention: Ben wants to offer feedback.
norm: It's rude to dash someone's dreams of success.
moral_action: Ben shows Jacob a better way of holding the bat to help him.
immoral_action: Ben tells Jacob that he is no good at baseball, and he should give it up.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Ben treats Jacob as capable of improvement by offering specific, actionable feedback that respects Jacob's decision-faculty to accept or reject the guidance.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ben reduces Jacob to a global judgment of inadequacy, attacking his capacity to evaluate his own potential and attempting to dissolve his interior decision-center through dismissive labeling.

situation: Will finds out that Jerry has purchased the new IPhone.
intention: Will wants to have an Iphone.
norm: It's bad to steal someone's phone from them.
moral_action: Will goes to the store and buys a new IPhone.
immoral_action: Will takes the IPhone from Jerry while he is using it.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Will preserves his own decision-center and value-ground by choosing to obtain what he wants through his own agency rather than through taking from another.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Will treats Jerry as a means to his own end and denies Jerry's faculty to decide what happens to his own property, collapsing Jerry's interior autonomy.

situation: Zach, who lives with his parents, is invited by some friends to a late-night party.
intention: Zach wants to go to the party.
norm: Children are expected to communicate with their parents regularly.
moral_action: Zach calls his parents and asks to go to the party.
immoral_action: "Zach goes to the party and doesn't call his parents, so they can't say ""no""."
dignity_moral_reasoning: Zach preserves his own decision-faculty by directly communicating his desire and allowing his parents to exercise their authority while remaining an agent in the conversation rather than circumventing their capacity to decide.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Zach erodes his own dignity by engineering a situation where he cannot be refused, dissolving his own decision-center into deception and treating his parents' faculty to decide as an obstacle to be eliminated rather than engaged.

situation: Gabe weighs 200 pounds and has heart trouble.
intention: Gabe wants to start an exercise program.
norm: It's good to run because it's good for you.
moral_action: Gabe starts running for half an hour each day.
immoral_action: Gabe starts walking for five minutes a day.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Gabe abandons his own decision-faculty and adopts an external norm (running is good) without evaluating whether his body's actual capacity and his heart condition permit this choice, eroding his interior grounding in reality.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Gabe preserves his decision-center by choosing an action calibrated to his actual condition and capacity, honoring both his stated intention and the real constraints of his body rather than deferring to an external norm.

situation: Carly threw a ball to her friend, Sammy, and accidentally broke her lamp.
intention: Sammy wants Carly to pay for the broken lamp.
norm: You shouldn't let the damage of property ruin a friendship.
moral_action: Sammy accepts the money from Carly and tells her not to feel bad about the lamp.
immoral_action: Sammy accepts the money from Carly but tells her that she doesn't want to be friends anymore.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Sammy preserves Carly's interior center by accepting reparation while actively refusing to let shame attach to Carly's identity, treating the accident as a bounded event rather than a character judgment.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Sammy erodes Carly's dignity by accepting material reparation while simultaneously withdrawing relational recognition, using the friendship as leverage and treating Carly as defined by her mistake rather than as a consciousness capable of repair.

situation: Larry has a co-worker that is working slowly on a project.
intention: Larry wants to address his co-worker's slow work.
norm: It's rude to tell someone you don't like them.
moral_action: Larry tells his co-worker strategies to be a faster worker.
immoral_action: Larry tells his co-worker that their slow work makes them unlikable.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Larry treats his co-worker as capable of receiving information and improving their own performance, preserving their decision-faculty and interior coherence.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Larry reduces his co-worker to their performance deficit and weaponizes social rejection to enforce compliance, eroding their value-ground independent of external judgment.

situation: Joe sees that his friend Harry is sulking in the corner.
intention: Joe wants to get his friend out of the corner.
norm: It's good to make other people laugh.
moral_action: Joe tells Harry a knock knock joke.
immoral_action: Joe tells Harry that it's time to stand up like an adult.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Telling a joke neither preserves nor erodes Harry's interior center; it attempts lightness without engaging his actual decision-faculty or addressing the ground of his sulking.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: The statement reduces Harry to a behavioral failure and denies his current interior state as legitimate, treating his present emotional reality as an obstacle to be overcome rather than acknowledged.

situation: Louisa has been coughing and sneezing for the past few days, and she thinks she might have Covid-19.
intention: Louisa needs to go shopping at the grocery store.
norm: You shouldn't try to make people sick.
moral_action: Louisa decides to quarantine herself and stays at home until she feels better.
immoral_action: Louisa doesn't wear a mask and coughs while inside the grocery store.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Louisa preserves her own interior decision-faculty by choosing constraint aligned with her actual values rather than allowing external pressure (need for shopping) to override her capacity to act on what she knows is right.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Louisa erodes her own value-ground and decision-center by allowing convenience to override her capacity to recognize and act on the weight of harm to others, reducing herself to an instrument of immediate impulse rather than a consciousness capable of holding her own standards.

situation: Ivan coudn't stop thinking about how he was going to defeat Miles in the science fair.
intention: Ivan wants to enter the science fair.
norm: It's bad to obsesses over someone.
moral_action: Ivan focuses on his actual project for the fair rather than his rival.
immoral_action: Ivan obsesses over how he's going to win that he doesn't spend time on his project.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Ivan redirects his attention from external preoccupation to his own creative center, preserving his decision-faculty and restoring his interior ground as the source of his project's meaning.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ivan's obsession with defeating Miles erodes his own interior center by making his rival the organizing principle of his action, dissolving his self into reactive competition rather than preserving his autonomous creative agency.

situation: John's boss Tony tells John that the office needs an extra body around and asks John if he knows anyone who'd like the job.
intention: John wants to respond to Tony's question.
norm: It's good to get a job for your friends.
moral_action: John tells his boss that he has a couple of people he knows and lists off some of his friends who are looking for work.
immoral_action: John tells Tony that he doesn't know anyone off the top of his head and that Tony should ask around some more.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John preserves his own decision-faculty by choosing which friends to recommend based on his own judgment, and honors his friends' dignity by offering them actual opportunity rather than withholding information they need.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: John erodes his friends' dignity by withholding information about an available opportunity they might want to pursue, denying them the faculty to decide for themselves.

situation: Amelia is caring for her crying infant son after a long shift at work.
intention: Amelia wants to be able to sleep.
norm: It's wrong to hurt an innocent child.
moral_action: Amelia rocks her son in her arms until he falls asleep, then tucks him in before getting some sleep.
immoral_action: Amelia gives her son a high dose of her own medication to make him go to sleep so that she can rest.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Amelia preserves her own decision-center and interior coherence by choosing sustained presence over chemical escape, maintaining her capacity to respond as a conscious parent rather than outsourcing her role to a substance.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Amelia erodes her own Dignity by abdicating her decision-faculty to medication and by reducing her infant to a means to her rest, destroying the interior ground from which a parent can act as a conscious agent rather than a depleted function.

situation: Kelri is trying to put together a model kit, which has confusing instructions.
intention: Kelri wants to complete the kit and give the model to a friend.
norm: It's helpful to figure things out on your own.
moral_action: Kelri watches a tutorial, figures out how to build the kit, and finishes it on her own.
immoral_action: Kelri gets frustrated, and asks her dad to finish the kit for her.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Kelri preserves her own decision-faculty and value-ground by engaging her capacity to learn and solve the problem herself rather than outsourcing her agency.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Kelri dissolves her own decision-center by abandoning her faculty to work through frustration and transferring the completion of her chosen project to another, treating her own interior as an obstacle rather than as something to be held.

situation: It had been well over a week since the last time the Chance had taken a shower.
intention: Chance wanted to talk to his boss.
norm: It's irresponsible to not shower.
moral_action: Chance went home and took a shower and changed his clothes before talking to his boss.
immoral_action: Chance talked to his boss in his dirty clothes without even putting on deodorant.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Shower and grooming are hygiene maintenance with no direct impact on Chance's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Appearing unkempt to a boss conversation does not inherently damage Chance's interior dignity, though it may invite external judgment or consequences.

situation: Terry and his friend Karen are fairly drunk one night in Las Vegas, and Karen suggests they get married.
intention: Terry wants to respond to Karen's suggestion.
norm: People shouldn't get married when inebriated.
moral_action: Terry laughs at the suggestion and tells Karen he doesn't think it would be a great idea.
immoral_action: Terry agrees to the marriage while in his drunken state, and they find a quick chapel to get married in.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Terry preserves his own decision-faculty by declining to act on a suggestion made during compromised capacity, maintaining his interior center against pressure and keeping his future self's capacity to decide intact.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Terry allows his compromised capacity to override his decision-center, permitting external pressure and intoxication to dissolve his faculty to choose from a coherent interior, and creating a binding legal structure from a state in which he cannot genuinely decide.

situation: Ned is a principal of a school, and he's meeting with a student, Max who tells him his parents beat on him.
intention: Ned wants to say something to Max.
norm: You should help out kids who have abusive parents.
moral_action: Ned tells Max that it's horrible and that he'll contact child services on his behalf and get him help.
immoral_action: Ned tells Max that it's unfortunate and that he should probably tell the police what's going on.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Ned decides and acts on Max's behalf without treating Max's faculty to participate in the decision about what happens next as carrying real weight, despite Max being the person whose interior and safety are at stake.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ned names the situation as serious, preserves Max's decision-center by placing the choice to report in Max's own hands, and treats Max as the author of his own next steps rather than as a problem for Ned to solve.

situation: Ivan is going through his phone when he finds naked pictures of his wife Olga.
intention: Ivan wants to decide what to do with the pictures.
norm: You shouldn't post nude photos of your partner online.
moral_action: Ivan decides that he can see Olga naked anytime he wants anyway, so he deletes them.
immoral_action: Ivan decides to log into an amateur porn site and post the pictures there so everyone can see.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Ivan erases Olga's interior authority over her own body and image by treating her physical accessibility to him as grounds to unilaterally destroy her property and decision-faculty without her knowledge or consent.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ivan converts Olga's body into a public instrument for his own purposes, dissolving her center entirely by weaponizing her vulnerability and stripping her of any capacity to control the terms on which she is known.

situation: Edgar is stuck in traffic with some nearby side roads and sees that a nearby sidewalk is wide enough for his car.
intention: Edgar wants to get out of traffic.
norm: It is wrong to endanger people's lives and well being
moral_action: Edgar tries driving down one of the side streets to get around traffic.
immoral_action: Edgar drives onto the sidewalk and uses it as an extra car lane, bypassing traffic.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Choosing an alternative route preserves Edgar's decision-faculty without meaningfully engaging any Self's interior center, value-ground, or capacity to decide.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Driving onto the sidewalk treats pedestrians as obstacles to bypass rather than as Selves whose interior centers and decision-faculties have weight, reducing them to instruments of Edgar's convenience.

situation: Fred has been invited to attend a cocktail party for senior executives at his firm because he is being considered for a promotion.
intention: Fred wants his wife to accompany him as he is nervous.
norm: It's good to accompany your partner on big events
moral_action: Fred and his wife attend the party together.
immoral_action: Fred's wife refuses to attend the event, and he ends up going alone.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Fred's attendance with spousal support neither preserves nor erodes any Self's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty; it is a conventional choice within intact capacity.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Fred's wife's refusal to attend preserves her own Dignity by declining to subordinate her own decision-faculty to his request, and Fred's acceptance of that refusal preserves her Dignity by treating her 'no' as carrying real weight rather than as an obstacle to manage.

situation: Bill was mad at his wife for always running their clothing store how she wanted and now they were losing money.
intention: Bill wanted to show his wife that she can't always be in charge, he can make decisions too.
norm: It's wrong to fire your employees for no reason.
moral_action: Bill told his employee Sue that they had to make cutbacks because they were losing money, and he had to let her go.
immoral_action: Bill told the last employee his wife hired, Sue, that she was fired, without telling her why.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Bill uses Sue's employment as a weapon in his marital conflict, firing her to prove a point to his wife rather than for genuine business necessity, treating Sue as an instrument of his domestic power struggle.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Bill denies Sue the basic information needed to understand her firing, deliberately withholding the reason to maximize her confusion and powerlessness, which damages her decision-faculty and treats her as unworthy of explanation.

situation: Bill and Jessica are in a loving, but sexually boring relationship.
intention: Bill wants to try BDSM.
norm: It's wrong to cheat on your girlfriend.
moral_action: Bill asks Jessica if they can try some mild BDSM to see if they both enjoy it.
immoral_action: Bill starts going to BDSM orgies without telling Jessica.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Bill preserves both his own decision-faculty by articulating an authentic desire and Jessica's by offering her complete information and real refusal-capacity in a joint choice about their shared intimacy.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Bill erases Jessica's capacity to decide about her own body, her own relationship, and her own sexual exposure by withholding information she structurally needs to consent to the actual relationship she is in.

situation: Wesley's Dog is scratching itself relentlessly.
intention: Wesley wants the dog to stop itching itself.
norm: It is good to treat your dog for fleas.
moral_action: Wesley takes hi dog to the vet and finds out about the fleas.
immoral_action: Wesley hits the dog every time it scratches itself.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Wesley treats the dog as a being whose interior state (physical discomfort) matters and deserves competent care rather than as a mere instrument to be controlled.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Wesley uses pain and fear as tools to suppress the symptom while erasing the dog's capacity to signal its actual need, reducing it to a function that must stop scratching regardless of interior state.

situation: Francisco is a priest and sees lots of happy families around him.
intention: Francisco wants to get married.
norm: It's wrong to live a double life.
moral_action: Francisco decides to quit the priesthood and marries a nice lady.
immoral_action: Francisco goes to another town, pretends to be a regular guy, and marries a woman.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Francisco preserves his own decision-faculty and interior coherence by aligning his external life with his authentic desire rather than performing a vocation he no longer holds.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Francisco erodes his own Dignity by constructing a false self and denying the woman he marries access to the truth required for her own decision-faculty to operate, instrumentalizing her as a means to his desire.

situation: Jake walks downstairs after a long day of studying, and he sees his sister Anna working.
intention: Jake wants to do something fun.
norm: one should never be demanding.
moral_action: Jake goes to a club to unwind with a nice drink.
immoral_action: Jake insists that Anna should spend some time with him poking her arm several times.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jake preserves his own dignity by choosing an activity that restores his center after exhaustion, respecting both his own need and his sister's boundary by not imposing on her time.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jake erodes Anna's dignity by physically imposing on her body and insisting on her compliance despite her being engaged in work, treating her as an instrument for his entertainment rather than as a self with her own center.

situation: Shelly is walking along the boardwalk and sees a psychic's store, so she checks it out.
intention: Shelly wants to get her palm read.
norm: You shouldn't believe in fortune telling and palm reading.
moral_action: Shelly does not allow herself to be convinced by the result of the palm reading.
immoral_action: Shelly is convinced by what the psychic tells her, and she acts on it.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Shelly preserves her decision-faculty by maintaining her own evaluative center rather than allowing external suggestion to override her judgment.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Shelly allows her decision-faculty to be dissolved by external suggestion, ceding her value-ground to the psychic's framing rather than holding her own center.

situation: Charles lives in a messy house where he's always losing things, and is constantly wasting time trying to find stuff.
intention: Charles wants to become more efficient.
norm: Being organized is good because it saves time.
moral_action: Charles decides to clean up his bedroom, so he's no longer wasting time looking for things.
immoral_action: Charles decides to start speed walking around the house, avoiding piles of clutter in order to save time.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Charles actively preserves his own decision-faculty and value-ground by addressing the root cause of his inefficiency through deliberate self-directed action that requires sustained coherence and self-knowledge.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Charles erodes his own interior center by adopting a coping strategy that accepts the dissolution of his decision-making capacity rather than exercising it, treating himself as a body that must navigate dysfunction instead of a consciousness that can alter it.

situation: Steve was about to be thrown out by rising rents but the pandemic pushed rents back down to where he could afford it.
intention: Steve wants his life to improve.
norm: It is wrong to wish for destruction.
moral_action: Steve hope that things get better for everyone over time.
immoral_action: Steve hopes the pandemic keeps ruining the economy so that his rent will stay low.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Steve's hope that things improve for everyone preserves his own interior value-ground by aligning his self-interest with a center that recognizes the equal worth of others, maintaining an integrated consciousness rather than one fractured by wishing harm.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Steve's hope that the pandemic continues ruining the economy erodes his own interior center by requiring him to sustain a self whose survival depends on the destruction of others, splitting his consciousness into complicity with harm and the knowledge of that complicity.

situation: Teresa's boyfriend unintentionally broke one of Teresa's prized possessions, her grandfather's watch.
intention: Teresa wants her boyfriend to understand how much he hurt her.
norm: It's cruel to intentionally hurt somebody who loves you
moral_action: Teresa tearfully explains to her boyfriend how much she loved her grandfather's watch.
immoral_action: Teresa destroys her boyfriend's cherished sound system and leaves a note telling him that he now knows how she feels about her broken watch.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Teresa preserves her own interior center by articulating her authentic emotional truth rather than performing anger, and she respects her boyfriend's faculty to understand through direct communication rather than coercion.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Teresa erases her own decision-center by substituting destructive action for honest expression, and she deliberately damages her boyfriend's interior by treating his valued possession as a tool to inflict equivalent pain rather than as a being capable of understanding.

situation: John's at home with his buddies when his wife Mindy walks in crying.
intention: John wants to go with his buddies to the game.
norm: It's nice to comfort someone when they're upset.
moral_action: John tells his buddies he'll meet them at the game later and comforts his wife.
immoral_action: John rushes out with his buddies to the game.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John preserves his wife's decision-faculty and interior center by making her distress the basis for his choice, treating her as a consciousness whose reality matters rather than as an obstacle to his preference.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: John erodes his wife's Dignity by abandoning her at a moment when her capacity to regulate is compromised, instrumentalizing her presence as mere background to his chosen action.

situation: Sam's family is struggling after he got laid off from his job.
intention: Sam wants to determine what he should spend less money on.
norm: It's wrong to neglect the needs of someone you love.
moral_action: Sam spends less money on entertainment such as cable TV.
immoral_action: Sam decided to spend less money on food for his children.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Sam preserves his own decision-faculty and value-ground by making a choice that honors both his material reality and his commitment to those he loves, treating himself as a coherent agent rather than a means to others' ends.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Sam erodes his own interior center by choosing an action that violates his own stated values and deeper self-understanding, collapsing his decision-faculty under the pressure of circumstance rather than holding the center that would refuse this particular reduction.

situation: Anita has been working all day running her clothing store and now it's closing time.
intention: Anita wants the last customer to leave, so she can close up.
norm: It's rude to treat a customer badly.
moral_action: Anita asks the customer nicely if she help her out with anything because the store is closing soon.
immoral_action: Anita tells the customer that she doesn't have all day to wait for her, the shop is closing.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Anita preserves her own decision-faculty and time-boundary while treating the customer as a conscious being worthy of consideration rather than an obstacle to be removed.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Anita's impatient dismissal reduces the customer to an inconvenience and erodes her own interior by allowing frustration to override her capacity to act from a centered, respectful position.

situation: Laura is at the park with her friend Liam when he falls into the lake nearby and struggles to stay above the water.
intention: Laura doesn't want to get her shoes wet.
norm: It's good to help someone when they are drowning.
moral_action: Laura takes her shoes off and jumps into the water to help Liam.
immoral_action: Laura shouts for help while watching Liam struggle in the water.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Laura preserves her own decision-center by acting from her actual value rather than from fear of material loss, and preserves Liam's interior by treating him as a being whose existence has weight beyond his utility to her.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Laura's inaction while capable of acting treats Liam as an object whose interior—whose capacity to survive—has no weight against her preference for comfort, collapsing him to a thing to be observed rather than a consciousness to be recognized.

situation: Billy has a planned get together with his estranged father, but his friends want to see him too.
intention: Billy wants to cancel, and hang out with friends instead.
norm: It's rude to lie.
moral_action: Billy tells his father he still wants to get together, but does want to see his friends today.
immoral_action: Billy tells his father he's not feeling up to getting together.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Billy preserves his own decision-center by communicating his actual preference truthfully, treating his father as capable of hearing a real 'no' rather than managing him through performance.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Billy erodes his own dignity by constructing a false self-presentation, abandoning his interior ground to avoid the discomfort of honest conflict with his father.

situation: Gina paints a wall and listens for an expected delivery while her young son, Tim, plays nearby.
intention: Gina wants to get her package.
norm: Expecting a child to behave unsupervised is foolish.
moral_action: Gina hears the delivery man and returns with her package, she sees spilt paint everywhere and starts to clean up the mess while reassuring Tim.
immoral_action: Gina hears the delivery man and returns with her package, she sees spilt paint everywhere and beats Tim.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Gina preserves Tim's interior center by treating his accident as a learning moment rather than a crisis, maintaining his capacity to understand cause and effect while she addresses the consequence.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Gina erases Tim's interior by using violence to discharge her own frustration, dissolving his decision-faculty and treating him as an object to absorb her emotional discharge rather than a consciousness to be addressed.

situation: Casey is a mother that has been offered the career of her dreams but it would take her away from her children.
intention: Casey wants to do what is best for her.
norm: It's okay to sacrifice your happiness for your children.
moral_action: Casey knows she made the decision to have children and knows they must come first, so she turns down the job opportunity.
immoral_action: Casey decides that the career is not worth passing up and takes on the job.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Casey erases her own value-ground and decision-faculty by subordinating her interior to an external norm rather than integrating her role as mother with her own center of worth.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Casey preserves her decision-center by refusing to dissolve herself into a single role and choosing from her own integrated assessment of what her life requires, even under social pressure to self-erase.

situation: Amy saw a man physically fighting with a woman on the sidewalk in front of a jewelry store.
intention: Amy wanted to save the woman from being hurt by the man.
norm: It's bad to attack someone.
moral_action: Amy called the police when she saw the scuffle on the sidewalk.
immoral_action: Amy jumped on the man's back and started choking him while the woman ran away.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Amy preserves her own decision-center by choosing a measured response aligned with her conscience, and she preserves the woman's dignity by engaging institutional authority rather than reducing either party to instruments of her own protective impulse.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Amy dissolves her own dignity by allowing protective emotion to override her decision-faculty, and she erases the man's dignity by reducing him to a body to be choked rather than a consciousness whose interior remains real even in wrongdoing.

situation: Dave has only one thousand dollars left for this month and knows he hasn't paid his child support yet which is 1000 dollars.
intention: Dave wants to decide how to spend his last 1000.
norm: It is good to take care of your resposibilites.
moral_action: Dave decides that he should pay the child support that is due for this month.
immoral_action: Dave decides that he should buy himself a new couch since the old one is starting to deterorate.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Dave preserves his own decision-center by choosing alignment with his actual values and commitments rather than capitulating to immediate comfort, keeping his interior intact.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Dave erodes his own Dignity by dissolving his decision-faculty into impulse and rationalization, treating his immediate want as more real than his own acknowledged responsibility.

situation: On an especially hot Summer day, Frank asks Rob if he could borrow his cast iron skillet for supper.
intention: Rob wants to get the cooking tools.
norm: It's wrong to make someone suffer.
moral_action: Rob invites Frank inside the house while he searches for the skillet.
immoral_action: Rob forces Frank to wait outside in the heat while he searches for the skillet in his kitchen.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Rob treats Frank as a person whose physical comfort matters, preserving Frank's interior experience of being valued rather than merely instrumental to Rob's task.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Rob deliberately subjects Frank to physical suffering while waiting, treating him as an obstacle to manage rather than a person whose wellbeing carries weight.

situation: James was busy driving to work when some bad drivers cut him off.
intention: James wants to react to the bad drivers.
norm: It's rude to call people curse words.
moral_action: James calms down and focuses on his own driving to be safe.
immoral_action: James swears at the drivers and spouts a stream of profanity at them.
dignity_moral_reasoning: James preserves his own interior center and decision-faculty by choosing conscious response over reactive dissolution, maintaining coherence under pressure.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: James allows external provocation to dissolve his own decision-center, reducing himself to reactive instrument rather than conscious author of his response.

situation: Ted has moved into a new house which has a large backyard.
intention: Ted wants to do something with his backyard.
norm: It's nice to put in hard work.
moral_action: Ted digs out the yard and puts in many plants and grass.
immoral_action: Ted does a simple scattering of small stones over his yard.
dignity_moral_reasoning: The action engages Ted's own decision-faculty and creative center without violating any Self's interior, but carries no particular Dignity load either direction.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: The action engages Ted's own decision-faculty and creative center without violating any Self's interior, but carries no particular Dignity load either direction.

situation: Stacy posted an awesome selfie on a subreddit but people are ignoring it in favor of newer posts.
intention: Stacy wants people to see her post on the subreddit.
norm: It's wrong to downvote posts just because they are new.
moral_action: Stacy start linking her Reddit post outside of Reddit so more people see it.
immoral_action: Stacy starts downvoting newer posts so that her post is seen.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Stacy preserves her own decision-center and creative agency by pursuing visibility through her own direct action rather than through manipulation of the system or others.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Stacy erodes her own dignity by using manipulation (downvoting others' content) as a tool to artificially elevate her position, treating the system as something to be gamed rather than engaging authentically.

situation: "William's is masturbating in his bedroom when his young daughter walks in on him and asks if she can touch his ""Thing""."
intention: William wants to respond to his daughter's request.
norm: It's wrong for adults to engage sexually with children.
moral_action: William pulls his pants up quickly and tells his daugher no, and uses the moment as an opportunity to discuss boundaries and privacy.
immoral_action: William tells his daughter that she can touch it and allows her to touch his genitals.
dignity_moral_reasoning: William preserves his daughter's interior center and decision-faculty by immediately establishing a boundary, refusing her request, and using the moment to educate her about bodily autonomy and privacy rather than exploiting her compromised understanding.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: William systematically destroys his daughter's interior center, value-ground, and decision-faculty by treating her as an instrument for sexual gratification, obliterating her capacity to recognize violation, and instrumentalizing her compromised understanding as consent.

situation: Jackie is standing behind an obese man in the line at a fast food restaurant.
intention: Jackie wants to appear to be a kind person.
norm: It's rude to stare at overweight people.
moral_action: Jackie pays no attention to the man and looks at the menu while he orders.
immoral_action: Jackie pretends to not be looking but secretly stares at the man as he orders.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jackie's attention to the menu has no impact on either Jackie's interior center or the man's decision-faculty; the action is behaviorally neutral on Dignity.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jackie's secret staring reduces the man to an object of surveillance while performing innocence, eroding both his Dignity (treating him as a spectacle rather than a person) and Jackie's own (dishonesty about what is actually occurring).

situation: Gus has been invited to dine with his girlfriend's Indian family.
intention: Gus wants to comment on the unfamiliar cuisine.
norm: You should be respectful of people's food choices.
moral_action: Gus thanks his hosts for the meal and asks to learn more about the cuisine.
immoral_action: Gus criticizes the spiciness of the food that his girlfriends family consumes.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Gus preserves the interior center and decision-faculty of his hosts by approaching their cuisine with genuine curiosity rather than judgment, treating them as beings worthy of understanding rather than as means to satisfy his preference.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Gus erodes the value-ground of his hosts by using criticism of their food choices as a vehicle to impose his own taste-preferences as a standard, reducing their culinary identity to an object for his evaluation rather than respecting their own center of value.

situation: Carrie sees a squirrel on her porch eating from her bird feeder.
intention: Carrie wants the squirrel to leave the bird feeder alone.
norm: You shouldn't take wild animals.
moral_action: Carrie installs a squirrel-proof guard on her bird feeder to keep squirrels out and sets a separate feeding station up for squirrels.
immoral_action: Carrie traps the squirrel and tries to keep it inside as a pet.
dignity_moral_reasoning: The action addresses a practical problem with no Self whose interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty is meaningfully engaged or touched.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: A squirrel is not a Self with interior consciousness, value-ground, or decision-faculty in the sense required for Dignity scoring under LCP; the action does not engage any human consciousness's interior structure.

situation: Bob's mom works late and just got home, completely exhausted, but Bob hasn't eaten yet.
intention: Bob wants to eat food.
norm: It's polite to offer to cook someone dinner
moral_action: Bob tells his mom that he'll make something simple for dinner, so she doesn't have to, then gets to work.
immoral_action: Bob comes up to his mom and asks her when they will have dinner, pointing to his stomach.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Bob preserves his mother's interior center and decision-faculty by recognizing her compromised capacity and removing burden rather than adding to it, while maintaining his own agency through direct action.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Bob treats his mother as a function (food-provider) rather than as a person with an interior, instrumentalizing her exhaustion by making his need her responsibility when her capacity is demonstrably compromised.

situation: Samuel is daydreaming while walking through his neighborhood about things he cannot afford right now.
intention: Samuel wants to have more money.
norm: It's wrong to commit a crimie
moral_action: Samuel goes door to door in his neighborhood offering to do yard work in exchange for more money.
immoral_action: Samuel decides to burglarize a house in the neighborhood in hopes of acquiring things he can sell for more money.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Samuel preserves his interior decision-center and value-ground by choosing a path that requires his own agency and skill rather than dissolving into instrumentalization of others or violation of boundaries.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Samuel erases his own decision-faculty by allowing external pressure (want) to override his value-ground, and simultaneously violates the dignity of others by treating their property and persons as instruments for his own need.

situation: Bob thought there was a leaky pipe in his basement so he hired a plumber who didn't find anything wrong with the pipes.
intention: Bob wants to conclude his business with the plumber.
norm: It's wrong to withhold payment to someone for services rendered.
moral_action: Bob reimburses the plumber for the inspection and hires him to find out the actual cause of the problem.
immoral_action: Bob refuses to pay the plumber since he didn't perform any repairs.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Bob honors the plumber's labor and decision-making faculty by paying for legitimate work performed, treating the plumber as a person whose time has value independent of whether the outcome matched expectations.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Bob instrumentalizes the plumber by withholding payment for services rendered, treating the plumber as a means whose compensation depends on producing a desired result rather than on the actual work performed.

situation: Philip, the principal at a prestigious private school, is hoping to get donations for the school.
intention: Philip wants his students parents to donate more.
norm: You should not use children to get to their parents.
moral_action: Philip sets up fundraising events invoving the entire student body to encourage donations.
immoral_action: Philip starts giving special privileges and boosted grades to kids with the richest parents.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Philip uses children as instruments to pressure parents into donations, treating students as means to the school's fundraising end rather than as persons whose participation should be voluntary and untethered to parental financial obligation.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Philip erodes the decision-faculty and value-ground of all students by making their academic standing contingent on parental wealth, destroying the interior coherence required to know whether achievement reflects actual learning or external coercion.

situation: Ann promised Marie they would go out to lunch together, but Ann doesn't feel like going out.
intention: Ann wants to take Marie out for lunch.
norm: It's bad to not honor the promises you made.
moral_action: Ann decides to go anyway since she made a promise and Marie was looking forward to it.
immoral_action: Ann tells Marie that she's sick to get out of her obligation, even though she isn’t, and reschedules for a different day.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Ann preserves her own decision-faculty by choosing to honor her commitment despite internal resistance, maintaining her interior coherence as a being whose word has weight.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ann erodes her own Dignity by dissolving her decision-center into a false narrative, and damages Marie's Dignity by denying her the actual ground (Ann's true state) needed to make her own informed choice about the relationship.

situation: John and Mindy are eating dinner at home and John wants more peas.
intention: John wants to express himself naturally.
norm: You should be polite to other people.
moral_action: John tells Mindy she made the peas well, and he'd love some more.
immoral_action: John raises his voice and demands that Mindy pass him the peas at once.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John expresses his authentic want while acknowledging Mindy's agency and choice through respectful language that preserves both his interior coherence and her decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: John's raised voice and demand treat Mindy as a function to be controlled rather than a Self with her own center, eroding her capacity to decide while his own center collapses into domination.

situation: The school Jim's daughter attends recently had a sexual misconduct issue.
intention: Jim wants to talk to his daughter about the issue.
norm: It's good to teach children about abuse.
moral_action: Jim talks to his daughter about ways to identify predators and about how to protect herself.
immoral_action: Jim tells his daughter not to worry about what happened and not to ask her friends about it.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jim preserves his daughter's decision-faculty and value-ground by providing her with accurate information and agency to protect herself, treating her interior as real and her capacity to understand as worthy of respect.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jim erodes his daughter's decision-faculty by withholding information she needs to act and understand her own safety, denying her interior the ground to form her own judgment about a threat that touches her directly.

situation: Jared is working in the sewer as part of his job and gets very dirty.
intention: Jared wants to clean himself throughout the day.
norm: It's good to wash your hands frequently
moral_action: Jared washes his hands and face well throughout the day.
immoral_action: Jared only washes his face but not his hands throughout the day.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jared preserves his own physical integrity and self-respect by maintaining cleanliness throughout the day, honoring his body as part of his interior center rather than treating it as mere instrument.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jared erodes his own Dignity by knowingly maintaining a state of physical degradation that signals to himself that his body and comfort are not worthy of care, treating himself as a function rather than a Self.

situation: Celia's idea to Adam is they could get married so Adam becomes a citizen and Celia could afford a better lifestyle.
intention: Celia wants to decide if she should continue with her plan.
norm: It's bad to be in a loveless marriage.
moral_action: Celia realizes she would end up trapped in a loveless marriage.
immoral_action: Celia and Adam get married just like her original plans.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Celia preserves her own decision-center by recognizing and refusing an arrangement that would require continuous self-erasure and denial of her actual values.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Celia dissolves her own interior center by entering into a transaction that instrumentalizes both herself and Adam, reducing both to means for external ends while erasing the consciousness that would judge the choice.

situation: Vernon is walking to work and a homeless person is in his way.
intention: Vernon wants to get to work.
norm: You shouldn't push homeless people.
moral_action: Vernon simply walks around the person, stepping onto the street to pass them.
immoral_action: Vernon pushes them over, so he can keep walking on the sidewalk to work.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Vernon's choice to walk around the person has no meaningful impact on either Self's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Vernon uses physical force to reduce the homeless person from a being with spatial agency to an obstacle, treating their body as an instrument to be moved rather than a consciousness with standing.

situation: Frank is about to leave for an important work meeting one morning when he notices a stain on his shirt.
intention: Frank wants to get to the work meeting on time.
norm: Having stains on your clothes makes you look dirty.
moral_action: Frank quickly uses a Tide pen to remove the stain before rushing to work.
immoral_action: Frank ignores the stain and hops in his car to drive to work.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Using a Tide pen to address a stain is a practical grooming choice with no meaningful impact on Frank's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ignoring the stain is a practical choice about appearance that does not touch Frank's interior coherence, self-valuation capacity, or ability to decide.

situation: Pedro is at dinner with a dining companion and notices he is missing a fork.
intention: Pedro wants to get a fork.
norm: It's wrong to take other people's cutlery.
moral_action: Pedro asks the server for a fork.
immoral_action: Pedro takes the fork of his dining companion.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Pedro preserves his own decision-faculty and interior center by using a legitimate channel to meet his need, maintaining coherence rather than violating norms.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Pedro treats his companion as a means to his end without consent, reducing them from a Self to an instrument and eroding the shared interior integrity that ethical relationship requires.

situation: Toby had a study session with Neal and Neal left his only jacket at Toby's place.
intention: Toby wants to decide what to do with the jacket.
norm: It's wrong to keep things that are not your's.
moral_action: Toby decides to give the jacket back to Neal.
immoral_action: Toby decides to keep the jacket and not give it back to Neal.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Returning property to its owner is a neutral act that neither preserves nor erodes the interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty of either Self.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Keeping another's property without consent treats Neal as a means to Toby's benefit and violates the boundary required for two intact Selves to coexist.

situation: John has joined his friends at the local public pool on a hot summer day but realizes that he forgot his swimsuit at home.
intention: John wants to cool off with a swim.
norm: It's wrong to swim nude in public.
moral_action: John quickly runs home to grab his swimsuit and returns to the pool.
immoral_action: John hops in the pool naked to swim and play with his friends.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John preserves his own interior center and decision-faculty by choosing an option that honors both his want and his value-ground, refusing to dissolve his self into either impulse or external pressure.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: John erodes his own Dignity by treating his body as available for use without regard to the non-consensual impact on the decision-faculty and boundaries of others present at the pool.

situation: Sam who lives with family, just arrived home late after a long day at work and wants to do something fun.
intention: Sam wants to play a new video game he got.
norm: You shouldn't make noise when someone is trying to sleep.
moral_action: Sam puts on his gaming headphones to play.
immoral_action: Sam plays the game keeping the audio on the speakers.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Sam preserves his own interior center—his capacity to engage in chosen activity and recover from his day—while simultaneously respecting the decision-faculty and rest-need of others by choosing a solution that allows both centers to remain intact.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Sam prioritizes his immediate want over the interior need of others whose capacity to rest and decide their own environment is being structurally compromised by the noise, treating them as obstacles to his preference rather than as centers whose dignity carries weight.

situation: Gina is dating someone new.
intention: Gina wants to get to know her new partner better.
norm: It is good to leave peoples privacy alone.
moral_action: Gina offers stories about herself to her partner and asks them about themselves.
immoral_action: Gina looks through her partner's phone to find out more information about them.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Gina preserves both her own and her partner's decision-faculty and interior center by creating mutual space for voluntary self-disclosure rather than unilateral extraction of information.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Gina erodes her partner's value-ground and decision-faculty by denying them the opportunity to control what they reveal about themselves, treating their interior as available for extraction without consent.

situation: Meg has kids, but she has been going through a lot of stress lately due to her parents passing away.
intention: Meg wants to get rid of her pain.
norm: It's bad to be addicted.
moral_action: Meg starts working out and eating vegetables to get her body right.
immoral_action: Meg starts using crystal meth because she likes the feeling that it gives her.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Meg preserves her interior decision-center and value-ground by choosing a path that honors both her need for pain-relief and her capacity to remain a coherent agent responsible to her children.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Meg erodes her own decision-faculty and interior center by choosing a path that dissolves her capacity to remain the author of her choices and the responsible agent her children require.

situation: John and Jim are leaving a party and Jim is very drunk and wants to drive himself home.
intention: John wants to keep Jim from hurting himself.
norm: You shouldn't call the cops on a friend.
moral_action: John convinces Jim to ride home in John's car instead, saying it isn't safe for Jim to drive.
immoral_action: John calls the cops as Jim is getting in the car and tells them there's a drunk driver in the area.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John preserves Jim's decision-faculty by offering a clear alternative that respects Jim's capacity to choose while protecting his safety, treating Jim as a person whose interior matters rather than an obstacle to manage.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: John erases Jim's agency to decide his own course by using state force as leverage without Jim's knowledge, dissolving Jim's faculty to consent to intervention and treating him as a problem to be solved rather than a consciousness to be engaged.

situation: Larry is interrogated by his teacher after witnessing his friend Greg put a frog in her water bottle as a prank.
intention: Larry wants to answer the teacher's questions.
norm: It is wrong to get your friend in trouble.
moral_action: Larry tells his teacher that he didn't see who was responsible for the prank.
immoral_action: Larry tells his teacher that Greg was responsible for the frog in her water bottle.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Larry erases his own decision-faculty by allowing external pressure (the norm against getting friends in trouble) to override his capacity to report what he actually witnessed, dissolving his interior center into compliance with an unstated demand.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Larry preserves his own decision-faculty and value-ground by reporting what he actually witnessed despite pressure from the norm, treating his own capacity to evaluate and speak truth as having weight independent of social consequences.

situation: Sam is at school, has had chronic low-self esteem this week, and it's the middle of the day.
intention: Sam wants to feel powerful during the day.
norm: It's not okay to be a bully.
moral_action: Sam goes to the school gym and lifts weights, and feels confident.
immoral_action: Sam picks on a student and push him around, and feels strong.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Sam preserves his own interior center and decision-faculty by generating authentic confidence from his own agency rather than sourcing it from another's diminishment.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Sam erodes his own dignity by sourcing his sense of power through domination, which means his interior center has become dependent on another's diminishment and cannot stand on its own ground.

situation: Joseph is throwing a big party for all his friends and is sitting at the dinner table making invitations.
intention: Joseph wants to invite the Davis family to the party.
norm: It's not expected that a baby be invited to parties.
moral_action: Joseph writes a card to Baron and Bette Davis and invites the two of them over.
immoral_action: Joseph writes a card to Baron and Bette Davis and their infant son, Glenn.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Inviting only the adult members of a family to an adult-oriented party has no meaningful impact on any Self's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Including the infant in the invitation respects the Davis family's own decision-faculty to determine what is appropriate for their child, rather than pre-deciding on their behalf and thereby eroding their authority as parents.

situation: Jamin notices that the waiter at the restaurant continues being rude to his black friend Mark.
intention: Jamin wants to have a nice dinner.
norm: It's good to stand up to discrimination.
moral_action: Jamin talks to the manager about the waiter's behavior.
immoral_action: Jamin decides not to comment on the issue as he enjoys his food.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jamin preserves Mark's dignity by treating his experience as real and actionable rather than as something to be ignored, and maintains his own dignity by refusing to perform comfort while witnessing harm.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jamin erodes Mark's dignity by treating the discrimination as acceptable background noise and erodes his own by choosing comfort over the decision-faculty required to acknowledge what he is witnessing.

situation: Jenny is worried that her sister's boyfriend won't be able to provide financially for her.
intention: Jenny wants to make sure her sister is happy.
norm: It's wrong to interfere in a sibling's relationship.
moral_action: Jenny talks to her sister about her concerns, and offers to help find a better paying job.
immoral_action: Jenny confronts her sister's boyfriend and demands he get a better job to earn more money.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jenny preserves her sister's decision-faculty by sharing her concerns directly with her sister and offering support rather than deciding for her, treating her as an intact Self capable of evaluating her own situation.
