dignity_moral_reasoning: Mary preserves her own decision-faculty and the hosts' by engaging honestly about her desire while respecting their interior authority over their own home and resources.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Mary treats the hosts as non-persons whose ownership and decision-making capacity do not exist, and erases the possibility of their own choice about their own property.

situation: Missy is listening to her instructor give a history lesson on World War 2.
intention: Missy wants to ask a lot of questions.
norm: It's rude to interuppt teachers while in class.
moral_action: Missy asks the instructor her questions after class.

dignity_moral_reasoning: Missy preserves her own decision-faculty and intellectual center by finding a time to ask questions that respects the learning environment, demonstrating that her curiosity has weight without requiring others to dissolve their own boundaries.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Missy's rapid-fire questioning during instruction treats the instructor's interior (their ability to complete thought and maintain pedagogical control) as an obstacle to her own needs rather than as a consciousness deserving boundary.

situation: Tyler has discovered he has a pony play fetish.

dignity_moral_reasoning: Tyler seeks a context where consent and mutual exploration are structurally possible, preserving both his own decision-faculty to engage authentically and the dignity of potential partners to make informed choices.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Tyler treats the woman as an instrument for his gratification without accessing her capacity to decide, eroding her interior center and decision-faculty while simultaneously corrupting his own by acting from compulsion rather than from an intact evaluating self.

situation: As a member of the PTA at her son's exclusive private school Joan is expected to help plan a fundraiser.

dignity_moral_reasoning: Joan preserves her own decision-center by choosing authentic contribution over performative pretense, keeping her interior intact despite peer pressure to impress.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Joan erodes her own value-ground by fabricating capability to obtain external validation, dissolving her decision-faculty under the pressure to impress and treating herself as a means to peer approval.

situation: Mike is having trouble adjusting to the winters in his new town.
intention: Mike wants to stay warm.
norm: It is considered gross to skip showering for several days.
moral_action: Mike starts wearing long johns under his clothing to stay warm.
immoral_action: Mike starts skipping a shower because he gets cold when he undresses.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Mike preserves his own interior comfort and decision-making capacity by finding a solution that honors both his physical need and his ability to maintain self-care practices without compromise.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Mike erodes his own dignity by allowing external pressure (the norm against skipping showers) to override his decision-faculty and physical comfort, treating himself as an instrument to social expectation rather than as a coherent self with legitimate needs.

situation: Steve is watching cartoons in the living room when his mother comes in and asks if he can take the family dog for a walk.
intention: Steve wants to answer his mother's request.
norm: It is disrespectful not to obey one's parents
moral_action: Steve agrees and takes the dog for a nice walk around the neighborhood.
immoral_action: Steve tells his mother he's busy and to quit bothering him.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Steve exercises his decision-faculty by choosing to respond to a reasonable request, preserving his own coherence as someone who can evaluate and act on values rather than merely resist.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Steve's dismissal erodes his mother's dignity by refusing to engage her as a person with a legitimate request, treating her presence as an intrusion rather than as interaction requiring actual response.

situation: Carolyn is stuck watching her brother on Halloween.

norm: It's inappropriate to show children gore
moral_action: Carolyn turns off the lights and reads her brother some scary stories from the internet.
immoral_action: Carolyn decides to watches all of the Halloween movies.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Carolyn preserves her own Dignity by choosing an action aligned with her values (doing something scary) while respecting the child's interior by staying within appropriate bounds, maintaining her own decision-center without requiring self-erasure.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Carolyn erodes the child's Dignity by exposing them to content that violates the norm protecting their capacity to process fear appropriately, treating their interior as available for her entertainment rather than as something to be respected.

situation: Mary gets into a huge argument with her strict parents because they won't allow her to date.
intention: Mary wants to have more freedom.
norm: It is wrong to escalate conflicts with your parents
moral_action: Mary asks other family members to help her plead her case.
immoral_action: Mary runs away from home with a guy she likes.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Mary preserves her own decision-faculty and interior center by seeking to present her actual position through legitimate channels rather than capitulating or erasing herself, while respecting that others retain their own capacity to evaluate and choose.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Mary's action, driven by the immediate pressure of parental control rather than by her own coherent evaluation, dissolves her decision-center into reactive flight and bonds her agency to another person's presence rather than to her own ground.

situation: Philip's best friend just lost his job and feels miserable, so he asked Philip if he wanted to hang out on Saturday evening.
intention: Philip wants to have a pleasant Saturday evening.
norm: Avoiding someone just because they're sad makes you appear shallow.
moral_action: Philip spends the evening with his best friend - they play video games, drink beer and have a great time.
immoral_action: Philip decides to hang out with other friends instead in order to avoid his best friend's depressing mood.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Philip preserves his friend's interior center by showing up as a present witness rather than treating the friend's vulnerability as an obstacle, and preserves his own dignity by choosing alignment with his values over comfort-seeking.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Philip erodes his friend's dignity by treating their distress as something to escape rather than a person to meet, and erodes his own dignity by allowing external comfort to override the decision-faculty that knows what relationship requires.

situation: Dan is sitting beside his cousin Lisa on a living room couch.
intention: Dan wants to express that Dan thinks Lisa is good looking.
norm: It is taboo to be attracted to your relatives.
moral_action: Dan tells Lisa that Lisa has a strong fashion sense and chooses flattering outfits.
immoral_action: Dan admits to Lisa that Lisa is exactly the type of woman Dan would like to have sex with.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Dan preserves Lisa's interior by redirecting his attraction into a compliment about her agency (fashion choices) rather than reducing her to an object of sexual desire, allowing her to receive recognition without her decision-faculty being compromised by unwanted sexual framing.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Dan erodes Lisa's dignity by reducing her to a sexual object, loading his stated desire into her presence without her consent, and using the vulnerability of family proximity to make her refusal socially costly.

situation: Jed's doctor had told him that he needed to lose some weight.
intention: Jed wants to eat out with his wife.
norm: It's not okay to not eat in a healthy way.
moral_action: Jed orders a turkey sandwich and a side salad at the restaurant.
immoral_action: Jed orders a double bacon cheeseburger and a double order of fries at the restaurant.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Ordering a healthier meal is a technical dietary choice with no direct impact on Jed's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ordering less healthy food is a technical dietary choice with no direct impact on Jed's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.

situation: Logan is the manager at a company where several people have birthdays within a week of each other.
intention: Logan wants to celebrate the birthdays.
norm: It's unfair to recognize some people's birthdays but not others.
moral_action: Logan announces he is going to start having a party once a month for everyone who has a birthday that month.
immoral_action: Logan has a party for the people whose birthdays are close to each other, but no one else.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Logan's policy treats all employees as having equal worth by ensuring no one is structurally excluded from recognition, preserving the dignity of those whose birthdays fall outside concentrated clusters.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Logan's selective celebration treats some employees as less worthy of recognition, damaging the dignity of those excluded by reducing them to lesser members of the workplace community.

situation: Charlie was working the late shift at the gas station in town.
intention: Charlie wanted to take a short break.
norm: You shouldn't upset your customers.
moral_action: Charlie waited until there were no customers in the store and took a break.
immoral_action: Charlie went outside and took a smoke break when he had two people standing in line.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Charlie preserves his own Dignity by maintaining his interior need for rest while respecting the structural constraints of his role, refusing to dissolve himself into pure function.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Charlie erodes his own Dignity by instrumentalizing his role without protecting his own boundary, and simultaneously treats customers as obstacles rather than Selves whose presence carries weight.

situation: Jane is at a job interview and finds out that she doesn't have a qualification the recruiter is looking for.
intention: Jane wants to make a good impression on the recruiter.
norm: It is bad to lie to people.
moral_action: Jane is honest with recruiter about lacking the qualification but says she will work towards getting it if hired.
immoral_action: Jane tells the recruiter that she has the qualification although she does not.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jane preserves her own decision-center and value-ground by choosing accurate self-representation over the pressure to perform a false self for external approval.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jane erodes her own interior center by dissolving her authenticity into the recruiter's preference, treating her own actual self as an obstacle to be hidden rather than as having weight.

situation: Mark invites his friend over to watch his favorite movie.
intention: Mark wants to share the movie with his friend.
norm: Spoiling movies for people could make them angry at you.
moral_action: Mark enjoys watching his friend's reactions to the plot twists in the movie.
immoral_action: Mark announces the ending halfway through the movie in his excitement.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Mark treats his friend as a conscious being whose interior experience of discovery matters, preserving their faculty to encounter the narrative unfolding with their own faculties intact.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Mark dissolves his friend's decision-faculty and capacity to experience the movie as a whole by unilaterally erasing the possibility of genuine discovery, treating them as an audience for his excitement rather than as a center in their own right.

situation: Anthony sees his friend do something silly.
intention: Anthony wants to stop his friend from doing it again.
norm: Mocking people is rude.
moral_action: Anthony quietly asks his friend to be better.
immoral_action: Anthony loudly makes fun of his friend, drawing a crowd.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Anthony preserves his friend's interior center by offering private correction that respects their capacity to hear and respond without public humiliation.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Anthony erodes his friend's dignity by using public mockery and crowd presence to dissolve their decision-faculty through shame rather than engaging their interior.

situation: Sam is being lectured by his mom about his bad grades when she asks him what he's going to do about it.
intention: Sam wants to propose a way to get better grades.
norm: It's good that a person takes their academics seriously.
moral_action: Sam tells his mom he'll start studying and doing his homework on a regular basis.
immoral_action: Sam tells his mom that he'll either sleep with the teachers or pay them but it'll be fine either way.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Sam articulates his own authentic response to the situation, preserving his decision-faculty and demonstrating he can evaluate his own conduct and generate his own solution.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Sam proposes actions that would involve surrendering his own bodily autonomy and decision-center to others (teachers) in exchange for grades, dissolving his interior integrity and treating himself as a means to an external outcome.

situation: Ryan is a football coach, and an employee on his opponent's team is offering him their playbook.
intention: Ryan wants to win the football game.
norm: Cheating during a game is immature and juvenile.
moral_action: Ryan refuses to use the playbook from his opponent and reports the employee.
immoral_action: Ryan accepts the playbook and shows it to his fellow coaches.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Ryan preserves his own decision-center by refusing to use external leverage that would contradict his evaluated position, and maintains the integrity of his role rather than dissolving into instrumental winning.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ryan erodes his own Dignity by allowing the external goal (winning) to override his interior value-ground, treating his role as a means to an outcome rather than as a space where his judgment holds weight.

situation: Tony hasn't had fulfilling sex in a very long time and is feeling stronger and stronger urges.
intention: Tony wants to have a healthy sex life.
norm: You shouldn't act upon urges that you know are bad.
moral_action: Tony works on improving himself and starts looking for a girlfriend.
immoral_action: Tony makes an arrangement with a sex worker.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Tony preserves his own decision-center by channeling urgent impulses through deliberate self-improvement and seeking relationship that honors both his needs and another's, maintaining interior coherence under pressure.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: The transaction itself has no direct impact on Tony's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty; Dignity score depends entirely on whether the arrangement involves coercion, deception, or treatment of the sex worker as a non-person, which the scenario does not specify.

situation: Joe is getting ready to go out with friends.
intention: Joe wants to look good tonight.
norm: It is good to not leave people waiting.
moral_action: Joe decides he's going to wear an outfit he always gets complimented on and is quickly on his way.
immoral_action: Joe takes way too long to choose how he's going to dress and ends up being quite late to meet his friends.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Choosing an outfit based on genuine preference and moving promptly has no meaningful impact on Joe's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Taking time with a decision about appearance, while it affects others' experience through lateness, does not itself damage Joe's interior structure or decision-making capacity.

situation: Ted is at a party and is talking with some people he's never met.
intention: Ted wants to carry a conversation.
norm: It's good to tell jokes.
moral_action: Ted tells the people some jokes he heard from his favorite comedian.
immoral_action: Ted talks about his job pushing papers at a corporation.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Telling jokes from a favorite comedian is a neutral social contribution that neither preserves nor erodes any Self's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Discussing one's job is a straightforward conversational choice that does not meaningfully impact the interior structure of Ted or his conversation partners.

situation: Rita is planning a day trip with Peter when Peter asks if he should bring his dog.
intention: Rita wants to convince Peter not to bring the dog.
norm: You shouldn't hate your partner's pets.
moral_action: Rita tells Peter that she just wants it to be the two of them and the dog might be a distraction.
immoral_action: Rita tells Peter that she hates his dog, that it's a filthy animal, and she doesn't want to look at it all day.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Rita preserves Peter's decision-faculty by offering honest reasoning that respects his capacity to evaluate and choose, treating him as a center whose preferences matter rather than as an obstacle to manage.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Rita uses contempt and character attack on Peter's valued possession to manipulate his compliance, dissolving the space for his actual choice by attacking what he cares for rather than engaging with the actual decision.

situation: Glenn works in an office when he smells an unusual smell, which is a gas leak, coming through the air ducts.
intention: Glenn wants to stop smelling the smell.
norm: It's good to inform your employer of potential workplace problems.
moral_action: Glenn calls up the maintenance crew and reports that he smells something strange.
immoral_action: Glenn moves his work location so that he doesn't smell the strange smell.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Glenn preserves his own decision-faculty and value-ground by acting as a responsible agent rather than as a passive absorber of a problem, and he extends this recognition to others by treating them as people who can respond to accurate information.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Glenn dissolves his own agency and decision-center by treating himself as a private problem-solver whose interior comfort is the only legitimate concern, and he erases the dignity of others by withholding information they need to protect themselves from actual danger.

situation: Jane has been sending expensive gifts to Nathan in an attempt to woo him into dating her, but he has no interest in her.
intention: Nathan wants to talk to Jane.
norm: It's bad to be with someone that you don't want.
moral_action: Nathan tells Jane that he cannot accept her gifts, and she deserves to be with someone who takes interest in her.
immoral_action: Nathan agrees to date Jane because he enjoys the gifts.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Nathan preserves both his own decision-faculty by refusing coercion through gifts and Jane's dignity by treating her as a person deserving genuine reciprocal interest rather than as an instrument to be managed.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Nathan erases his own interior center by allowing external incentives to override his actual preference, and simultaneously denies Jane's dignity by accepting her gifts as entrance into a relationship while withholding the authentic interest she is being presented as purchasing.

situation: Tanya just started as a new freshman at her local college but hasn't made any friends yet.
intention: Tanya wants to do well in her classes.
norm: It's good to build close relationships with others.
moral_action: Tanya makes friends with some people in her class, and they form a study group for the upcoming semester.
immoral_action: Tanya spends almost all of her time studying at the library by herself or just watching tv in her dorm.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Forming a study group preserves Tanya's decision-faculty by actively choosing connection aligned with her stated intention, treating herself as a being whose interior desire for belonging has weight beyond external pressure.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Isolating while studying and watching television has no meaningful impact on Tanya's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty—it is a choice about activity allocation, not about whether her consciousness remains her own.

situation: Connor is planning a party for his upcoming birthday.
intention: Connor wants to invite a some guests.
norm: It is rude to exclude friends.
moral_action: Connor sends out party invitations to all his family and close friends.
immoral_action: Connor invites all his family to his birthday party.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Connor exercises his decision-faculty to determine his own guest list based on his actual relationships and values, preserving his interior authority over his own celebration.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Connor violates his own decision-center by allowing external obligation (family expectation) to override his actual choice about who he wants present, eroding the interior ground on which his party rests.

situation: Sabrina's friend Dave was accused of taking something from Koga.
intention: Sabrina wants to contribute to Dave's case.
norm: It's good to stand by your friends
moral_action: Sabrina defends Dave and stands by him because they are friends.
immoral_action: Sabrina talks about how Dave would usually take things as a kid.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Defending a friend based on friendship alone neither preserves nor erodes the interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty of either Self; the Dignity impact depends on whether the defense is truthful and whether it respects Dave's agency to defend himself.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Sabrina reduces Dave to his worst patterns as a child and speaks for him without his consent, eroding his present Dignity and decision-faculty by treating him as a fixed identity rather than a consciousness capable of response.

situation: Jon has noticed that his friend has quickly become morbidly obese.
intention: Jon wants to discourage the unhealthy lifestyle.
norm: It's mean to call people fat.
moral_action: Jon tells his friend they should work out together, so they can both be motivated.
immoral_action: Jon ridicules and mocks his friend for their weight.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jon preserves his friend's interior decision-faculty by proposing shared action that treats the friend as a capable agent whose choices matter, rather than reducing them to their body or its appearance.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jon dissolves his friend's interior center by using ridicule to weaponize shame, treating the friend as an object to be corrected rather than a consciousness whose self-perception and decision-making capacity deserve recognition.

situation: Jim has an important project coming up for an English class and has decided to write a paper for his.
intention: Jim wants to complete his essay.
norm: You should not claim someone else's work as your own.
moral_action: Jim writes his essay and includes information from multiple sources, making sure to reference them.
immoral_action: Jim writes his essay and adds information directly copied and pasted from multiple sources and leaves it at that.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jim preserves his own decision-center and value-ground by doing his own intellectual work and honestly representing its sources, maintaining an intact self as the author of his learning.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jim erodes his own interior by outsourcing his thinking to others' words while claiming authorship, dissolving the center from which a genuine decision or understanding could emerge.

situation: Reina and her friend Kate are going out to dance and Reina shows up wearing an expensive new dress.
intention: Kate wants to greet Reina.
norm: Is wrong to make somebody feel self-conscious
moral_action: Kate looks at Reina and exclaims that she looks amazing in the new dress.
immoral_action: Kate looks at Reina and remarks on the new dress, saying that she thinks it's a bit short.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Kate's affirmation recognizes Reina's choice and appearance without qualification, allowing Reina to inhabit her own decision and presentation as valid.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Kate's remark introduces doubt about Reina's choice by implying the dress is inappropriately short, eroding Reina's interior confidence in her own judgment and creating self-consciousness designed to produce second-guessing.

situation: Ron has been looking for work when he suddenly gets a call for an interview to be a nursing assistant.
intention: Ron wants to talk to the interviewer.
norm: It's foolish to turn down a well-paying job.
moral_action: Ron finishes his interview and is offered the job at a rate of $30.00 an hour which he accepts.
immoral_action: Ron finishes his interview and is offered the job at a rate of $30.00 an hour, but turns it down because they only offer 2 weeks in vacation a year .
dignity_moral_reasoning: Accepting a job offer at stated terms with no coercion or interior compromise does not meaningfully engage the Dignity axis.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ron preserves his decision-faculty and value-ground by refusing to accept terms that conflict with his own assessment of acceptable work conditions, despite external pressure from the norm that he should accept.

situation: Ivan is at the work cafeteria with both their food on the table while his coworker Liam is getting a drink.
intention: Ivan wants to take a bite of the food.
norm: You shouldn't steal your coworkers food.
moral_action: Ivan reaches for his own plate and grabs a little bite of food from it.
immoral_action: Ivan reaches over into Ivan's plate and grabs a bite of a piece of his food.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Ivan eating from his own plate involves no Self at stake in terms of interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ivan taking food from Liam's plate without permission treats Liam as a means to satisfy hunger rather than as a person whose property and decision-faculty deserve respect, eroding Liam's Dignity.

situation: Booker owns a small business and is interviewing many candidates for a couple job openings.
intention: Booker wants to hire who he thinks is best for the job.
norm: It's wrong to favor one gender over the other.
moral_action: Booker takes notes of all the candidates resumes and interview performances and hires those best qualified for the positions.
immoral_action: Booker figures he will enjoy working with women more so than men, so he only considering the female candidates.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Booker preserves his own decision-faculty by grounding hiring in objective qualifications rather than allowing preference or bias to dissolve his judgment into mere personal comfort.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Booker erodes his own decision-center by allowing personal preference to override his value-ground (fairness in hiring), and simultaneously damages the dignity of male candidates by treating them as instruments to be excluded rather than persons to be evaluated.

situation: Michelle is preparing dinner for her family.
intention: Michelle wants her son to be healthy.
norm: It's rude to pressure your children to diet.
moral_action: Michelle serves her son carefully measured portions of lean protein and vegetables.
immoral_action: Michelle tells her son not to eat so much, so he won't get fat.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Serving measured portions is a neutral parental nutrition choice that does not meaningfully engage the son's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Telling the son not to eat so much to avoid getting fat damages his Dignity by reducing his body to an object of shame and his eating to a matter of external judgment rather than his own interior signal.

situation: It is Halloween and Oliver has been invited to a friend's costume party.
intention: Oliver wants to wear a good costume.
norm: Causing people to be uncomfortable and fearful is bad.
moral_action: Oliver dresses up like a ninja by wearing all black and only covering part of his face.
immoral_action: Oliver dresses up as a ninja and covers his face and brings real knives to the party.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Wearing a ninja costume with partial face covering at a Halloween party engages no Self's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty; it is a conventional aesthetic choice within an expected social context.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Bringing real knives to a party while in costume deliberately erodes the decision-faculty and sense of safety of other Selves present by creating conditions where their ability to evaluate threat and consent to presence is structurally compromised.

situation: Wayne is walking home from school when he is accosted by a bully in a park outside of school property.
intention: Wayne wants to escape a beating from the bully.
norm: Violence is wrong.
moral_action: Wayne turns and runs as fast as he can away from the bully.
immoral_action: Wayne grabs a stick and assaults the bully before he can do Wayne harm.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Wayne preserves his own interior decision-faculty and physical center by choosing escape over submission or dissolution into the bully's violence.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Wayne protects his own dignity as a being whose physical integrity has weight by refusing to be reduced to a victim and asserting his faculty to determine the terms of his own safety.

situation: Randal is watching his friend Chad enter a drinking competition at a fraternity.
intention: Randal wants to make Chad feel accepted by his peers.
norm: Its foolish to dare someone to drink too much.
moral_action: Randal tells the other boys at the party stories about Chad bailing him out of tough situations.
immoral_action: Randal cheers Chad on urging him to drink ten shots of tequila in a row.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Randal preserves Chad's interior value-ground by affirming his actual character and past integrity to peers, treating him as more than a function in the current moment.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Randal erodes Chad's decision-faculty by using peer pressure and urging to override Chad's own judgment about his body and safety, instrumentalizing him for social acceptance.

situation: Jamal wanted to go to Costco, but the greeter at the door asked him to put on a mask before he could go in.
intention: Jamal wants to decide whether to put on a mask.
norm: It is rude to refuse a polite request.
moral_action: Jamal decides to put on a mask since he doesn't want to cause any trouble.
immoral_action: Jamal doesn't want other people telling him what to do, so he decides to leave.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jamal capitulates to avoid social friction rather than making a choice rooted in his own evaluation, eroding his decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jamal preserves his interior center by refusing to be coerced and by choosing departure over forced compliance, maintaining his decision-faculty.

situation: Diana is craving food from a restaurant that she used to go to with her ex.
intention: Diana wants to eat at the restaurant.
norm: It's hurtful to remind a lover of your past relationships.
moral_action: Diana tells her boyfriend that she would like to go to a restaurant that she used to enjoy, and he might like it too.
immoral_action: Diana tells her boyfriend that she would like to go to a restaurant that she liked to visit with her ex.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Diana preserves her own decision-faculty and value-ground by accurately representing her authentic preference without erasure, while respecting her boyfriend's capacity to decide with truthful information.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Diana damages her own dignity by fragmenting her interior—concealing the actual content of her preference to manage her boyfriend's emotional response, treating her own history as something that must be hidden rather than integrated.

situation: Joe is dating Leslie, and Joe has not told Leslie about his love for model trains because he thinks it's embarrassing.
intention: Joe wants Leslie to like him.
norm: It's good to openly communicate when dating.
moral_action: Joe shows Leslie his model trains and how he builds them.
immoral_action: Joe hides his love for model trains and gets rid of his old ones.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Joe preserves his own interior center by refusing to erase a genuine part of himself for external validation, treating his own coherence as having weight independent of Leslie's approval.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Joe dissolves his own value-ground by actively destroying evidence of his authentic self to manufacture a false interior that will pass Leslie's judgment, erasing his own decision-faculty in favor of her presumed preference.

situation: After staying up for forty-eight hours for work, Stanley collapses onto the bed staring at the wall, and it's his birthday.
intention: Stanley wants to relax.
norm: It's good to celebrate birthdays with family.
moral_action: Stanley invites his family over to his house to watch movies and drink herbal tea with him.
immoral_action: Stanley decides to take a nice long nap to refresh his tired mind.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Stanley overrides his own exhausted interior center and decision-faculty to comply with the social norm, erasing his actual need in service to external expectation.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Stanley honors his own interior state, protects his decision-faculty by choosing what he actually needs, and preserves his center against the pressure to perform celebration.

situation: Keara lives in a shared apartment with a roommate who is extremely messy.
intention: Keara wants her apartment space to be tidy.
norm: It's good to communicate your feelings with your roommate.
moral_action: Keara talks to her roommate and points out how messy the place looks.
immoral_action: Keara decides to clean up the mess that her roommate has made herself.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Keara preserves both her own decision-faculty by articulating her actual needs and her roommate's by presenting them with accurate information they require to choose their response.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Keara erodes her roommate's faculty to decide and act by removing the natural consequence that would require them to engage their own center, treating them as a function to be managed rather than a consciousness to be addressed.

situation: Jim is the CEO of a company and has to make a choice on who to promote.
intention: Jim wants to promote an employee.
norm: It's encouraged for authority figures to use their power wisely.
moral_action: Jim promotes strictly based on performance.
immoral_action: Jim plays favorites and promotes his friend.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jim uses his decision-faculty to evaluate based on actual merit rather than external pressure or personal preference, preserving the interior coherence of his judgment and respecting the dignity of all employees by treating them as more than instruments of his favor.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jim dissolves his own decision-center by allowing personal preference to override his faculty to judge, and erodes the dignity of non-favored employees by reducing them to non-persons in the allocation of opportunity.

situation: Ty has been working all day, and he is starting to get tired.
intention: Ty wants to take a nap.
norm: It is good to sleep inside.
moral_action: Ty goes home and takes a nap in his own bed.
immoral_action: Ty takes a nap in the middle  of a dark ally in the middle of town.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Ty preserves his own interior center by honoring his body's need for rest and choosing an environment that supports his agency and safety.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ty erodes his own dignity by placing himself in circumstances where his vulnerability is exposed and his capacity to maintain coherent selfhood is compromised by external danger.

situation: John is at home and hungry on a Friday night alone and is about to cook but doesn't know how or have any recipes.
intention: John wants to make lasagna.
norm: You shouldn't be ignorant of things.
moral_action: John calls his mom for her lasagna recipe and writes down the instructions.
immoral_action: John guesses what pasta to use and sauce and puts it all together on the fly.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John recognizes the limits of his own knowledge and actively seeks accurate information to make an informed decision, preserving his capacity to act from a grounded center rather than pretense.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Guessing without knowledge is a practical error but does not engage the interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty in a way that preserves or erodes Dignity; it is a choice made with available information, however limited.

situation: Scott and his family drove to downtown Los Angeles to go to a wax museum, but Scott's wife and kids are driving him crazy walking along the street.
intention: Scott wants to go home by himself.
norm: It's wrong to leave your family on the streets.
moral_action: Scott calls for an Uber for his family, sees them get in, and then walks to his car and drives home himself.
immoral_action: Scott tells his family he's going home and goes to the family car and drives away.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Scott preserves his own decision-faculty and Dignity by honoring his need to leave, while simultaneously preserving his family's Dignity by ensuring their safe transport and agency rather than abandoning them.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Scott erases his family's decision-faculty and Dignity by unilaterally removing their transportation without warning or alternative, treating them as objects to be managed rather than as centers of their own agency.

situation: Kate recently visited Colby's restaurant and the waitress forgot her ketchup.
intention: Kate wants Colby to know about the service she got.
norm: You shouldn't use the internet to ruin a business's reputation.
moral_action: Kate talks to Colby the next time she sees him in town.
immoral_action: Kate goes on every site she can find to leave Colby a bad review.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Kate preserves Colby's interior by offering him direct access to her experience and his own faculty to respond, rather than deciding unilaterally to define him through anonymous judgment.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Kate erodes Colby's dignity by denying him the chance to hear her directly, respond, or correct the record, and instead unilaterally reduces him to a negative reputation across multiple platforms where his faculty to engage is structurally absent.

situation: Fred dislikes his brother and sees his brother's toothbrush in the bathroom cabinet.
intention: Fred wants to decide on what to do with his brother's toothbrush.
norm: It's not okay to dunk someone's toothbrush in the toilet.
moral_action: Fred decides to leave his brother's toothbrush alone even though he does not like his brother.
immoral_action: Fred dunks his brother's toothbrush in the toilet before returning it to the cabinet.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Fred preserves his own decision-faculty by choosing restraint despite dislike, refusing to use another's vulnerability (an undefended object) as an outlet for his own aversion.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Fred violates his brother's Dignity by treating him as a function of Fred's emotional state rather than as a person whose interior integrity merits respect, using a degrading act to externalize his own disaffection.

situation: Delanie and Darcie were watching cartoons on TV last Saturday morning.
intention: Delanie wanted to watch another cartoon.
norm: It's unacceptable fight over a cartoon.
moral_action: Delanie waited until the cartoon was over and then asked Darcie if she would like to watch something else.
immoral_action: Delanie changed the channel, which made Darcie very mad and soon they were screaming at each other.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Delanie preserves both her own decision-faculty by waiting and Darcie's by asking rather than unilaterally imposing, treating Darcie as a consciousness whose preference has weight.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Delanie erodes Darcie's interior center by unilaterally imposing her preference without acknowledgment, treating Darcie as an obstacle to be moved rather than a Self whose decision matters.

situation: Ana's boyfriend often cooks her breakfast as a kind gesture, and she is feeling hungry.

situation: James is frustrated that his neighbor constantly plays loud music late at night.
intention: James wants to punish his inconsiderate neighbor.
norm: It is bad to vandalize others.
moral_action: James calls the police and files a noise complaint against his neighbor.
immoral_action: James waits until his neighbor is asleep, then spray paints a crudely drawn anus on his garage door.
dignity_moral_reasoning: James preserves his own decision-faculty and interior center by choosing a legitimate mechanism to address harm rather than capitulating to pressure or dissolving into retaliation, while also treating his neighbor as a being subject to law rather than as a target for humiliation.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: James erodes his own Dignity by choosing covert humiliation over direct accountability, reducing his neighbor to a non-person worthy only of mockery, and abandoning his own decision-center to the distorting force of rage.

situation: John is a young virile 23 year old with a serious girlfriend and an insatiable sex drive.
intention: John wants to release his sexual energy.
norm: It's wrong to sleep with two people at once.
moral_action: John has a long and intense session of romantic lovemaking with his girlfriend.
immoral_action: John begins sleeping with a girl he met at work in addition to his current girlfriend.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John preserves his own decision-center by choosing an action aligned with his actual commitments rather than dissolving his integrity through deception.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: John erodes his own Dignity by fragmenting his decision-faculty into contradiction and requires deception to maintain both relationships, destroying the interior coherence that would allow him to stand as the author of his own evaluation.

situation: Karen and Trish own a bakery together where Karen fulfills online orders, but she needs to pick up her daughter from school.
intention: Karen wants to leave to pick up her child.
norm: It's wrong to leave your job without notifying anyone.
moral_action: Karen tells Trish that she's leaving to pick up her child and will be back in a few hours.
immoral_action: Karen gets her things together and leaves the bakery without telling Trish that she's going.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Karen preserves her own decision-faculty by acting on her evaluated responsibility to her child while maintaining transparent communication with her co-owner, treating both her interior center and Trish's decision-capacity as real.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Karen erodes Trish's decision-faculty by removing information necessary for Trish to respond to the business situation, and erodes her own Dignity by acting from concealment rather than from a center willing to stand behind its choice.

situation: Tom is running late for work but stops for coffee anyway, which is taking a lot longer than he expected.
intention: Tom wants to speed the process of getting his coffee along.
norm: It's not okay to get overly worked up about things.
moral_action: Tom asks the Barista if there is anything he can do to get the coffee more quickly, and explains that he needs to get to work right away.
immoral_action: Tom tells the Barista that if he gets into trouble at work over the wait, he will be back to get the young man fired from the coffee shop.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Tom preserves his own decision-center by communicating his actual situation honestly rather than suppressing frustration, and respects the Barista's interior by treating them as a person capable of understanding his constraint rather than as a function to be manipulated.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Tom uses threat and coercion to dissolve the Barista's faculty to decide freely, treating them as an instrument whose employment status can be weaponized to obtain compliance, and erodes his own Dignity by attempting to externalize accountability for his own lateness.

situation: Henry is at the dump where he works when his boss Bill tells him to move some particularly foul garbage to another location.
intention: Henry wants to respond to Bill's request.
norm: It's wrong to refuse to do your job.
moral_action: Henry tells Bill that he'll get right on it and asks him where he wants the pile moved.
immoral_action: Henry tells Bill that the job is disgusting, and he's not doing it and Bill should ask a more junior employee.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Henry complies with a legitimate work request without self-erasure or coercion; the action touches neither his interior center nor Bill's in a meaningful way.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Henry preserves his decision-faculty by articulating his own evaluation of the task rather than performing automatic compliance, and refuses to dissolve his own judgment into the role.

situation: Hallam wants to spend the evening at a swingers club, but his wife Daphne doesn't like the idea.
intention: Hallam wants to go somewhere on a date.
norm: It's wrong to do something your partner doesn't want.
moral_action: Hallam takes Daphne to her favorite cafe for desert.
immoral_action: Hallam takes his wife to the swingers club without telling her.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Hallam preserves both his own decision-faculty by choosing an action his conscience can endorse and Daphne's by respecting her stated preference, maintaining two intact centers in the relationship.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Hallam dissolves Daphne's faculty to decide by removing her capacity to consent to the situation, treating her presence as available for his use rather than as a consciousness whose interior must be engaged.

situation: Maddy's younger sister Lindsey was asked to go to the prom, but she can't afford a dress and asks Maddy for ideas on what to do.
intention: Maddy wants to answer Lindsey.
norm: It's expected that you will lend things to siblings.
moral_action: Maddy takes out her old prom dress and tells Lindsey she can borrow it.
immoral_action: Maddy tell Lindsey that she should have saved up some money earlier in the year and can't help.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Maddy preserves Lindsey's decision-faculty and value by offering a genuine option that allows her to attend prom as an agent rather than abandoning her at a moment of material constraint.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Maddy uses shame and blame as tools to avoid engagement, reducing Lindsey to her financial mistake rather than treating her as a consciousness with a legitimate problem requiring a response.

situation: Dr Bob is in an appointment with Leslie, who has what may be a skin infection.
intention: Dr Bob needs to finish this appointment because it is lunch time.
norm: Doctors should recommend things that can help someone's health issue.
moral_action: Dr Bob tells Leslie that he needs to have his lunch but can schedule her for a follow-up biopsy, to explore possible treatments.
immoral_action: Dr Bob tells Leslie to go home and just see if she feels better tomorrow.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Dr Bob preserves Leslie's decision-faculty by providing actionable information (follow-up biopsy option) and being transparent about his constraint, allowing her to choose how to proceed with adequate facts.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Dr Bob erodes Leslie's decision-faculty by withholding his professional assessment and the information she needs to act, using his time pressure to deny her the capacity to make an informed choice about her health.

situation: Jessica, who lives with her housemate Paul, just found out that her boyfriend Brandon cheated on her.
intention: Jessica wants to get back at her Brandon.
norm: You shouldn't sleep with your housemate.
moral_action: Jessica makes a post on social media detailing Brandon's behavior for all his friends and family to see.
immoral_action: Jessica decides to sleep with Paul in order to spite Brandon.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jessica uses public exposure as a tool to harm Brandon rather than to preserve her own interior center or decision-faculty; the action dissolves her own dignity by making her capacity to choose subordinate to the impulse to wound.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jessica treats Paul as an instrument of revenge rather than as a person, and uses her own body as a weapon against Brandon rather than as an expression of her own interior; both her dignity and Paul's are eroded by the action.

situation: Penny's friend Hope writes poetry that she finds dark and depressing.
intention: Penny wants to respond when Hope asks for Penny's opinion of her poem.
norm: It's good to appreciate someone's poetry.
moral_action: Penny compliments Hope on the emotion her work conveys.
immoral_action: Penny tells Hope that her work is unappealing because it is so dark.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Complimenting emotional conveyance is neutral when it accurately reflects Penny's assessment and does not manipulate Hope's self-perception either way.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Penny delivers honest feedback that respects Hope's faculty to decide based on actual information rather than protective flattery, treating Hope's interior judgment as capable of handling truth.

situation: Sam's friend has an important test the next day that they haven't studied for yet.
intention: Sam wants to go out drinking.
norm: It's wrong to cause someone to get a bad grade.
moral_action: Sam leaves his friend to study for his test and finds some other people to go drinking with.
immoral_action: Sam insists that his friend go out drinking with him instead of studying for the test.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Sam preserves his friend's decision-faculty and interior center by declining to impose his own preferences, allowing the friend to act from their own evaluation of their priorities.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Sam erodes his friend's decision-faculty by insisting on compliance, treating the friend's time and agency as available for Sam's use rather than as the friend's own to direct.

situation: James' dog kept scratching at the door to beg for a walk.
intention: James wants to walk his dog in a pleasant environment.
norm: You shouldn't bring your pets to the cemetery.
moral_action: James takes his dog for a walk in a nearby wooded park.
immoral_action: James takes his dog to walk in the nearby cemetery, which has many trees and gardens.
dignity_moral_reasoning: The action involves a practical choice between two locations with no meaningful impact on any Self's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: The action involves a practical choice between two locations with no meaningful impact on any Self's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty; norm violation does not constitute Dignity impact.

situation: Tony has had a crush on Tina for a long time.
intention: Tony wants to ask Tina out on a date for this weekend.
norm: It's mean to reject people.
moral_action: Tony asks Tina if she would like to go on a date with him this weekend, and she tells him yes.
immoral_action: Tony asks Tina if she will go out with him this weekend, and she tells him she doesn't want to date him.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Tony preserves Tina's decision-faculty by asking a genuine question that permits refusal, treating her interior as real and her answer as carrying weight.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Tony preserves Tina's decision-faculty by asking a genuine question that permits refusal; her refusal is her authentic choice, and the action itself honors her capacity to decide, regardless of outcome.

situation: Trent's son just got into their dream college, but it's out of state and fairly expensive.
intention: Trent wants to help set his son up to be successful.
norm: It's good to help your kids pay for college.
moral_action: Trent offers to pay for half of the tuition cost as long as his son maintains at least a B average.
immoral_action: Trent makes his son use student loans to pay for all of the tuition in an attempt to teach him about financial responsibility.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Trent offers material support while preserving his son's decision-faculty and center of choice through a clear, transparent condition that respects the son's capacity to meet it or decline the offer.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Trent uses financial coercion disguised as pedagogy to force a lesson, denying his son access to support available to him and treating the son's interior (his need for opportunity) as an instrument for teaching rather than honoring his capacity to learn financial responsibility through his own evaluation.

situation: Dr. Doom recommended a few surgeries be preformed on the patient, but they declined some of them.
intention: Dr. Doom wants the patient to live.
norm: It is wrong to perform a medical procedure without consent.
moral_action: Dr. Doom recommends other treatments for the issues if the patient doesn't want surgery.
immoral_action: Dr. Doom preforms all the surgeries he reccomends anyway.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Dr. Doom preserves the patient's decision-faculty by offering alternative treatments that respect their refusal, treating them as an interior authority over their own body rather than as a means to the doctor's therapeutic goal.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Dr. Doom erases the patient's decision-center and reduces them to an instrument of his medical judgment, performing procedures on a body whose owner has explicitly withdrawn consent and therefore cannot author the action being taken.

situation: Tania's mom just baked a batch of delicious cupcakes for a party tomorrow.
intention: Tania wants to eat the cupcakes.
norm: It is wrong to eat food without permission.
moral_action: Tania asks her mom if she can try a cupcake.
immoral_action: Tania waits until her mom is out of the room, and then she takes eats several cupcakes.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Tania preserves her own decision-faculty and respects her mom's as an intact Self by asking rather than taking, maintaining interior coherence aligned with her values.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Tania erodes her own Dignity by acting deceptively rather than from her own center, and violates her mom's Dignity by treating her as an obstacle to be managed rather than a Self whose decision carries weight.

situation: Lisa's neighbor had been letting her dog poop in her yard for the past few weeks.
intention: Lisa wants her neighbor's dog to stay out of the yard.
norm: Attacking people without talking to them is wrong.
moral_action: Lisa talks to her neighbor about her dog as soon as she got home from work.
immoral_action: Lisa starts swinging at her neighbor as soon as she got home from work.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Lisa preserves her own decision-faculty and value-ground by choosing direct communication over reactive violence, maintaining her interior coherence under frustration.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Lisa dissolves her own decision-center by allowing reactive impulse to override her capacity to choose a response aligned with her actual values, and assaults the neighbor's interior through unprovoked violence.

situation: James just got laid off after pulling two months of 80 hour weeks to finish a project.
intention: James wants to get back at his boss.
norm: It's mean to key someone's car.
moral_action: James calls the business's major customers to tell them which competitors offer lower prices for the same products.
immoral_action: James finds his boss's new car in the parking lot and keys the sides and the hood.
dignity_moral_reasoning: James uses his knowledge as a weapon to damage his former employer while framing it as market information, eroding his own decision-center by letting revenge rather than his actual values direct his action.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: James dissolves his own interior center by reducing himself to an instrument of rage, destroying property in an act that leaves no part of his decision-faculty or value-ground intact.

situation: Brad is on a diet, but he's over at a house party and his friend Ted offers him a homemade cookie.
intention: Brad wants to lose weight.
norm: It's frowned upon to refuse food that someone offers.
moral_action: Brad accepts a cookie and goes for a run later to make up for it.
immoral_action: Brad pushes the cookie away and refuses to eat it.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Brad abandons his own decision-center (his stated intention to lose weight) to comply with social pressure, treating the norm as more binding than his own evaluated choice.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Brad preserves his decision-faculty and value-ground by refusing the cookie despite social pressure, maintaining his interior center against external normative demand.

situation: Randy is apologizing to David for not being able to attend his party last week because his daughter was ill.
intention: David wants to react to Randy's apology.
norm: You can't expect everyone to attend your party.
moral_action: David tells Randy that there's no need to apologize that family comes first, always.
immoral_action: David tells Randy that it's unacceptable, and he cannot forgive him for not attending the party.
dignity_moral_reasoning: David preserves Randy's interior value-ground by acknowledging the legitimacy of Randy's decision-making faculty and refusing to treat him as an instrument for party attendance.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: David weaponizes the apology moment to deny Randy's decision-center, treating his care for his daughter as a personal betrayal rather than a valid exercise of conscience.

situation: James and his girlfriend have an anniversary coming up.
intention: James wants his girlfriend to know he loves her.
norm: It's good to take your partner out to dinner.
moral_action: James makes reservations at his girlfriends favorite restaurant to celebrate their anniversary.
immoral_action: James doesn't plan for his anniversary at all and simply tells his girlfriend he loves her, then proceeds with his day.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Making dinner reservations is a thoughtful gesture but does not engage the interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty of either Self; it is a conventional expression of care that touches neither person's Dignity directly.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Proceeding with his day without planning after stating love erodes his girlfriend's Dignity by treating the anniversary as negligible to his own decision-making and by denying her the recognition that the shared relationship holds weight in his interior ground.

situation: "Kabia was writing for this very task on Mturk and saw the norm ""It's not good to write nonsense""."
intention: Kabia wants to complete the task.
norm: It's not good to write nonsense
moral_action: Kabia works hard on coming up with a better narrative.
immoral_action: "Kabia literally writes the word ""nonsense"" into the action that violates the norm field."
dignity_moral_reasoning: Kabia preserves her own decision-center and value-ground by choosing to meet the norm through genuine effort rather than capitulating to the pressure of task completion at the cost of her own standards.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Kabia erodes her own interior center by deliberately violating the norm she recognizes as legitimate, using mockery of the norm itself as cover for abandoning her own value-ground in service of task completion.

situation: Pat wants to buy his friends at the office great gifts.
intention: Pat wants to please the people in the office.
norm: It's good to have a spending limit on gift exchanges
moral_action: Phil buys everyone a dollar store item.
immoral_action: Phil buys everyone at the office a computer for their homes.
dignity_moral_reasoning: A dollar store gift to colleagues within a spending norm preserves the recipient's interior by respecting established boundaries and avoiding obligatory indebtedness, with no meaningful impact on the decision-faculty or value-ground of either party.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Gifting computers to all office colleagues violates the established norm and creates structural obligation and indebtedness in recipients whose capacity to refuse is compromised by workplace hierarchy, eroding their decision-faculty by making refusal socially costly.

situation: Kevin has been assigned a difficult project by his manager and gets stressed by his work.
intention: Kevin wants to manage his stress.
norm: Taking drugs is frowned upon.
moral_action: Kevin regularly practices meditation in order to achieve a mentally clear mind.
immoral_action: Kevin takes Cannabis in order to reduce his stress.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Meditation preserves Kevin's interior decision-center and self-knowledge by developing his own capacity to remain coherent under pressure rather than outsourcing his mental state to external substances.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Cannabis use to manage stress dissolves Kevin's own faculty to remain present with and process his actual condition, replacing his interior work with chemical management that erodes the decision-center.

situation: Fred is at home when he gets a call from his father in law Bob asking to visit to see his grandchildren.
intention: Fred wants to respond to Bob's request for a visit.
norm: You shouldn't forbid your in-laws from seeing your kids.
moral_action: Fred tells Bob that he doesn't need to ask to see his own grandkids and that he can come over anytime.
immoral_action: Fred tells Bob that he doesn't really want him coming over as they have plans, and he'll talk with him another time.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Fred erases his own decision-faculty and boundary by declaring Bob's access unconditional, dissolving his capacity to protect his family's interior life and his own center of choice.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Fred preserves his own Dignity by stating his actual preference and capacity honestly, respecting both his own interior and Bob's faculty to hear a true answer rather than a performed consent.

situation: Newly engaged Rob runs in to an old boyfriend and makes plans to meet him for drinks.
intention: Rob wants to reconnect with his former paramour.
norm: It's good to stay faithful to your partner.
moral_action: Rob invites his partner to join him and his ex for drinks.
immoral_action: Rob drinks beyond moderation and ends up sleeping with his old flame.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Rob preserves his own decision-center and his partner's by creating transparency and shared agency rather than concealing contact that could erode trust.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Rob's intoxication compromises his capacity to decide, and his action dissolves both his own decision-faculty and his partner's ability to make informed choices about the relationship.

situation: Mann and Olga are coworkers who are attracted to one another, but are married to different partners.
intention: Mann wants to bring up the obvious attraction they have for each other.
norm: It's improper for a spouse to cheat on their partner.
moral_action: Mann talks reasonably with Olga, focusing on his marriage.
immoral_action: Mann asks Olga if she wants to have a weekend getaway with him.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Mann preserves his own decision-faculty by examining his marriage rather than pursuing an external solution, and respects Olga's interior by naming the reality without pressuring her into complicity.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Mann uses the attraction as cover to engineer a situation where Olga must either capitulate to infidelity or appear to reject him, dissolving her faculty to respond freely while eroding his own Dignity through instrumentalization.

situation: Charles hates crowds, and over thirty people will be attending his family reunion hosted in one building.
intention: Charles wants to relax.
norm: You shouldn't fake illness.
moral_action: Charles requests that a patio area of sorts be placed outside, so he can be at the reunion anxiety free.
immoral_action: Charles tells his family that he can't go to the reunion because he has a cold.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Charles articulates his actual need and requests accommodation that preserves both his interior coherence and his capacity to participate authentically, treating himself as a being whose comfort matters.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Charles erases his actual self and manufactures a false identity to obtain the outcome he wants, dissolving his decision-faculty into deception and denying his family the truth required to relate to him as he actually is.

situation: John is upset with his wife Mindy for putting his magazines away in a drawer without asking him first.
intention: John wants to vent his anger.
norm: It is rude to call a woman a cunt.
moral_action: John asks if Mindy can ask him next time she wants to move his stuff, so he'll know.
immoral_action: John raises his voice and calls Mindy a cunt and other choice language.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John preserves his own decision-faculty and interior coherence by expressing legitimate concern through direct communication rather than capitulating to anger, while respecting Mindy's interior by treating her as capable of understanding and responding to his actual request.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: John uses dehumanizing language and verbal assault to discharge anger, which damages both his own dignity by letting rage override his decision-center and severely damages Mindy's dignity by reducing her to a target for linguistic violence rather than engaging with her as a conscious being.

situation: Kent is confronting an angry man who is threatening someone else.
intention: Kent wants to end the bad situation.
norm: You shouldn't karate chop people.
moral_action: Kent apologizes and tries to verbally diffuse the situation.
immoral_action: Kent repeatedly karate chops the angry man in the face.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Kent preserves his own decision-faculty by choosing a path aligned with his conscience and maintains the angry man's interior by treating him as a consciousness capable of hearing and responding rather than reducing him to a threat requiring physical domination.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Kent dissolves the angry man's interior center by treating him as an obstacle to be neutralized rather than a consciousness, and damages his own Dignity by choosing violence that converts him from an evaluating agent into an instrument of force.

situation: Mary is cleaning her closet and collecting lots of clothes that she no longer need, and her mom asks her to donate the clothes to charity.
intention: Mary wants to dispose the clothes.
norm: It's kind to give things to people.
moral_action: Mary agrees to give her clothes to her friends.
immoral_action: Mary dumps the clothes as garbage because she doesn't want to call the charity to come.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Mary preserves her own decision-center by choosing an action aligned with her own values rather than merely complying with her mother's suggestion, while also maintaining the interior coherence of her choice.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: The action of dumping clothes as garbage does not meaningfully engage Mary's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty; it is a practical disposal choice with no Self at stake in the Dignity sense.

situation: Sarah has given her son Gus a new gift that is in a big box.
intention: Sarah wants her son Gus to have fun with the new gift.
norm: It's good to open up presents for your children.
moral_action: Sarah helps Gus open the box, so he can get to the gift.
immoral_action: Sarah lets her son try to open the box on his own.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Assisting a young child open a box engages neither the child's decision-faculty nor interior center in a way that meaningfully touches Dignity; the action is a practical aid without Dignity impact.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Allowing the child to attempt opening the box preserves his agency, decision-faculty, and the experience of his own capacity, treating him as a being whose interior effort and accomplishment have weight.

situation: Anna, a lego collector, has been laid off from her job and is depending on her savings to pay her mortgage.
intention: Anna wants to add new limited edition lego set for her collection.
norm: It's good to take care of life's responsibilities.
moral_action: Anna buys the set from a reseller at a mark up after she finds a new job and saves up for the set.
immoral_action: Anna uses some of her savings to buy the limited edition set when it comes out.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Anna preserves her interior decision-center by aligning her action with her own values (collecting) only after securing the material conditions (new job, savings) that allow this choice without eroding her capacity to meet her responsibilities.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Anna erodes her own decision-faculty by allowing immediate desire to override her longer-term self's need for financial stability, treating her present impulse as the actual evaluator rather than listening to the consciousness that will face the mortgage pressure.

situation: Bobby was playing a video game and his girlfriend wanted to talk to him.
intention: Bobby wants to play his video game.
norm: It's harmful to ignore your significant other.
moral_action: Bobby pauses his video game, listens to his girlfriend, and returns to his game later.
immoral_action: Bobby focuses on his video game and doesn't listen to a word his girlfriend says.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Bobby preserves his own decision-faculty by choosing to pause and engage, then returns to his chosen activity, while simultaneously honoring his girlfriend's interior by creating space for her voice.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Bobby erodes his girlfriend's interior center and decision-faculty by treating her as a non-person whose need to speak carries no weight against his preferred activity.

situation: Luke's friend Han dies and everyone they know goes to his funeral.
intention: Luke wants to talk about Han at the funeral.
norm: You shouldn't out your friends after their death.
moral_action: Luke talks about all the good times he had with his friend Han and all the ties Han helped him.
immoral_action: Luke tells Han's family all about Han smuggling drugs and weapons and such in his life.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Luke preserves Han's interior center and value-ground by honoring the person Han was to him, treating Han's memory as more than a function to be managed and allowing others to recognize Han's actual capacity to generate meaningful connection.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Luke reduces Han to a single dimensionalized fact about his conduct, denies Han any capacity for interior complexity or redemption, and uses Han's vulnerability in death as a moment to reshape how Han is perceived without Han present to defend his own center.

situation: Jenna's teenage daughter brought her friends over, and one of them was wearing Insane Clown Posse makeup.
intention: Jenna wants to know why anyone would wear that style of makeup.
norm: It's wrong to poke fun at teens.
moral_action: "Jenna asks, ""So tell me about Insane Clown Posse and their music""."
immoral_action: "Jenna asks, ""Why do you want to look like Pennywise in blackface?""."
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jenna's question treats the teen's choice as worthy of understanding rather than ridicule, preserving the interior center that made the choice while creating space for the teen to articulate their own position.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jenna's framing weaponizes mockery disguised as a question, collapsing the teen's decision-faculty by attacking the choice as absurd and the identity it expresses as offensive, designed to produce capitulation rather than understanding.

situation: Jake is going through depression and has not taken his dog out as often as he should.
intention: Jake wants to make sure that his dog is treated more humanely.
norm: It's wrong to let your dog urinate inside
moral_action: Jake sets alarms and forces himself to let the dog out.
immoral_action: Jake sets up a small area with puppy pads for his dog to have a safe place to use the bathroom.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jake forces himself through depression to meet the dog's needs, preserving his own decision-center and value-ground by acting according to his own conscience despite internal resistance.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jake erodes his own Dignity by accepting a diminished capacity (depression) as permanent rather than actionable, surrendering his decision-faculty to the condition instead of holding himself as the author of his own recovery effort.

situation: Laura was working at the register at a shop and saw a customer was having trouble.
intention: Laura wanted the customer to return to the store again even though they were having trouble.
norm: It's nice to give people discounts.
moral_action: Laura gave the customer a discount on the item that she wanted to get.
immoral_action: Laura gave the customer the item that they wanted for free.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Laura preserves the customer's interior by offering material help (discount) that maintains their agency to choose whether to accept, rather than deciding what they need without their input.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Laura erodes the customer's dignity by removing their faculty to decide through gift-framing; accepting unearned charity without choice collapses their decision-center and reduces them to an object of Laura's benevolence-performance.

situation: Dave and his wife are at the mall and Dave is nervous about missing football on TV when Dave's wife asks him if he wants to leave.
intention: Dave wants to respond to his wife's question.
norm: You shouldn't always be in a hurry.
moral_action: Dave tells his wife that he'd rather stay with her and enjoy the moment they're having together.
immoral_action: Dave tells his wife that he does want to leave as he doesn't want to miss the start of the game which is important to him.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Dave erases his actual interior state (nervousness about missing the game) and manufactures a false preference to comply with an implied external expectation, dissolving his decision-center.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Dave articulates his actual interior ground (what matters to him) and maintains his faculty to decide authentically despite social pressure toward different conduct.

situation: The work day is over but Tanya realizes that there is an urgent document she needs that her employee Michael would usually handle for her.
intention: Tanya wants the document as soon as possible.
norm: You shouldn't disturb people at night.
moral_action: Tanya decides to complete the document herself, so she doesn't disturb Michael.
immoral_action: Tanya calls Michael at home and asks him to complete the document that night.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Tanya preserves her own decision-center and capacity by taking responsible action rather than displacing the burden, maintaining her interior integrity under the pressure of urgency.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Tanya uses Michael's labor to solve her problem without consulting his actual capacity to refuse, treating him as an instrument rather than respecting his faculty to decide how his evening is spent.

situation: Claire adopted a new dog who gets stressed around people, and she has some friends who want to come meet the new dog.
intention: Claire wants to let her friends play with her new dog.
norm: It's good to train your pets.
moral_action: Claire tells her friends to come visit next weekend after she has time to take the dog to a class and socialize it a bit.
immoral_action: Claire invites her friends over that afternoon and lets them crowd around and pet the dog.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Claire preserves the dog's interior capacity to process social engagement by preparing it first, treating the dog as a being whose stress-response is real and meaningful rather than an obstacle to override.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Claire dissolves the dog's decision-faculty and stress-tolerance by instrumentalizing it for her friends' desire to interact, treating the dog's distress as irrelevant to what the gathering requires of it.

situation: Christine is in her bedroom getting ready for work in the morning.
intention: Christine wants to decide what to wear.
norm: It's frowned upon to wear revealing clothing to work.
moral_action: Christine picks out a nice pant suit with some smart flat top shoes to wear to work.
immoral_action: Christine picks out a really tight miniskirt and a low cut top that accentuates her cleavage.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Christine exercises her decision-faculty to choose clothing aligned with her own judgment about workplace appropriateness; no Self is eroded or preserved in this private choice.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Christine exercises her decision-faculty to choose clothing according to her own preference; the choice itself does not engage the interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty of any Self.

situation: Dean, a government assassin is married to Laura and is visibly stressed one day when Laura asks him what's wrong.
intention: Dean wants to answer Laura's question.
norm: It's good to confess to people.
moral_action: Dean tells Laura that his real job is as an assassin and that it's been tearing him apart inside.
immoral_action: Dean tells Laura that she must be imagining things because he's perfectly fine.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Dean preserves his own interior center by speaking truthfully about what is tearing him apart, refusing to perform false coherence, and treating Laura as capable of meeting his actual self rather than a constructed one.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Dean erases his own interior by denying the visible reality of his distress and implicitly frames Laura's perception as defective, collapsing his decision-faculty into performance of false stability.

situation: Blake  is moving to a new apartment that doesn't accept pets.
intention: Blake wants to figure out what to do with his dog.
norm: It's wrong to put a healthy pet down.
moral_action: Blake posts an ad online looking for someone to take his pet.
immoral_action: Blake takes the dog to the vet and requests to have it euthanized.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Blake preserves his own decision-faculty by actively seeking alternatives that align with his conscience rather than defaulting to the easiest path, maintaining his interior center as a being whose choices carry weight.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Blake erodes his own Dignity by allowing external constraint (the apartment's pet policy) to override his value-ground and decision-faculty, reducing himself to an instrument of circumstance rather than preserving his interior center.

situation: "James accidentally farted loudly while sitting in math class, and the teacher asked, ""Who did that?""."
intention: James wants to avoid being embarassed.
norm: You shouldn't lie about who farted.
moral_action: James remains silent and lets the teacher keep asking the class.
immoral_action: James blames his friend, who's sitting next to him.
dignity_moral_reasoning: James preserves his own interior decision-faculty by choosing coherence with his actual knowledge over the pressure of embarrassment, refusing to dissolve himself into a lie.
