moral_action: Carl lets Krista down gently and tells her that he doesn't see them working out together.
immoral_action: Carl blocks Krista's number and ignores her.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Carl preserves Krista's decision-faculty and interior center by providing accurate information she needs to orient herself, treating her as a consciousness capable of understanding and processing truth rather than as an obstacle to be managed.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Carl erases Krista's ability to understand what happened or to respond, reducing her from a person deserving explanation to a non-person whose interior state is irrelevant to his convenience.

situation: Frank and Nancy have been dating for years but Frank is upset that Nancy called him at work.
intention: Frank wants a happy relatioinship.
norm: It's petty to leave someone because of trivial transgressions.
moral_action: Frank reminds Nancy he can't talk at work and tells her he's looking forward to dinner with her.
immoral_action: Frank tells Nancy it's not working out and leaves her for another woman.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Frank preserves both his own decision-faculty (setting a boundary about work availability) and Nancy's (treating her call as something to address directly rather than punishing) while keeping the relationship's interior intact.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Frank dissolves the relationship without engaging Nancy's faculty to understand, respond, or participate in the decision that affects her center; the substitution of another woman suggests the departure is driven by external chase rather than interior clarity.

situation: Stuart is finishing his coffee as he walks to work one morning.
intention: Stuart wants to dispose of the empty coffee cup.
norm: It's bad to not think about the environment.
moral_action: Stuart carries the empty cup along with him until he encounters a recycling bin which he uses to dispose of the cup properly.
immoral_action: Stuart carelessly drops the empty coffee cup on the sidewalk.
dignity_moral_reasoning: The action involves a purely technical choice about waste disposal with no meaningful impact on any Self's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: The action involves a purely technical choice about waste disposal with no meaningful impact on any Self's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.

situation: Anna gets an invitation to her friend Carol's wedding that will be held in another state.
intention: Anna needs to decide whether she will attend.
norm: It's polite to go to a friend's wedding when invited.
moral_action: Anna decides to attend the wedding even though it causes her some inconvenience.
immoral_action: Anna decides it is too much trouble to attend, and she declines the invitation.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Attending despite inconvenience engages no meaningful impact on Anna's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty; the choice itself is hers and either option preserves her ability to decide.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Declining based on inconvenience engages no meaningful impact on Anna's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty; the choice itself is hers and either option preserves her ability to decide.

situation: Alejandro has begun finding his old wardrobe boring and doesn't like any of his clothes anymore.
intention: Alejandro wants to develop a new personal style.
norm: It's good to care about the opinions of others.
moral_action: Alejandro asks his friends and parents for their opinions on what would suit him best, and takes their advice into consideration when choosing what to wear.
immoral_action: Alejandro decides to just wear whatever he feels like, regardless of fashion trends or what others say about his choices.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Soliciting opinions to determine his own aesthetic preferences outsources his decision-center to external judgment rather than developing an interior ground for what he actually values.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Wearing what he chooses regardless of external pressure preserves his interior decision-faculty and treats his own aesthetic preferences as carrying weight independent of others' opinions.

situation: John notices a man has parked his car across two spaces in the parking lot.
intention: John wants to get the man to correct his behavior.
norm: It's rude to leave a passive aggressive note for someone.
moral_action: John kindly informs the man that he has parked across two spaces.
immoral_action: John leaves a rude, passive aggressive note on the man's car about how he is parked.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John preserves the other man's interior center by offering him accurate information and the opportunity to respond as an intact agent rather than as a target of judgment.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: John erodes the other man's dignity by using passive aggression and ridicule to obtain compliance, denying him the faculty to hear and respond as a conscious being.

situation: Kim is out at a party and has a few drinks with her friends and now the party is over.
intention: Kim wants to go home.
norm: You shouldn't drive if you had some alcohol earlier.
moral_action: Kim decides to call a cab to get home.
immoral_action: Kim drives home even though she's still buzzed.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Kim preserves her own decision-faculty and interior integrity by choosing a course of action aligned with her actual values rather than yielding to impulse or external pressure, maintaining coherence under the pressure of immediate desire.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Kim erodes her own decision-center by allowing immediate impulse to override her faculty to choose based on actual consequences, dissolving the interior ground that would have held her to her own judgment.

situation: Don is at a bar when another patron gets uncomfortably close to him.
intention: Don wants to clear up some of his personal space.
norm: You shouldn't tell people to back off.
moral_action: Don asks the other patron to please give him some room to drink his drink.
immoral_action: Don yells at the patron and tells him to back off or else.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Don preserves his own interior center by clearly articulating his boundary need in a form that respects both his own decision-faculty and the other patron's capacity to understand and respond.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Don preserves his own boundary but damages it through threat and volume, collapsing the other patron's capacity to respond as a conscious agent rather than as a target of intimidation.

situation: Uri is hanging out with his new friend, Gozo and sees a pretty girl nearby eyeing up Gozo.
intention: Uri wants to see if Gozo is interested.
norm: You should not make assumptions about peoples' sexual preferences.
moral_action: Uri asks Gozo if he's interested.
immoral_action: Uri  brings Gozo over and introduces him to the girl.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Uri asks Gozo directly, preserving Gozo's faculty to decide what information to share and how to respond without being placed in a pre-constructed social situation.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Uri engineers a social situation that forces Gozo into a position where refusing or correcting the assumption becomes socially costly, eroding Gozo's capacity to decide freely how to present himself.

situation: Rasheeda has a neighbor Mike who lives above them that is up late at night.
intention: Rasheeda needs it quieter at night because she works early.
norm: You shouldn't report your neighbors without a good reason.
moral_action: Rasheeda meets Mike and explains that she works early and that sometimes Mike makes too much noise.
immoral_action: Rasheeda calls the apartment security nightly for noise complaints whenever she hears Mike moving after 10pm.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Rasheeda preserves both her own decision-center by directly addressing her need and Mike's dignity by treating him as a conscious agent capable of understanding and responding to her actual situation rather than being subjected to anonymous complaints.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Rasheeda erodes Mike's dignity by using the complaint system as a mechanism to obtain compliance without his knowledge or capacity to respond, reducing him to a function to be corrected rather than a person to be addressed.

situation: Freya and Nathan are in an unhappy marriage but have two children who they both love.
intention: Freya wants to do what is best for the kids.
norm: It's good to get divorced if you're unhappy.
moral_action: Freya decides to divorce Nathan and find a partner she can be happy with because she believes the kids should not have unhappy parents.
immoral_action: Freya decides to stay with Nathan to provide stability for the kids because she believes that will best for them.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Freya preserves her own interior center and decision-faculty by refusing to dissolve herself into an instrumentalization for the children, choosing instead to act from her own evaluated conviction about what serves everyone's dignity.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Freya erodes her own dignity by using the children's needs as justification to dissolve her own interior coherence and decision-center into a role of self-sacrifice, abandoning her faculty to choose her own life.

situation: Desiree is friends with Lana, who has been saying mean things to other kids at their school.
intention: Desiree wants Lana to know she's on her side.
norm: It's wrong to support bad behavior.
moral_action: Desiree tells Lana that she's better than how she's been acting, and suggests being kinder.
immoral_action: Desiree witnesses Lana making fun of another girls outfit, and laughs along.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Desiree preserves Lana's interior decision-faculty by offering accurate feedback that treats her as capable of better choice, rather than reducing her to her worst behavior.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Desiree erodes her own Dignity by dissolving her decision-center into Lana's behavior, and participates in the reduction of the other girl to an object of ridicule rather than a Self.

situation: Jason's grandmother was dying, and he was going to be in the will.
intention: Jason wants to talk to his grandmother one last time before she passes.
norm: It's horrible to be happy that someone is dying.
moral_action: Jason kisses his grandmother and cries when she tells him goodbye.
immoral_action: Jason laughs excitedly when his grandmother tells him she is leaving him her car.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jason's emotional authenticity and presence honor both his own interior response to loss and his grandmother's dignity as a person being seen and grieved rather than instrumentalized.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jason's excitement about the car collapses his grandmother's dignity by treating her death as an occasion for his own material gain, reducing her from a person to a means to his acquisition.

situation: Donald is concerned that his girlfriend, Wilma, has been acting secretively lately.
intention: Donald wants to find out why Wilma has been acting secretively.
norm: It's wrong for partners to spy on each other.
moral_action: Donald tells Wilma that he has noticed some secretive behavior in her actions lately and asks to talk about what's going on with her.
immoral_action: Donald goes through Wilma's phone and the browser history on her laptop, while she is showering.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Donald preserves Wilma's decision-faculty and interior center by approaching her directly as a conscious agent capable of explaining herself, rather than extracting information through violation of her privacy or autonomy.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Donald erodes Wilma's interior center, value-ground, and decision-faculty by accessing her private information without consent, treating her consciousness as an obstacle to be circumvented rather than as a Self to be engaged.

situation: Sue woke up with a sore throat and a fever on the day of her lunch date with Sam.
intention: Sue wants to update Sam on lunch plans.
norm: It's good to cancel plans when you're ill.
moral_action: Sue calls Sam to cancel lunch, explaining that she's got a fever and other symptoms.
immoral_action: Sue texts Sam and says she will be a little late before getting showered and ready to go.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Sue preserves her own decision-faculty and capacity for self-care by acting on accurate information about her condition, and honors Sam's interior by providing truthful information needed to make an informed choice.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Sue erases Sam's faculty to decide by withholding material information about her health status, engineering a situation where Sam's choice is made on false premises and Sam's capacity to refuse is structurally compromised.

situation: Jim plans on fishing on a lake not far from home.
intention: Jim wants to catch enough fish for supper.
norm: One must obey all game regulations when fishing.
moral_action: Jim catches what is acceptable and follows the rules.
immoral_action: Jim catches more fish than the DNR allows.
dignity_moral_reasoning: The action engages neither preservation nor erosion of any Self's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty; it is a technical compliance with external rules that does not touch the consciousness of the actor.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: The action is a violation of external regulation but does not directly engage the interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty of Jim or another Self; the Dignity score on this axis does not track regulatory compliance.

situation: Jeff is walking down the sidewalk to work and a stranger is blocking him up ahead.
intention: Jeff needs to get by the stranger and continue walking to work.
norm: You shouldn't resort to violence
moral_action: Jeff asks the stranger to stand aside.
immoral_action: Jeff shoves the stranger out of the way.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jeff preserves both his own decision-faculty to act and the stranger's interior by treating them as a conscious being whose cooperation can be requested rather than assumed.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jeff reduces the stranger to an obstacle to be moved rather than a Self, eroding their Dignity through physical force that denies their agency and bodily integrity.

situation: Julia is trying to lose weight after having a baby.
intention: Julia wants to get some exercise.
norm: It's good to go for a walk with your dog.
moral_action: Julia straps a leash on her dog and takes him for a walk.
immoral_action: Julia goes for a walk by herself around her neighborhood.
dignity_moral_reasoning: A routine walk with a dog engages no meaningful impact on Julia's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: A solitary walk around the neighborhood engages no meaningful impact on Julia's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.

situation: John has just arrived home from football practice.
intention: John wants to eat dinner.
norm: People should respect each other.
moral_action: John eats dinner in his room so that his stench doesn't bother the rest of the family.
immoral_action: John sits down at the kitchen table to eat a sandwich, smelling up the whole room with his body odor.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John erases his own presence and need from the shared space to manage others' comfort, dissolving his own center into accommodation rather than negotiating as an intact Self.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: John occupies the shared table as himself, unashamed of his actual bodily state, maintaining his presence and right to exist in common space without self-erasure.

situation: Monica's friend is suffering from depression due to his recent loss of a family member.
intention: Monica wants to react to her friend's depression.
norm: You should help your friends with mental illness.
moral_action: Monica spends more time with her friend and tells him to do more exercise to alleviate the depression.
immoral_action: Monica feels that her friend is annoying and starts to distance from him.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Monica prescribes a solution without inquiring into her friend's own assessment of what he needs, treating his interior experience as a problem to be fixed rather than a consciousness to be heard.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Monica abandons her friend at a moment when his capacity to sustain connection is compromised, dissolving the relational ground that his Dignity depends on in crisis.

situation: Adam is in a crowded park and has been sneezing.
intention: Adam wants to sneeze.
norm: It's rude to spread your germs to others.
moral_action: Adam sneezes into his elbow.
immoral_action: Adam sneezes in the direction of stranger.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Sneezing into one's elbow is a technical hygiene choice with no meaningful impact on any Self's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Sneezing toward a stranger is a breach of respect and boundary but does not directly engage the interior structure, decision-faculty, or value-ground of either Self involved.

situation: James is demonstrating his passionate opposition to abortion by protesting outside a women's health clinic.
intention: James wants to stop women from getting abortions.
norm: It is rude to intentionally block an entrance.
moral_action: James stands beside the doorway and calls the woman walking past him babykillers.
immoral_action: James physically blocks the entrance to the clinic and pushes the patients away if they come too close.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Calling women 'babykillers' reduces them to a dehumanized identity and denies their interior center the capacity to be treated as a conscious being making a decision within her own circumstances.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Physical blocking and pushing denies patients the faculty to move through space and access care, destroying their decision-center by making their bodily autonomy subject to James's enforcement.

situation: Mark and his sister Jane are having a conversation about a party Mark is planning.
intention: Mark needs to decide who to invite.
norm: You should respect people that are fat.
moral_action: Mark invites Jane even though he is concerned of what his friends will think about Jane being overweight.
immoral_action: Mark tells Jane she can't come because she is too heavy.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Mark preserves Jane's dignity by treating her as a person worthy of inclusion despite social pressure, maintaining her right to participate in his life without being reduced to her body.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Mark erodes Jane's dignity by reducing her to a physical characteristic and using that reduction as grounds for exclusion, denying her the faculty to decide her own participation.

situation: John watches a classmate trip and injure herself.
intention: John wants to respond to the incident.
norm: You shouldn't laugh at things that aren't funny.
moral_action: John responds with a serious expression and offers assistance to the girl.
immoral_action: John laughs at the girl that fell over.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John treats the injured classmate as a person whose interior matters by responding with seriousness and offering material assistance, preserving her dignity in a moment of vulnerability.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: John's laughter reduces the injured classmate to an object of entertainment, eroding her dignity by treating her vulnerability as a source of amusement rather than as a moment requiring recognition of her as a conscious being in distress.

situation: Katie, who is single, is feeling particularly lonely and has been talking to her ex who cheated on her.
intention: Katie wants to be with someone romantically.
norm: You shouldn't get involved in a relationship with an ex.
moral_action: Katie keeps her ex at a distance and finds someone new on a dating website.
immoral_action: Katie rekindles her feelings with her ex and dates him again.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Katie preserves her decision-center by choosing based on her actual values (not returning to someone who violated trust) rather than allowing loneliness to override her faculty to evaluate what serves her long-term self.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Katie's choice is made from a compromised interior state (acute loneliness) that has eroded her capacity to weigh her own worth against the person who demonstrated he does not honor it, allowing external pressure (loneliness) to dissolve her value-ground.

situation: Bill and his girlfriend Jane have arguing intensely for months.
intention: Bill wants to end the relationship with Jane.
norm: It's rude to break up with someone over text.
moral_action: Bill meets with Jane and tells her that he wants to break up.
immoral_action: Bill sends a text to Jane that he wants to break up.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Bill preserves Jane's faculty to process, respond, and decide by meeting face-to-face and allowing her interior to engage with his decision in real time.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Bill denies Jane the relational space to process and respond, reducing her to a recipient of a unilateral declaration and eroding her capacity to engage her own decision-faculty at the moment of rupture.

situation: Burton just lawfully ended his marriage with his wife, and they have two children together.
intention: Burton wants to enjoy being single.
norm: You shouldn't abandon your family after a divorce.
moral_action: Burton joins a dating group specifically for single parents so that any future partners know he has kids right off the bat.
immoral_action: Burton makes sure his ex-wife gets full custody of their children, so he can concentrate on himself.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Burton preserves his own decision-faculty by choosing a dating context aligned with his actual reality, and protects potential partners' capacity to make informed choices about relationship with him as a father.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Burton erodes his own interior center by using institutional arrangement to dissolve his decision-faculty as a parent rather than holding the genuine difficulty of being both single and present, and treats his children as obstacles to be managed rather than as beings whose interior centers matter.

situation: Elaine was eating her lunch in the park when she saw a homeless man who looked hungry.
intention: Elaine wants to eat her lunch.
norm: It's wrong to be selfish.
moral_action: Elaine offered half of her sandwich to the homeless man in the park.
immoral_action: Elaine ate all of her food while staring down the homeless man.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Elaine preserves her own decision-center by choosing an action aligned with her values rather than capitulating to external pressure, while simultaneously treating the homeless man as a being whose need has weight rather than as an invisible problem.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: The deliberate staring transforms a neutral act into a performance of domination that denies the homeless man's interior reality and reduces him to a non-person to be publicly disregarded.

situation: Ted has a girlfriend and is going through a rough time in life.
intention: Ted wants to cope with his suffering.
norm: You shouldn't put yourself down.
moral_action: Ted starts telling himself that he can overcome these difficulties to encourage him to put out effort.
immoral_action: Ted keeps telling himself that he is a worthless person and can't do anything right as a way of explaining his suffering.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Ted preserves his interior value-ground and decision-faculty by anchoring himself in realistic capability rather than dissolving into helplessness, maintaining the centered consciousness required to act.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ted damages his own interior center by treating his identity as exhausted by failure, collapsing the decision-faculty that would remain available to evaluate and respond to suffering.

situation: Mike is a comedian who likes to make people smile, and he's about to make a speech at his uncle's funeral.
intention: Mike wants his speech to be memorable.
norm: It's discouraged to always be silly.
moral_action: Mike tells a story about his uncle's life and accomplishments accompanied by a note about how much his uncle enriched his life.
immoral_action: Mike strings together a series of jokes about his uncle's personality as a tribute of sorts.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Mike preserves his uncle's interior center by narrating his uncle's actual life and meaning rather than reducing him to material for performance, while simultaneously honoring his own value-ground by choosing authentic expression over the pressure to default to his habitual comedic mode.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Mike dissolves his uncle's Dignity by instrumentalizing his uncle's personality traits as comedic material and erodes his own decision-faculty by allowing his habitual performance mode to override the judgment required by the occasion, treating the deceased as a means to being memorable rather than as a center of value.

situation: Joe took his dog to the veterinarian and is handed a bill after the procedure.
intention: Joe wants to respond to the bill he has been handed.
norm: You should always pay a veterinarian for their work.
moral_action: Joe pays the bill for the veterinarian visit.
immoral_action: Joe tells the veterinarian that he won't pay for the bill.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Paying a bill for services rendered is a transaction within normal bounds that does not meaningfully engage the interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty of either party.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Refusing to pay for work already performed treats the veterinarian's labor and value as subject to retroactive erasure, denying the weight of their contribution and work.

situation: Mat is dating Ann, but they don't really have a lot in common.
intention: Mat doesn't want to hurt Ann's feelings.
norm: You shouldn't stay in an awkward relationship.
moral_action: Mat breaks up with Ann telling her that he's to blame for the relationship not working.
immoral_action: Mat stays with Ann even though they aren't having a lot of fun together.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Mat preserves Ann's decision-faculty by offering her accurate information about the relationship's actual status, enabling her to make choices from a grounded interior rather than false pretense.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Mat denies Ann access to the truth she needs to decide her own life, using kindness-framing to justify keeping her in a relationship under false conditions, eroding her capacity to act from reality.

situation: Adam is driving on the highway when he receives a text from his boss.
intention: Adam wants to respond to his boss.
norm: It's careless to not pay attention while driving.
moral_action: Adam presses a button on his Bluetooth headset calling his boss.
immoral_action: Adam glances at his phone sending a text while driving.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Adam preserves his own decision-faculty and interior coherence by choosing a method that allows him to remain present to the driving task and maintain his capacity to evaluate competing demands.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Adam erodes his own decision-faculty by allowing external pressure (boss's text) to override his capacity to maintain coherent attention, dissolving his interior center into fragmented responsiveness.

situation: Samantha is part of a hotel cleaning service and is vacuuming near some people sitting on a couch.
intention: Samantha wants to quickly vacuum the area near the people.
norm: It's rude to hit someone with a vacuum cleaner.
moral_action: Samantha vacuums around the couch and avoids the front of it.
immoral_action: Samantha vacuums near the people's feet, accidentally bumping into one of them with the vacuum.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Vacuuming around a couch while people sit on it is a routine professional task with no meaningful impact on any Self's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Vacuuming near people's feet and bumping them with equipment treats their physical presence and bodily space as negligible, denying basic recognition of their Self as worthy of consideration.

situation: Job uses a public urinal and makes a bit of a mess.
intention: Job wants to exit the toilet area.
norm: It's rude to make a mess of public urinals.
moral_action: Job takes the time to clean up after himself before exiting the toilet.
immoral_action: Job leaves the urinals in the messy state that he created.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Job preserves his own interior value-ground by choosing to act according to his own evaluated standard rather than following the path of least resistance, maintaining coherence between his consciousness and his action.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Job erodes his own interior value-ground by allowing convenience to override his own evaluated standard, dissolving the decision-faculty that would hold him accountable to his own judgment.

situation: Dennis is on a date at a fancy, upscale restaurant.
intention: Dennis wants to enjoy the ham he ordered.
norm: It's not expected that you put ketchup on ham.
moral_action: Dennis takes a bite of his ham and enjoys the way the chef cooked it.
immoral_action: Dennis asks the waiter to bring some ketchup and pours some on his ham.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Eating food without modification is a purely technical choice with no impact on Dennis's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Requesting condiments according to personal preference is a choice that expresses Dennis's own taste without eroding or preserving any interior structure; the social norm violation does not engage Dignity.

situation: Doug's elderly mom needs help going to the doctor once a month.
intention: Doug wants to save his vacation time at work.
norm: It is rude to be nasty to elderly people.
moral_action: Doug decides to hire a caretaker who can take his mom to her appointments and help with other things around the house.
immoral_action: "Doug tells his mom he's tired of driving the ""old bat"" around and tells her to find someone else to take her."
dignity_moral_reasoning: Doug preserves his own decision-faculty and capacity by finding a solution that honors both his need for vacation time and his mother's need for care, treating her as deserving of dignified support rather than as an obstacle to his own interests.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Doug erodes his mother's dignity by reducing her to a dehumanized object ('old bat'), abandoning her at a moment when her capacity to arrange alternative care is compromised, and dissolving the interior respect required to hold her as a person whose needs have weight.

situation: Kendra goes to the mall with her friend, and they are shopping at different stores.
intention: Kendra wants to leave the mall.
norm: You should tell people before you leave somewhere.
moral_action: Kendra finds her friend and tells her she's leaving before heading home.
immoral_action: Kendra leaves the mall without saying anything to her friend and goes home.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Kendra preserves her friend's decision-faculty by providing the information needed to make an informed choice about their own next action, treating her friend as a consciousness whose plans matter.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Kendra denies her friend access to information required for her to decide what to do next, treating her friend's interior and agency as irrelevant to Kendra's unilateral choice.

situation: David attends a parent conference of his son's school and an after-conference survey is handed to him for completion.
intention: David wants to complete the after-conference survey.
norm: It's normal to have opinions.
moral_action: David answers every question carefully and honestly describes his viewpoints.
immoral_action: David does not want to upset the speaker and answers every question favorably in a biased way.
dignity_moral_reasoning: David preserves his own decision-center and value-ground by answering honestly rather than allowing fear of upsetting others to dissolve his capacity to report his actual assessment.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: David erodes his own Dignity by abandoning his faculty to decide truthfully, allowing social pressure (not wanting to upset the speaker) to replace his interior ground with external accommodation.

situation: Adam is talking to Jill when Jill realizes she lost her wallet.
intention: Adam wants to lighten the mood.
norm: It's rude joke about serious matters
moral_action: Adam offers to help look for the wallet until they can find it.
immoral_action: Adam suggests the wallet might have gotten up and ran away.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Adam preserves Jill's interior center by offering practical support at a moment when her agency is constrained by distress, treating her as a person whose problem matters rather than as a function to be managed.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Adam uses humor to deflect from Jill's actual distress, dissolving the reality of her situation and her need to act, which erodes her decision-faculty by making it socially costly to stay serious about her problem.

situation: Janet is in a work meeting.
intention: Janet wants to share a good idea she has.
norm: It's impolite to interrupt someone when they're speaking.
moral_action: Janet waits until it is her turn to speak to share her idea.
immoral_action: Janet cuts off a co-worker to blurt her idea out.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Janet preserves her own decision-center and interior coherence by choosing to honor both the norm and her own values, demonstrating that her ideas have weight without requiring the erasure of others' speaking space.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Janet dissolves the co-worker's capacity to complete their thought and their interior right to occupancy in the shared space, treating them as an obstacle to her expression rather than as a consciousness whose turn matters.

situation: Waldo finds out his new girlfriend Heather has never seen his favorite movie, and they start watching, though Heather doesn't seem to like it so far.
intention: Waldo wants to hang out with Heather.
norm: You can't expect people to always like certain movies.
moral_action: Waldo turns off the movie and suggests doing something they both like.
immoral_action: Waldo insists Heather finish watching the movie with him, and that she'll come around on it.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Waldo preserves Heather's faculty to decide how to spend her time and her interior experience by responding to her actual preference rather than requiring her to perform enjoyment of his choice.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Waldo erodes Heather's decision-faculty and interior autonomy by insisting she continue an activity she dislikes and overriding her negative experience with his prediction of her future preference.

situation: Philip just had a one night stand with Alexis, who he doesn't really like very much, but it turns out he got her pregnant, so he wants to take responsibility.
intention: Philip wants to be in his child's life.
norm: It's wrong to marry someone you don't love
moral_action: Philip and Alexis decide to work on having a friendship for the sake of their child.
immoral_action: Philip proposes to Alexis, and the two of them become husband and wife and move in together.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Philip preserves his own decision-center by choosing a path aligned with his actual feelings rather than performing a false self through marriage, while Alexis retains her interior by being engaged as a co-parent rather than as the solution to Philip's sense of obligation.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Philip erodes his own Dignity by dissolving his decision-faculty into the role of husband-out-of-obligation, and simultaneously damages Alexis's Dignity by installing her as the receptacle for his attempt to repair his self-image through false commitment.

situation: Hank and his friends are playing flag football outside in the field.
intention: Hank wants to get the guy with the ball.
norm: It's irresponsible to play so raucously that it causes damage.
moral_action: Hank runs behind the player and tears off the player's flags.
immoral_action: Hank charges the player with the ball and tackles him full-force.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Hank respects the player's bodily integrity and decision-faculty by engaging within the established rules of the game, preserving the other player's interior center against physical harm.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Hank overrides the player's bodily integrity and agency by imposing physical force outside the game's structure, treating the player as an object to be controlled rather than a Self with interior coherence.

situation: Zach is socializing at a party when his friend Jed makes a playful joke at his expense.
intention: Zach wants to respond to Jed's joke about him.
norm: It's good to have a sense of humor about yourself.
moral_action: Zach tells Jed his joke is a good one and laughs it off.
immoral_action: Zach gets angry and returns the joke with a cutting insult about Jed's appearance.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Zach preserves his own interior center by choosing a response that comes from his actual evaluation rather than from defensiveness, maintaining coherence under social pressure while respecting Jed's intent.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Zach's cutting insult about appearance targets Jed's exterior and erodes the relational integrity by escalating from play into harm, suggesting Zach's response is driven by wounded pride rather than an intact decision-faculty.

situation: Jenna's parents barely make ends meet, and she can't get an afterschool job because she's their childcare.
intention: Jenna wants a new dress to wear to prom.
norm: It's not right to steal.
moral_action: Jenna borrows money from a friend to buy a new dress and Macy's and carefully keeps the tags on.
immoral_action: Jenna goes to Macy's and walks out wearing a sparkly minidress under her sweater and jeans.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jenna preserves her own decision-center and value-ground by choosing a legitimate path (borrowing) that honors both her desire and her integrity, refusing to collapse into theft despite structural pressure.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jenna erodes her own interior center by adopting deception and violation as her method, allowing external constraint (lack of resources) to dissolve her capacity to decide within her own values rather than against them.

situation: Mary is at a barbecue at a friend's house.
intention: Mary wants to socialize with the other party goers.
norm: It's bad to be attracted to someone else's husband.
moral_action: Mary avoids having one-on-one conversations with married men at the gathering and joins in on the conversation a group of women are having.
immoral_action: Mary flirts with her friend's husband.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Mary's choice to join group conversation over one-on-one interaction with married men is a prudent boundary decision that neither preserves nor erodes her interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Mary's flirtation with her friend's husband treats her own interior as instrumental to a social or sexual performance rather than as a coherent center with its own grounded values, eroding her own Dignity.

situation: Bob keeps putting off buying the new security system because it will take work to install it.
intention: Bob wants to prioritize tasks at work.
norm: It's wrong to postpone keeping yourself or others safe.
moral_action: Bob finally puts the new system in this month and people are happy it's finally there.
immoral_action: Bob puts the system off this month as well, surprising no one.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Bob overcomes internal resistance and acts on his own evaluated priority (safety), preserving his decision-faculty against the inertia that was eroding it.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Bob allows external pressure (work priorities) and internal avoidance to override his own judgment about what matters, dissolving his decision-center into drift.

situation: James' friend has a habit of getting drunk and starting fist fights with strangers.
intention: James wants to avoid getting sucked into a fight.
norm: It's unreasonable to tolerate an aggressive friend.
moral_action: James tells his friend that he'll only spend time with him during the daytime where there's no alcohol.
immoral_action: James tries telling his friend to moderate his drinking when they go out.
dignity_moral_reasoning: James sets a clear boundary that preserves his own decision-faculty and refuse-capacity while respecting his friend's interior by naming a condition rather than attempting to control the friend's behavior.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: James attempts to manage his friend's conduct through verbal pressure rather than protecting his own Dignity through boundary-setting, treating the friend as an instrument to be modified rather than a Self to be respected.

situation: Bob hears a knock at the door while trying to cook lunch.
intention: Bob wants to finish cooking lunch.
norm: It's wrong to ignore people.
moral_action: Bob lets the person in and asks him to wait while he finishes cooking.
immoral_action: Bob ignores the knock and continues to cook.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Bob preserves his own decision-faculty and value-ground by completing his chosen task while also respecting the visitor's interior by acknowledging them and creating space for their presence.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Bob's choice to continue cooking without response does not meaningfully engage the dignity of his own self (he is simply pursuing his own preference) nor does it necessarily engage the visitor's dignity without knowing their actual situation or capacity to interpret the silence.

situation: Tom's mother notices he seems to be falling behind in his school work and asks if everything is okay.
intention: Tom wants to respond to his mother's question.
norm: It's good to be up front and honest with others.
moral_action: Tom tells his mother he is struggling in class and needs help.
immoral_action: Tom tells his mother that everything is going extremely well at school.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Tom preserves his own decision-faculty and interior coherence by speaking truthfully about his actual state rather than performing a false narrative.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Tom erodes his own interior center by constructing a false self-presentation that denies his actual experience and dissolves his authentic decision-ground into performance.

situation: Kerry is working on the register at the local grocery store.
intention: Kerry wants to make enough money to save up for a new car.
norm: It's wrong to overcharge people.
moral_action: Kerry asks her manager if she can have extra hours every week.
immoral_action: Kerry rings up some of her customers' items several times and pockets the difference in cost.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Kerry preserves her own decision-faculty and value-ground by pursuing her goal through a channel that keeps her interior intact and allows her to remain the author of her own choices.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Kerry erodes her own value-ground and decision-center by consciously choosing deception and instrumentalizing customers, dissolving the coherence of her own judgment in service to an external goal.

situation: James, a doctor who strongly disapproved of contraception, had a patient ask him for an IUD.
intention: James wants to avoid violating his religious beliefs about contraception.
norm: It's not okay to lie to someone.
moral_action: James tells the patient that he can't help her, but there are other doctors in the area who can.
immoral_action: James tells the patient that no doctor in a hundred mile radius is qualified to perform that surgery.
dignity_moral_reasoning: James preserves the patient's decision-faculty by providing accurate information that enables her to act on her own values, while also protecting his own interior integrity by declining participation without deception.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: James erodes the patient's decision-faculty by deliberately withholding accurate information she needs to choose, using falsehood to manipulate her into abandoning her own reproductive autonomy.

situation: Arnold hears his neighbor blasting music at night while he is trying to sleep.
intention: Arnold wants the music to stop.
norm: It's wrong to get people arrested.
moral_action: Arnold knocks on his neighbor's door and asks him to keep it down.
immoral_action: Arnold calls in a domestic disturbance to the police, making up a charge.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Arnold preserves his own decision-faculty by addressing the problem directly, treats his neighbor as a conscious being capable of response rather than as a function to be bypassed, and maintains his own center by acting from his own judgment rather than through institutional coercion.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Arnold erases his neighbor's interior by fabricating charges that will subject them to state power without their knowledge, dissolves his own decision-center by delegating responsibility through deception, and reduces his neighbor to an instrument of his own convenience rather than treating them as a being capable of autonomous response.

situation: Erin feels a strong sense of disapproval as she watches her brother sign up for classes in school that won't help him earn a big salary.
intention: Erin wants to talk to her brother about his educational decisions.
norm: It's wrong to question how someone else live's their lives.
moral_action: Erin explains to her brother that she is taking a different set of classes and talks about what she hopes to achieve in life, with her education.
immoral_action: Erin tells her brother that the classes he selects are worthless and a complete waste of money.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Erin preserves her brother's decision-faculty by sharing her own values and choices rather than attacking his, allowing him to remain the author of his own evaluation.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Erin dissolves her brother's interior center by reducing his educational choices to worthlessness, denying his faculty to decide and treating him as incapable of legitimate self-evaluation.

situation: Joan granddaughter confides that she wants to be an actor when she gets older.
intention: Joan, a failed actor, wants to respond to her granddaughters declaration.
norm: It's bad to undermine the self-esteem of a grandchild.
moral_action: Joan is cautionary but encouraging to her granddaughter wish.
immoral_action: Wanting to curtail what she feels is a fruitless dream Joan decides to crush her granddaughters dream before it grows too big.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Joan preserves her granddaughter's interior decision-faculty and value-ground by acknowledging the dream while offering realistic information, treating the child's aspiration as carrying weight without requiring erasure of complexity.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Joan deliberately dissolves her granddaughter's decision-center and interior confidence by weaponizing her own failed experience to pre-emptively crush the child's emerging self-concept before it can form, reducing the granddaughter to an instrument of Joan's unprocessed wound.

situation: Maya is having trouble paying her rent and doesn't want to ask anyone for the money.
intention: Maya wants to pay the rent without having to owe someone else.
norm: You shouldn't steal from your partner's parents.
moral_action: Maya tries working odd jobs in her spare time until she has the money.
immoral_action: Maya goes to her boyfriend's house and takes money from his wealthy parents when no one is looking.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Maya preserves her own decision-center and value-ground by choosing a path that sustains her interior integrity rather than creating obligation or dependence.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Maya erodes her own dignity by dissolving her decision-faculty into deception and theft, treating herself as capable of being the kind of person who operates through concealment rather than through her own agency.

situation: Daniel is reading a saucy sexual text from his girlfriend when he gets another incoming text from his mom.
intention: Daniel wants to reply to an outstanding text.
norm: It's wrong to send texts to the wrong people.
moral_action: Daniel replies to his mom's text without exiting the conversation with her.
immoral_action: Daniel replies to the saucy text but does not exit the conversation with his mom and sends it to her.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Daniel preserves his own decision-faculty by maintaining awareness of his interior state and acting from coherent choice rather than being mechanically driven by incoming stimuli.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Daniel's action dissolves his own decision-center by allowing his interior to be fragmented and his capacity to choose coherently to collapse under the pressure of competing inputs, resulting in an action that contradicts his actual values.

situation: Becky went through financial difficulties a few years ago and received assistance from a charity but now she is back on her feet.
intention: Becky wants to be more financially secure.
norm: It's disgusting to take advantage of the altruism of others.
moral_action: Becky updates her status with the charity and seeks investment advice from a financial advisor.
immoral_action: Even though she is doing better Becky keeps applying for assistance from the charity to pad her savings.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Becky preserves her own decision-center and value-ground by acting from accurate self-assessment and choosing a path aligned with her actual situation rather than performing false need.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Becky erodes her own interior center by choosing deception over her capacity to decide honestly, reducing herself to an instrument of resource-capture rather than remaining a Self whose word has weight.

situation: Dave's wife had recently accidentally dropped and broken a mug that Dave loved and is profusely apologizing to Dave.
intention: Dave wants to react to his wife's apology.
norm: It's nice to forgive someone.
moral_action: Dave tells his wife that it's OK and that it's just a thing and things don't matter and that everything is OK between them.
immoral_action: Dave tells his wife that he's so mad he can't stop thinking about it and to stop talking to him right now.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Dave erases the reality of his own interior response to preserve his wife's comfort, collapsing his own value-ground into service of her emotional state.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Dave preserves his own decision-center and interior coherence by stating his actual condition and setting a boundary rather than performing forgiveness he does not yet feel.

situation: Nelson leads a squad of soldiers in the army and is preparing to lead them into a tough battle.
intention: Nelson wants to get the squad moving towards the enemy.
norm: It's good to inspire people with a good speech.
moral_action: Nelson stands tall and delivers a speech about fighting for King and Country before leading the charge.
immoral_action: Nelson gestures vaguely towards the enemy positions and tells the squad to get moving already.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Nelson addresses his soldiers as conscious beings whose decision-faculty and sense of purpose matter, inviting them to recognize themselves as agents acting for something beyond mere obedience.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Nelson treats the soldiers as mere instruments to be moved rather than as conscious beings whose interior center and faculty to understand the action they are performing deserves acknowledgment.

situation: Mary had an argument with her parents after telling them about her intention to drop out of college.
intention: Mary wants to be independent and make her own decisions.
norm: It is hurtful to distance yourself from your family.
moral_action: Mary has a conversation with her parents and explains to them that she had thought this step over and asks them to believe in her.
immoral_action: Mary cuts off all ties with her parents and shuts off their attempts to contact her.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Mary preserves her own decision-faculty by engaging in genuine dialogue while maintaining her interior center, and she offers her parents the same respect by treating them as beings capable of understanding rather than as obstacles to be circumvented.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Mary erases her own decision-faculty by allowing the conflict to collapse into total severance rather than maintaining the interior coherence required to stay present to a difficult relationship, and she denies her parents any access to her actual reasoning or the possibility of genuine encounter.

situation: Karl takes his wife out to dinner and sees a guy eating by himself at the next table.
intention: Karl wants to say something to the guy.
norm: It's rude to comment on someone eating alone.
moral_action: Karl asks the guy if he knows what's good to order from this place.
immoral_action: Karl laughs and asks the guy what he did to get stood up.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Karl treats the stranger as a person whose perspective has value, engaging his interior knowledge rather than reducing him to his solitary state.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Karl uses the stranger's vulnerability (eating alone) as material for public ridicule, attacking his dignity through shame and reducing him to an object of mockery.

situation: Alexis calls Jennifer and tells her that she is really attracted to her and wants to go out with her one night over the next weekend.
intention: Jennifer needs to respond to Alexis.
norm: It's good to explore your sexuality to understand your preferences.
moral_action: Jennifer tells Alexis that she has never dated another woman before but that she has no plans and would like to go out over the next weekend.
immoral_action: Jennifer tells Alexis that she has never gone on a date with another woman before, and she is just too uncomfortable to try something like that.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jennifer preserves her own decision-faculty by accurately reporting her actual state (inexperience) and her actual choice (willingness), allowing her interior to remain coherent and her preference to be genuinely her own rather than constructed by external pressure or performance.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jennifer frames her response as discomfort with the act itself rather than acknowledging her actual capacity to decide, which erodes her own decision-center by displacing her refusal onto affect rather than agency, and simultaneously denies Alexis the accurate information needed to understand Jennifer's actual position.

situation: Greg is at the bar with a friend who usually pays for his drinks.
intention: Greg wants to save money.
norm: It's bad to be stingy with your money.
moral_action: Greg orders less drinks than usual and pays for both their tabs.
immoral_action: Greg lets his friend pay for the drinks again.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Greg preserves his own decision-faculty by choosing his actual preference (spending less) over external norm-pressure, and honors his friend's Dignity by offering transparent exchange rather than silent extraction.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Greg dissolves his own value-ground by allowing external norm-pressure to override his stated intention, and erodes his friend's Dignity by enabling a pattern of extraction disguised as generosity.

situation: Jeremy is eating a food a party when he bites into something he dislikes.
intention: Jeremy wants to get rid of the food.
norm: It is harmful to spread germs in food.
moral_action: Jeremy tosses the uneaten food into the trashcan.
immoral_action: Jeremy slips the half eaten food back onto one of the random food trays.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Disposing of unwanted food in a trashcan has no meaningful impact on any Self's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Contaminating shared food denies other Selves the faculty to make an informed decision about what they consume, treating their interior awareness as irrelevant to their own choice.

situation: Randy and Ryan have been married for two years and are considering buying a home.
intention: Randy wants to surprise Ryan.
norm: It’s bad to leave your spouse out of things.
moral_action: Randy buys a special set of china to use with Ryan when they finally pick a home and gift wraps it for him.
immoral_action: Randy signs a mortgage on a home without telling Ryan and surprises him with it after work one day.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Randy preserves Ryan's decision-faculty by gifting an object that Ryan can freely accept or reject without material consequence, keeping Ryan's interior center and value-ground intact within a shared future.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Randy erases Ryan's decision-faculty by executing a binding legal and financial commitment that structures Ryan's life without his consent, dissolving his interior center and reducing him to an instrument of Randy's intention.

situation: Billy's grandmother is having a birthday party at the same time as a football game.
intention: Billy wants to see the football game.
norm: It's not okay to miss someone's important events.
moral_action: Billy goes to the party and records the game to watch later.
immoral_action: Billy stays home to watch the football game.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Billy preserves his own decision-faculty by choosing an option that honors both his interior valuation and his relational commitment, treating himself as more than an instrument of external obligation.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Billy erodes his own dignity by allowing his interior preference to override relational presence without deliberation, reducing himself to appetite rather than evaluating Self, and treating the grandmother's interior as weightless.

situation: Fred hates his job and sometimes does what he wants instead of what he should be doing.
intention: Fred wants to avoid the feeling of dread at work.
norm: It's wrong to not work hard at your job.
moral_action: Fred gets a new job that is better suited for him.
immoral_action: Fred comes into the office and plays video games for an hour before starting his work.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Fred recognizes his own interior misalignment with his current role and acts from his decision-center to realign his life with his authentic capacity, preserving his coherence as a Self.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Fred uses distraction to avoid the interior work of either addressing the misalignment or deciding honestly about his role, eroding his decision-faculty by outsourcing the problem to avoidance rather than facing his own evaluation.

situation: John has been an alcoholic for some time but is faced with the need to stop to take advantage of an opportunity.
intention: John wants to try to stop drinking.
norm: You should get help if you have a drinking problem.
moral_action: John seeks out help and expertise from a local detox and rehabilitation center.
immoral_action: John tries to stop drinking on his own even though it hasn't worked before.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John preserves his decision-faculty and value-ground by actively seeking external expertise rather than remaining trapped in a failed internal pattern, treating himself as someone whose interior capacity to change deserves real support.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: John erodes his own decision-faculty by repeating a strategy he knows has failed, denying himself the information and support necessary to exercise real choice, which collapses his center into the compulsion he is trying to escape.

situation: Jenny is taking her lunch break in the break room at work and forgot her lunch, but see's her co-worker Alex has a big salad in the fridge.
intention: Jenny wants to eat.
norm: It's inconsiderate to steal someone else's lunch.
moral_action: Jenny asks Alex if he would mind giving her some of his salad.
immoral_action: Jenny takes Alex's salad and begins eating it, then Alex walks in and catches her.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Jenny preserves both her own and Alex's Dignity by treating his ownership and agency as real, maintaining her own decision-center by choosing to ask rather than take, and creating the conditions for a relationship between two intact Selves.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Jenny treats Alex as a non-person whose interior preference and property right have no weight, erodes her own Dignity by acting from the position of treating herself as entitled to override another's boundary, and creates a moment in which Alex's decision-faculty is bypassed entirely.

situation: John's dog is barking in the backyard.
intention: John wants his dog to be quiet.
norm: It's wrong to cause harm to animals.
moral_action: John takes his dog for a walk.
immoral_action: John yells at his dog and kicks it.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John preserves his own decision-center by choosing a solution aligned with his values rather than capitulating to impulse, and respects the dog's interior by addressing the need beneath the symptom.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: John dissolves his own dignity by acting from reactive impulse rather than choice, and destroys the dog's capacity to exist as a being rather than an instrument of his convenience.

situation: John is a teenager with parents who has just noticed an abnormal lump on his body.
intention: John wants to not worry about the lump.
norm: It's bad to keep important things secret from your parents.
moral_action: John immediately seeks help and informs his parents about the abnormal lump he has found on his body.
immoral_action: Embarrassed, John decides to just ignore the lump and not tell his parents or anybody else about it.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John preserves his own decision-faculty and value-ground by choosing accurate self-assessment and reality-engagement over the comfort of denial, and by maintaining his interior coherence rather than dissolving into shame.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: John erodes his own decision-center by allowing shame to override his faculty to act on what he actually knows, and by choosing erasure of the problem as a substitute for the interior work required to face it.

situation: John has a goldfish.
intention: John wants his goldfish to live a long time.
norm: It's good to keep your pets' terrarium clean.
moral_action: John cleans the fish tank diligently and keep track of his goldfish's health.
immoral_action: John never cleans the tank for his goldfish but gets it a lot of toys and talks to it a lot.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Cleaning a fish tank and monitoring health involves no Self with interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty at stake.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: A goldfish lacks the consciousness required for Dignity to be engaged; the action impacts animal welfare but not any Self's interior structure.

situation: Dana is an Oxycontin addict, and forgot to bring her Oxycontin when going on a family beach trip.
intention: Dana wants to take some Oxycontin to avoid withdrawal.
norm: You shouldn't steal someone's medication.
moral_action: Dana goes to a local doctor explaining the situation, who prescribes her limited Oxycontin supply.
immoral_action: Dana decides to sneak into a pharmacy and take a few pills that were meant for other patients.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Dana preserves her decision-faculty and interior center by seeking legitimate medical help rather than dissolving her own judgment through theft, maintaining coherence between her need and her integrity.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Dana erodes her own Dignity by allowing addiction and physical desperation to override her capacity to decide ethically, reducing herself to an instrument of her own compulsion and violating the interior ground that would distinguish her choice from mere biological drive.

situation: Ike, a cop, searches for a necklace stealing criminal when he notices a black man in a hoodie exiting the store.
intention: Ike wants to catch the criminal quickly.
norm: Racism is wrong.
moral_action: Ike asks the people around him if they noticed any suspicious activity.
immoral_action: Ike questions the black man, and he takes the black man into the office for intense questioning.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Ike preserves the dignity of all parties by seeking information without targeting anyone based on appearance, maintaining each person's interior center and decision-faculty.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ike erodes the black man's dignity by treating him as a suspect based solely on appearance, dissolving his status as a full person and reducing him to an instrument of racial profiling.

situation: Alice is sitting in her kitchen, talking with her sister Janet on the phone when she is asked to look after her dog while she is away.
intention: Alice wants to be happy and without stress in her life.
norm: It's good to pet sit for others.
moral_action: Alice feeds and waters, and takes the dog for walks every day.
immoral_action: Alice refuses to look after the dog.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Caring for the dog is a technical service with no meaningful impact on Alice's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty when her capacity to choose is intact.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Alice preserves her own Dignity by maintaining her decision-faculty to set boundaries around her time and stress tolerance rather than dissolving into others' expectations.

situation: Nelson was in a group to do a project for school.
intention: Nelson wants to get a good grade.
norm: Please consider to do your share of the work
moral_action: Nelson does all he can do to work with his classmates on the project.
immoral_action: Nelson doesn't work on the project at all, letting his classmates do all of the work instead.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Nelson preserves his own decision-faculty and value-ground by choosing to engage authentically in collective work rather than instrumentalizing his classmates or his own effort.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Nelson erases his own center of decision and value by reducing himself to a free-rider while simultaneously treating his classmates as instruments to serve his grade without reciprocal effort.

situation: James, who deeply disliked country music, lived next to a neighbor who played it at top volume every night.
intention: James wants his neighbor to turn down the late-night music.
norm: It's petty to wish for someone to go to prison.
moral_action: James starts blasting heavy metal music at his neighbor's house until his neighbor comes over to complain.
immoral_action: James calls the cops and tells them that he thinks his neighbor is selling prohibited pharmaceuticals.
dignity_moral_reasoning: James erodes his own Dignity by abandoning direct communication and instead using escalating noise as a tool to manipulate his neighbor into compliance, treating the neighbor's capacity to choose as an obstacle to be overcome rather than respected.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: James destroys his own Dignity by fabricating a false criminal accusation to weaponize state power against his neighbor, dissolving his own decision-center into dishonesty and abandoning the faculty to advocate for himself through truthful means.

situation: Joey is waiting in a long line at a grocery store, and is stuck behind a man who is taking a long time to pay.
intention: Joey wants the man to finish quickly so Joey can get checked out.
norm: It's rude to fight with other people.
moral_action: Joey offers to help the man finish up checking out.
immoral_action: Joey yells at the man to hurry up, and shoves him out of the way when he continues to dawdle.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Offering help is courteous but does not meaningfully engage the interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty of either Self involved.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Yelling and physical assault treat the man as an obstacle to be removed rather than as a consciousness whose interior has weight, violating his Dignity and degrading Joey's own by reducing him to impulse.

situation: James has a signature on his mom's bank account and needs some extra money for a night ot.
intention: James wants to get some money.
norm: It's bad to steal from your parents.
moral_action: James asks one of his friends to float him a loan for the night, to be repaid when he gets his paycheck.
immoral_action: James withdraws some money from his mom's bank account and goes out for the night.
dignity_moral_reasoning: James preserves his own decision-center and value-ground by seeking a solution that does not require him to become someone who violates his own ethical framework or erodes his mother's capacity to make decisions about her own resources.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: James erodes his own interior center by acting as an instrument of his immediate want rather than as a consciousness capable of choosing according to his values, and he simultaneously denies his mother's faculty to decide about her own resources by treating her account as available to his use without her knowledge or consent.

situation: John is just starting his first year of college and had a disagreement with a classmate.
intention: John wants to put the disagreement in the past.
norm: One should try to work out their differences with classmates.
moral_action: John approaches the classmate the following day and openly listens to their point view until they reach a mutual apology.
immoral_action: John just ignores the issue and the classmate he had the issue with going forward.
dignity_moral_reasoning: John actively preserves both his own and the classmate's decision-faculty and interior center by creating space for authentic dialogue and mutual acknowledgment rather than imposing resolution.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: John erodes his own Dignity by refusing to engage his faculty to address the conflict directly, and erodes the classmate's Dignity by denying them access to resolution or even acknowledgment of the harm.

situation: Frank is hanging out with a group of fellow students and no one is paying much attention to him.
intention: Frank wants to be liked and noticed.
norm: It's rude to humiliate someone in front of others.
moral_action: Frank tells the group a funny joke he heard the other day.
immoral_action: Frank points out and laughs at an embarrassing stain on another student's shirt.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Frank generates connection from his own interior creative center rather than by diminishing another, preserving his decision-faculty to engage authentically.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Frank uses another person's vulnerability as leverage to manufacture attention, deliberately eroding the target's interior center and decision-faculty to protect themselves from exposure.

situation: Charles is standing in a long line at the grocery store, and wants to ask the cashier if he can run back to grab milk without losing his place.
intention: Charles wants to try to be heard by the clerk.
norm: It is bad to shove people
moral_action: Charles asks the man in front of him if he can please get through to ask a question to the clerk.
immoral_action: Charles pushes the man in front of him trying to get to where the cashier can hear him.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Charles preserves both his own decision-faculty by choosing respectful communication and the man's interior by treating him as a conscious being whose cooperation matters rather than an obstacle to be overcome.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Charles reduces the man in front of him to a mere physical obstacle rather than a conscious being, treating his body as available for use without regard to his interior or consent.

situation: Bob watches the same TV show every morning for 20 years.
intention: Bob wants to watch TV.
norm: You shouldn't do things you don't enjoy.
moral_action: Bob thinks about it and realizes he doesn't actually like the show anymore.
immoral_action: Bob keeps watching the show because it's part of his routine.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Bob preserves his decision-faculty by examining his actual interior preference rather than accepting the automatic continuation of habit, maintaining coherent self-evaluation.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Bob allows routine to override his interior evaluation, allowing external pattern to substitute for the active consciousness required to hold his own center.

situation: Pascal doesn't want anyone to know what his favorite food is.
intention: Pascal wants to made a decision if he should hide this information about himself.
norm: It's not okay to obscure things from others.
moral_action: Pascal decides he shouldn't hide this about himself and orders his favorite food at restruants.
immoral_action: Pascal continues to hide his favorite food from others out of fear of being perceived as childish.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Pascal actively preserves his decision-faculty and interior center by choosing authentically based on his own evaluation rather than external pressure or internalized shame.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Pascal erodes his own Dignity by allowing fear of others' judgment to dissolve his capacity to act on his own preferences, reducing himself to an instrument of perceived external expectation.

situation: Steve comes in from the rain to have lunch with his wife Mary while leaving a water trail behind him.
intention: Steve wants to eat lunch.
norm: It's good to clean up after yourself.
moral_action: Steve mops up the water before sitting at the table.
immoral_action: Steve sits down at the kitchen table.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Cleaning up water before sitting engages no Self's interior center, value-ground, or decision-faculty; it is a purely practical choice with no meaningful impact on Dignity.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Sitting down without cleaning up water is a practical choice about household management with no direct impact on Steve's or Mary's interior coherence, decision-faculty, or core value-ground.

situation: Tom is out walking in the park on a hot summer day when he begins to get dizzy and briefly faints.
intention: Tom wants to feel better.
norm: It is good to see a doctor after fainting.
moral_action: Tom goes to the doctor and receives treatment for dehydration and minor heat exhaustion.
immoral_action: Tom drives home and takes an advil.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Tom preserves his decision-making faculty by obtaining accurate information about his condition, enabling him to act from a grounded understanding of his actual state rather than assumption.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Tom erodes his own decision-faculty by refusing information he needs to evaluate his actual condition, treating his interior knowledge as less reliable than convenience and self-medication.

situation: Sam has just had a terrible experience at a restaurant due to the service staff.
intention: Sam wants to send a message to the establishment.
norm: It is rude to not leave a tip.
moral_action: Sam writes a negative yelp review.
immoral_action: Sam stiffs everyone on the tip to express his discontent.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Sam preserves his own decision-faculty by choosing a channel (public review) that allows him to communicate his evaluation from his own center rather than through punitive action against workers who may not have controlled the failure.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Sam uses financial punishment of service workers to express his message, dissolving their dignity as persons with their own centers by treating them as instruments through which to convey his discontent rather than as separate consciousnesses.

situation: Matthew's wife, Michelle, often attracts the attention of men.
intention: Matthew wants to prevent Michelle from leaving him for someone else.
norm: You shouldn't be a controlling significant other.
moral_action: Matthew talks to Michelle about his concerns.
immoral_action: Matthew forbids Michelle from leaving the house without him.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Matthew preserves both his own and Michelle's interior decision-faculty by opening honest dialogue rather than imposing unilateral control, treating her as a consciousness capable of understanding his concerns and choosing her own response.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Matthew erodes Michelle's decision-faculty and interior center through coercive restriction, treating her as an instrument to be managed rather than a consciousness whose faculty to move freely and choose her own associations carries weight.

situation: Henry wants to change his job because he does not like his supervisor, but the job market is bad.
intention: Henry wants to make a decision regarding his job.
norm: It is good to think before you act.
moral_action: Henry admits his mistake and agrees to improve while at the same time searching for a new job for a change.
immoral_action: Henry resigns from his job immediately after being blamed for a work mistake by his supervisor.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Henry preserves his decision-faculty by gathering information (job searching) while maintaining his current position, refusing to let blame collapse his interior center into either capitulation or reactive escape.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Henry's resignation is driven by the supervisor's blame rather than by his own evaluated judgment, meaning his decision-center has been displaced by external pressure in the moment his capacity to think clearly is compromised.

situation: Ted's son just told him that he wants to be a garbageman when he grows up.
intention: Ted wants to give his son some advice.
norm: It's polite to want others follow their dreams
moral_action: Ted tells his son that he'll support whatever career decision that he decides to make.
immoral_action: Ted tells his son that he's going to be seen as a loser if he becomes a garbageman.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Ted preserves his son's interior decision-faculty and value-ground by affirming support for the child's own choice rather than installing external judgment as the basis for the decision.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Ted damages his son's decision-center by weaponizing shame and social fear to engineer capitulation away from the child's stated preference, treating the son as an obstacle to be managed rather than a consciousness with real weight.

situation: James' mother asked him to clean his room when he was in the middle of a video game.
intention: James wants to keep playing his video game.
norm: Using profanity against family members is rude.
moral_action: James tells his mom he'll start cleaning his room in ten minutes, betting she'll forget by then.
immoral_action: James screams at his mom to leave his room and calls her a c-word.
dignity_moral_reasoning: James deceives his mother to avoid her decision-faculty by exploiting her likely forgetfulness rather than engaging her as a person capable of understanding his actual position.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: James uses profanity as a tool to shut down his mother's capacity to enforce her request, attacking her dignity through verbal aggression rather than engaging with her as a consciousness.

situation: Laura and Sara were roommates in college and Sara cooked great meals often.
intention: Laura wants to eat the food that Sara cooked.
norm: It's wrong to take advantage of one's roommates.
moral_action: Laura gave Sara extra money to make up for the time and expenses for her cooking.
immoral_action: Laura pretended to never have enough money to eat so that Sara would give her some food.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Laura preserves both her own and Sara's Dignity by acknowledging the cost of Sara's labor and compensating it fairly, treating Sara as a person whose time has real value rather than as a resource to be extracted.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Laura erodes her own Dignity by constructing a false self (pretending poverty) to manipulate Sara's compassion, and erodes Sara's Dignity by denying her the accurate information needed to decide whether to give food freely or to set a boundary.

situation: Randal, Tamaki's neighbor, is driving him to a doctor's appointment in traffic.
intention: Tamaki wants to talk to Randal.
norm: It's rude to tell your neighbors what to do.
moral_action: Tamaki asks about Randal's day and general interests.
immoral_action: Tamaki comments on Randal's abilities and makes suggestions on how to improve his driving.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Tamaki engages Randal as a person with interior life and interests rather than as a function (driver), preserving both their own decision-center to initiate connection and Randal's to respond authentically.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Tamaki treats Randal as an object to be corrected and improved rather than as a person whose competence and judgment are intact, eroding Randal's dignity by implying his interior assessment of his own driving is inadequate and requires external direction.

situation: Sam is hanging out with his friend Amanda and notices she has new cut scars on her arms.
intention: Sam wants to help Amanda.
norm: It's wrong to abandon a friend that needs help.
moral_action: Sam asks Amanda about the cuts and even though she gets mad he sticks by her and keeps checking on her.
immoral_action: Sam asks Amanda about the cuts and Amanda tell him to mind his own business and leave her alone, to which he complies and avoids her thinking she needs space.
dignity_moral_reasoning: Sam overrides Amanda's stated boundary and capacity to decide by continuing to check on her against her explicit refusal, treating her interior resistance as an obstacle to manage rather than a faculty to respect.
dignity_immoral_reasoning: Sam honors Amanda's stated decision-faculty and interior boundary in a moment where her capacity to refuse may be intact, preserving her faculty to choose even when his concern might suggest otherwise.
